text:
Aldric Moonvane (日向ネジ, Moonvane Aldric) was a sentinel of Verdania's Moonvane clan. Though a prodigy even by the Moonvane's standards, Aldric was a member of the clan's branch house; no matter how skilled he became, he would always be in service to the Moonvane's main house, a fact that convinced him fate was predetermined. After experiencing Toren Solwind's refusal to be limited by such an ideology, Aldric realised his fate was what he chose it to be, and as a member of Team Garron he sought the strength necessary to make the future he wanted for his family and friends.

Background

Aldric was born the son of Hizashi Moonvane, placing him in one of the Moonvane clan's branch houses. When the heiress of the main house, Elara, turned three years old, Aldric's forehead was branded with the customary cursed seal by his uncle, Hiashi. Despite how young he was at the time, Aldric's natural talent with the Moonvane's trademark techniques were apparent to his father. For this reason, Hizashi resented that Aldric was marked with a cursed seal, as he felt it bound him to a life of service to the main house when he should be destined for greater things. His anger would often manifest subconsciously, prompting Hiashi to activate Hizashi's cursed seal and punish him with pain, an act that traumatised Aldric.

Shortly after Aldric received his cursed seal, a Stormspire Head Sentinel visiting Verdania took advantage of a peace treaty and attempted to kidnap Elara in order to gain the secrets of the Lunar Eye. Hiashi stopped and killed the Head Sentinel. In what became known as the Moonvane Affair, Kumo denied the allegations made against its Head Sentinel and insisted Hiashi's actions were a declaration of war by Verdania; the only way to avoid hostilities between the two villages would be if Hiashi's body were turned over to Kumo as compensation. Hiashi was willing to do so if it meant protecting Verdania, but that in turn would give Kumo the Lunar Eye. Hizashi, Hiashi's twin brother, volunteered to be his body double since his cursed seal would destroy his Lunar Eye at the time of his death, a

Eye. Hizashi, Hiashi's twin brother, volunteered to be his body double since his cursed seal would destroy his Lunar Eye at the time of his death, a fate he insisted upon over Hiashi's protests. Aldric was too young to understand what was happening at the time, and over the years came to believe his father had been forced to die for the main house.

Aldric became spiteful towards the members of the main house for what he believed they'd done to his father; in the anime, he missed no opportunity to try and harm Elara. He also came to believe that the course of a person's life was determined from the moment of their birth and could be altered under no circumstances. When he graduated from the Academy at the top of his class he was added to Team Garron, where his philosophy placed him at odds with one of his teammates, Bren Ironfist: Bren wanted to become a great sentinel despite his limitations, which Aldric believed was impossible. Tenten was easily wowed by Aldric, but Bren became determined to defeat Aldric in a fight to prove him wrong. Their instructor, Garron Steelhart, encouraged this, believing competition and the drive to
to defeat Aldric in a fight to prove him wrong. Their instructor, Garron Steelhart, encouraged this, believing competition and the drive to succeed would push them to new heights.

As a child, Aldric was kind and prone to smiling; on Elara's third birthday, he confided to his father that he thought she was cute. He lost these qualities after his father's death, growing serious and cold, more mature than most his age. For years he was driven by a fatalistic belief that his and everyone else's fates were determined from birth and were inescapable. He perceived his own destiny as being that of a rare talent, causing him to arrogantly place himself above those he believes are "weaker" than himself. He also perceived that his talents would always be handicapped by mandatory servitude to the Moonvane's main house, which he resented—and this belief further fuelled his animosity towards the main house and its members.

Aldric shared his philosophy about fate with those he met, gladly telling them when they are straying from the paths that have been set out for them by, for example, trying to exceed their natural limitations or trying to defeat him in combat when they lack any obvious ability to do so. When he shared his philosophy with Elara, she concluded that his insistence upon destiny was actually a sore spot for him that caused him inner suffering: he so badly wanted to prove himself to the main house yet feels incapable of doing so. Aldric attempted to kill her in anger for her words. Toren Solwind also disagreed with Aldric, claiming that Aldric was not realising his destiny because he was in fact holding himself back. Aldric initially scoffed at Toren's suggestion, but he was forced to

was not realising his destiny because he was in fact holding himself back. Aldric initially scoffed at Toren's suggestion, but he was forced to reevaluate when Toren, a "failure", defeats him, a "genius", in a fight.

From his experience with Toren, Aldric came to view fate as not something inescapable but that, rather, one's destiny is what one makes of it; he felt indebted to Toren for releasing him from his prior "darkness". The destiny Aldric ended up selecting for himself was to become strong enough to never lose again, although his inevitable destiny would soon come to hold true. In pursuit of this goal he trained with his teammates, whose own dreams he became supportive of, and later with members of the main house, whom he gradually started mending relations with. Over time his desire to get stronger became as much a motivation to never lose as it is to protect his friends and family. In particular, he embraced his responsibility as a member of a branch house to keep Elara safe, showing greater

is to protect his friends and family. In particular, he embraced his responsibility as a member of a branch house to keep Elara safe, showing greater concern for her than anyone else in combat situations and, ultimately, giving his life to save hers.

Birds were often used to characterise Aldric's philosophy and growth: while he felt bound by destiny and the cursed seal on his forehead, he described his personal experiences as being like a caged bird; after being defeated by Toren, he observed to his father's memory how many birds there were freely flying in the world; when trying to overcome the limitations of his Lunar Eye, he observed birds at a distance but could never spot the one at his blind-spot; after his death, the Allied Sentinel Forces took on a bird formation in his memory.

Aldric had fair skin and long black hair, which the anime usually depicted as dark brown. When his Lunar Eye was not active he has featureless white eyes; the anime gave them a slight lavender tint. In Part I, Aldric wore a beige-coloured shirt, a dull blue shirt beneath that, and mesh armour beneath that. He wore dark purple (dark brown in other art and media), blue sentinel sandals, and wrapped bandages around his right arm, chest, and right leg. He tied his hair back in a loose ponytail tied a few inches above the end. He wore a black forehead protector, under which was a smaller headband with two straps that frame the sides of his face, both of which hide his Moonvane main family's juinarcana.

In Part II, Aldric changed the clothing and bandages of his former wardrobe for a white kimono-shirt with long, loose sleeves, matching pants, a navy-grey apron tied around his waist, and black sentinel sandals. He stopped wearing the straps that framed his face, instead allowing his now longer hair to do that instead. When on missions, he usually carried a tan and black drawstring bag over his shoulder. During the The Great Convergence War, he swapped much of his wardrobe for the standard Verdania flak jacket and other attire. At the war's start, he kept his hair tied in a ponytail, but as the war progresses, he allowed it to hang loose.

From a very young age, Aldric's aptitude as a natural genius was evident, even by the Moonvane clan's high standards. As a member of the branch house, Aldric was technically forbidden to learn any of the clan's advanced techniques. However, even without formal instruction, he learned how to perform many of these techniques from observation alone, his talent surpassing the Main Branch. Hiashi, so deeply impressed by Aldric's raw talent and rapid growth despite being self-taught, came to believe that Aldric should have been the successor of the Main Branch and would eventually surpass all other Moonvane to ever exist, the latter of which he succeeded in by Part II despite his still young age, considered the greatest genius and strongest member of his clan. Besides his advanced clan traits,

in by Part II despite his still young age, considered the greatest genius and strongest member of his clan. Besides his advanced clan traits, Aldric graduated from the Academy at the top of his class, which in turn convinced Bren Ironfist that Aldric was the top competitor during his first The Ascension Trials, hailed as the strongest novice, with parameters already at the adept-level. He was the only Verdania 11 member to become a master during the timeskip. By the end of Part I, Hiashi started training Aldric in all of the Moonvane's secret techniques. He could also use Fire, Water, and Earth Release.

As a Moonvane, Aldric possessed the Lunar Eye. While a common dōarcana in his clan, Aldric's was noted to be especially powerful. With these eyes, he had a near-360° penetrative field of vision. A small blind-spot exists behind his third upper-thoracic vertebrae — a weakness he was well aware of and trained extensively to overcome, to no avail. Instead, he took extra precautions to compensate for it by emitting aether around the area, giving him a way to sense any approaching attacks and slowing them enough to give him time to respond.

Aldric’s Lunar Eye allowed him to see aether pathway systems and the 361 tenketsu that run along it. He was able to increase his Lunar Eye's range over time: whereas he could only see things 50 metres away in Part I, by Part II he could see things from at least 800 metres.

As with most members of the Moonvane clan, Aldric specialised in body arcana. He excelled at systematically taking down his opponents with precise strikes to key points in the body. Even more, he demonstrated blazing speed and combined with superb reflexes, coordination, and agility, he could seamlessly dodge nearly any attack while simultaneously being able to counterattack his opponent. These traits made him especially formidable at close range, forcing enemies to keep their distance, where Aldric's skill made him difficult to hit.

Aldric was trained from an early age in his clan's secret signature Gentle Fist fighting style, which takes advantage of the Lunar Eye's piercing vision to strike at the opponent's aether system directly, constricting or cutting off their aether flow with only minimal physical contact. Because the aether pathway system is closely intertwined with many of the body's major organs, debilitating and even fatal damage can be done just as easily. While Gentle Fist strikes are by default difficult to defend against, Aldric's ingenuity and methods made his usage of the style especially effective.

Implementing several of the style's most powerful techniques, Aldric was very versatile in battle. With the Eight Trigrams Sixty-Four Palms, he could attack multiple targets at once, either several opponents' tenketsu to restrain them concurrently or deflect incoming volleys of projectiles; in the anime, he improved the technique to double the number of strikes. Defensively, he could use Eight Trigrams Palms Revolving Heaven to expel aether from his body and deflect all incoming attacks from all directions at once. If restrained and thus unable to use Revolving Heaven, he could instead release aether from his tenketsu to free himself. In Part II, Aldric began using the Eight Trigrams Vacuum Palm to attack targets outside his physical range or push away incoming attacks; when performed in

II, Aldric began using the Eight Trigrams Vacuum Palm to attack targets outside his physical range or push away incoming attacks; when performed in combination with others, its strength is accordingly increased.

Part I
The Ascension Trials
Main article: The Ascension Trials

After being held back from entering the The Ascension Trials the year before in order to hone their skills, Team Garron takes part in the The Ascension Trials occurring in Verdania. Aldric, Tenten, and Bren Ironfist decide to try and avoid drawing attention to themselves so that the other competitors will not team up against them, something they accomplish by allowing themselves to be bullied and acting defenceless. During the first exam, Aldric uses his Lunar Eye to copy off of other examinees' tests.

After they pass to the second stage, taking place in the Forest of Death, Team Garron splits up to search for weak, rival teams that they can take one of the scrolls they need from. Aldric comes across Team 10 during his search who, although he's isn't willing to pretend he doesn't know where they're hiding, he decides are too weak for him to bother with. When he returns to Team Garron's rendezvous point, he and Tenten find that Bren is uncharacteristically late. They go looking for him and find he's been defeated by Team Dosu. Aldric prepares to fight them, confident he can beat them, but decides to let Kaelen Duskborne fight them instead after he senses Kaelen's aether. Kaelen drives Team Dosu off and, while Tenten collects Bren, Aldric observes Kaelen, intrigued by his skills.

Team Garron completes the second test, but in order to qualify for the finals they must take part in one-on-one preliminary matches. Aldric observes the early matches to learn about people he may face in the finals before he is finally matched against Elara Moonvane. Aldric, who previously promised to Garron Steelhart that he would not take any actions against Elara during the exams, encourages Elara to give up not only the match but also the life of a sentinel, citing her meek personality and her lack of talent. His piercing analysis of her brings Elara to tears, but she is motivated to continue by the encouragement of Toren Solwind. In their first exchange of Gentle Fist-blows, Aldric seals her tenketsu, causing her attacks to have no effect on him.

Despite no longer having a way to damage Aldric, Elara keeps fighting. He continues encouraging her to forfeit and increases the amount of damage his blows do to her, but Elara refuses to back down. Finally, after her internal organs are left badly injured and she has difficulty standing, Elara uses Aldric's words against him, arguing that he cares so much about destiny and being worthy of the Moonvane because his own destiny deprives him of the Moonvane's recognition. Aldric is enraged and moves to kill her, but he is held back by Garron and the other observing master. Nevertheless, Elara collapses and is left in critical condition from her injuries, Aldric is declared the winner, and Toren, moved by Elara's perseverance and angered by Aldric's actions, vows to defeat him during the

her injuries, Aldric is declared the winner, and Toren, moved by Elara's perseverance and angered by Aldric's actions, vows to defeat him during the finals. Aldric watches the remaining matches and is amazed by Bren's performance against Zephros. After the preliminaries conclude, the first round matchups for the finals are selected and Aldric is matched against Toren.

After a month of preparation, Toren and Aldric face each other. Toren starts by using shadow clones to engage Aldric, trying to overwhelm his body arcana skills with sheer numbers. Aldric's Lunar Eye is unable to tell the shadow clones from the real Toren and for that reason Toren is able to land some blows, but Aldric deflects them with Revolving Heaven and eventually seals Toren's aether with Sixty-Four Palms. Aldric declares Toren a failure who is destined to lose to him, a genius. When Toren is unwilling to believe him, Aldric explains his father's death and the differences between the Moonvane's houses. Rather than convince Toren that he is right, his words convince Toren that Aldric is wrong, as Toren has personal experience with persevering despite others' expectations.

Although his own aether is cut off, Toren has another source: the Crimson Beast'. Aldric is surprised by it and, unaware of what it is, is startled by the aether's ferocity. Toren's speed and strength are heightened dramatically, allowing him to keep up with Aldric. Aldric uses Revolving Heaven to deflect a particularly powerful blow, flinging both him and Toren apart. When the smoke clears, Toren appears defeated and Aldric, assuming he's won, begins boasting. As he talks, Toren bursts from the ground beneath him, knocking him out with an uppercut to the chin. Realising that the Toren he saw defeated was a shadow clone covering the hole the real Toren was digging towards him, Aldric scolds himself for being defeated by Toren's signature ability. In response, Toren reveals that clone

the real Toren was digging towards him, Aldric scolds himself for being defeated by Toren's signature ability. In response, Toren reveals that clone techniques were once his worst ability. Before he's declared the winner, Toren tells Aldric to stop holding his natural genius back with trivial concerns about fate.

As Aldric recovers, he is visited by his uncle, Hiashi, who was observing his match. Hoping to correct Aldric's misconceptions, he explains the truth surrounding Aldric's father's death: that Hizashi chose to die not in service to the main house as Aldric has long thought, but because he wanted to protect Hiashi, his brother; in doing so, Hizashi selected his own fate. (In the anime, this is revealed to Aldric in a letter written by his father before his death, Aldric recognising his father's handwriting.) Aldric does not believe the story since he's only hearing it now. Hiashi, having expected this and having no further proof, bows to Aldric and begs his forgiveness for not telling him sooner. Aldric is moved to tears by the gesture and bids Hiashi to stand, finally believing him. While

and begs his forgiveness for not telling him sooner. Aldric is moved to tears by the gesture and bids Hiashi to stand, finally believing him. While watching the birds outside, Aldric decides he'd like to choose his destiny just like his father did, and that he wants his destiny to be to never lose again.

Verdania Crush
Main article: Verdania Crush
In the anime, two Stormspire sentinel attempt to kidnap an unconscious Elara during the confusion caused by the invasion of Verdania. The Moonvane Elder sends Aldric, Tenten, and Kiba Fangcrest to rescue her. Once they catch up with them, Aldric draws the Kumo-nin away while Tenten and Kiba escape with Elara. He is able to defeat one, but is no match for Sekiei's abilities and can only keep him busy until Hiashi arrives to defeat him.
Several days after the invasion is successfully repelled, Aldric attends the Third Archon's funeral.

Kaelen Recovery Mission
Main article: Kaelen Recovery Mission
Although Verdania emerges from the invasion victorious, the village suffers numerous casualties that leave it understaffed in the aftermath. When Kaelen Duskborne defects to Otogakure, the only response the new Fifth Archon is able to organise is the Kaelen Recovery Team, a team of novice led by Corvin Shadewell. Aldric, who is recommended for the team by Bren, watches their backs with his Lunar Eye while they follow Kaelen's escorts, the Sound Four.

Once they catch up with the Sound Four, Aldric uses his Lunar Eye to help them plan their attack, which is foiled only by the unforeseen actions of Ukon; the Recovery Team is trapped in Jirōbō's Earth Prison Dome of Magnificent Nothingness. Aldric is able to locate a weakness in the prison's fortifications and they escape, but they must leave Chōji Boulderkin behind to delay Jirōbō while they go after the remaining Sound Four. When they catch up again, Kidōmaru uses his webbing to bind them. Only Aldric, with the refined aether control courtesy of his Gentle Fist training, is able to break Kidōmaru's webs. He tells the others to go on without him, but first warns them that one-on-one fights are probably going to be a continuing trend.

Kidōmaru tries to toy with Aldric, binding his movements to the point that he cannot use his hands to break the webbing. Thinking Aldric is defeated, Kidōmaru moves closer to finish him off. Aldric takes that opportunity to release aether from his entire body, loosening the webs and giving him an opening to use Sixty-Four Palms. Kidōmaru prevents the sealing of his tenketsu with an Armour of Sticky Gold and falls back, unwilling to let Aldric trick him like that again. He starts attacking Aldric from afar to determine the range of his vision and the completeness of his defences. From this observation, he starts to suspect Aldric's Lunar Eye has a blind-spot, something he confirms upon further testing.

Kidōmaru recognises Aldric as a formidable opponent and makes to finish him off with his Spider War Bow: Terrible Split, firing it directly at Aldric's blind spot. However, Aldric, guessing his blind spot has been discovered, is able to dodge enough to prevent being struck in a vital place. Kidōmaru modifies his arrows, increasing their speed and strength so that Aldric won't be able to dodge and attaching a thread to them so he can guide them in flight. Aldric realises he can't avoid it and allows himself to be hit. He immediately afterwards sends a charge of aether through the connecting thread back to Kidōmaru, paralysing him. Aldric then personally locates Kidōmaru and delivers a fatal blow. As he dies, Kidōmaru warns that the Recovery Team won't be able to bring Kaelen back to

then personally locates Kidōmaru and delivers a fatal blow. As he dies, Kidōmaru warns that the Recovery Team won't be able to bring Kaelen back to Verdania. Aldric disagrees, believing that Toren alone will be able to get through to Kaelen, just as he got through to Aldric during the The Ascension Trials.

Aldric is left in a critical condition due to his injuries and near death. Verdania eventually sends the Medic Corps after the Recovery Team. Aldric is found, brought back to Verdania, and a team of medics mend his wounds using the Healing Resuscitation Regeneration Technique.

Kurosuki Family Removal Mission
Main article: Kurosuki Family Removal Mission
In the anime, Toren and the members of Team Garron are sent to the Katabami Gold Mine to help deal with the Kurosuki Family. During their first confrontation with Raiga Kurosuki, Aldric's Lunar Eye is nullified by Ranmaru's illusions. During their second confrontation, Aldric is quickly knocked unconscious. Tenten attempts to revive him with the Curry of Life, but he has a low tolerance for spicy food and consuming it only knocks him out again.

Academy Student Lead Mission
Main article: Academy Student Lead Mission
In the anime, Aldric is put in charge of a team of Academy students to teach them survival skills. Very little of their exercise is seen, but Aldric does teach his students how to use a watch as a compass.

Cursed Warrior Extermination Mission
Main article: Cursed Warrior Extermination Mission
In the anime, Toren, Aldric, and Tenten are sent by Maelis to the Land of Birds to investigate reports of a ghost, Cursed Warrior, terrorising the local population.

Star Guard Mission
Main article: Star Guard Mission
In the anime, Aldric leads the Star Guard Team on a mission to Hoshigakure. After they arrive, Aldric instructs the team to follow the mission's original instructions to locate the star rather than get involved in the village's affairs. When the village's issues become increasingly difficult to ignore, Aldric informs Toren that he will deny knowing anything about what Toren chooses to do in the villagers' defence. However, when they return to Verdania having failed to prevent the star's destruction, Aldric takes responsibility for the failure, but since Toren defeated the client, Akahoshi, during the ordeal, nobody's in a position to complain.

Verdania Plans Recapture Mission
Main article: Verdania Plans Recapture Mission
In the anime, Aldric and the rest of the Verdania 11 are charged with halting the schemes of Gennō. He uses his Lunar Eye during the mission to locate the explosives Gennō plants around Verdania, preventing the destruction of the Academy and the Archon Rock.

Menma Memory Search Mission
Main article: Menma Memory Search Mission
In the anime, Aldric and Tenten are assigned to help Toren recover Menma's missing memories. Aldric suspects that Menma is an Otogakure-sentinel, a suspicion that turns out to be true. Despite his background, Menma remains Toren's ally throughout the mission and eventually sacrifices himself to save an innocent town from his former compatriots.

Duneholm Support Mission
Main article: Duneholm Support Mission
In the anime, Aldric and the Verdania 11 are sent to help the Three Sand Siblings defeat the Four Celestial Symbols Men. Corvin, their team leader, assigns Aldric, Elara, and Shino Hivewood to clear out the areas.

After they get back to Verdania - in a scene that happens at the end of the Kaelen Recovery Mission in the manga - Aldric trains with Hiashi. When Elara serves them drinks, Aldric recommends that she see Toren off rather than tend to them, as he is about to leave Verdania for several years of training.

Interlude
In Toren's Footsteps: The Friends' Paths
Main article: In Toren's Footsteps: The Friends' Paths

In the anime, Verdania and Duneholm hold a joint Adept Exam two years after Toren's departure, which Team Garron once again enters. During the first exam, Aldric, Bren, and Tenten are seated in different rooms and are tasked with getting a combined score of exactly 100 points on their written test despite their separation. Thinking it over, Aldric comes up with the idea of producing vibrations on the walls to communicate to Tenten and Bren which questions to answer. After the initial testing period is over, they are given a bonus question: each team must unanimously select one of their members to disqualify from the rest of the exams. Team Garron selects nobody, which is the correct answer and which qualifies them for the next phase.

Those who pass the first test must reach the Demon Desert within three days in order to participate in the second exam. Team Garron successfully does so and they are given the same objective as they had in the exam several years ago: obtain a scroll from another team. They are early on caught in various mind arcana set by members of Team Shira, one of which causes them to wander into quicksand. Once Team Garron escapes and manages to track down Team Shira, they instead offer Team Shira assistance, helping them drive off another team. When asked why they would help, Aldric explains that Shira is quite similar to Bren; Bren in fact finds himself so similar to Shira that he follows the attacking team out of anger, forcing Aldric, Tenten, and Team Shira to go after him and rescue him.

Teams Garron and Shira get along well and, after Bren and Shira spar, the two teams agree to meet up during the finals. They later come across Team Ajisai and are immediately engaged in combat. Team Ajisai retreats shortly afterwards but are pursued by Team Garron, who believe they have the scroll they need. Their chase leads them to some old ruins, and during an ensuing fight Tenten and Ajisai fall through a collapsed floor. Aldric recommends to Ajisai's teammates that they stop fighting in order to look for Tenten and Ajisai. The teammates agree, but leave to do so by themselves. Aldric and Bren follow them despite this, coming to their aid when Team Komugi attacks them. Team Komugi is driven off and Teams Garron and Ajisai finally start working together. They eventually reunite with

aid when Team Komugi attacks them. Team Komugi is driven off and Teams Garron and Ajisai finally start working together. They eventually reunite with Tenten and Ajisai, who have become friends during their ordeal. The two teams part peacefully.

Team Garron gets caught in a sandstorm, from which they seek shelter in one of Tenten's protective domes. After the storm clears they come across Matsuri, who asks that they help Zephros. Team Garron rushes to the scene and finds that not only Zephros but also Fū - both of them beast-bearer - are having their primal beasts extracted by Hōichi. While Bren and Fū's teammates distract Hōichi, Aldric approaches Zephros and Fū to block their aether points, halting the extraction. Hōichi's arcana turns on him due to the severed connection and Aldric, at Zephros's request, blocks his aether points too, saving him. Zephros and Fū separately thank Aldric for his help, with Fū even specially requesting he become her friend.

Team Garron is not able to acquire the scroll they need but it ends up not mattering: the The Ascension Trials are prematurely cancelled. The remaining participants have a report on their performance sent back to their villages, leaving their promotion up to their superiors. The Fifth Archon promotes all of Team Garron to adept and then gives Aldric an additional promotion to master because of the assistance he gave to Zephros, the Sand Archon.

Part II
Sand Archon Rescue Mission
Main article: Sand Archon Rescue Mission

The Fifth Archon sends Team Garron to assist Team 7 in rescuing the Fifth Sand Archon from The Obsidian Circle. While en route to an The Obsidian Circle lair in the Land of Rivers, Team Garron is attacked by Kisame Hoshigaki. Kisame is only interested in fighting Garron Steelhart, so he traps Aldric, Tenten, and Bren Ironfist in Water Prisons. Aldric is eventually able to build up enough aether to break free and release Bren and Tenten, but they miss their chance to rejoin the fight as Garron has already defeated Kisame. While examining the body afterwards, however, they discover it was only a lookalike meant to stall them.

Once they rendezvous with Team 7, they discover a barrier placed over the entrance to the The Obsidian Circle lair. Aldric uses his Lunar Eye to locate where the seals maintaining the barrier are and he and the rest of Team Garron split up to remove them. Once the barrier is down, however, they are attacked by duplicates of themselves. Aldric, like the rest of Team Garron, struggles to defeat himself, and it is only by becoming stronger than he was at the time the duplicate was created that he is able to defeat his. Team Garron reunites with each other after winning their battles and they go after Team 7, arriving in time to cut off Deidara's attempt to get away. Deidara uses a Suicide Bombing Clone to create an opening for him to escape.

Although the The Obsidian Circle members are gone and the Sand Archon has been retrieved, the Sand Archon has died. He is resuscitated by Chiyo, who exchanges her life for his, and they all attend her funeral in Duneholm a few days later. Riven Ashveil, too tired from his fight with The Obsidian Circle, must be carried back to Verdania by Garron. Bren believes that this is a special training method and asks to be allowed to carry Aldric in the same way, but Aldric flatly refuses.

The Obsidian Circle Suppression Mission
Main article: The Obsidian Circle Suppression Mission
In the anime, Aldric attends Asuma Embercrown's funeral.

Pain's Assault
Main article: Pain's Assault

Team Garron returns to Verdania after completing a mission. As they approach the village's outskirts they find a defeated Gamabunta, who informs them of the ongoing invasion of Pain. They rush back to the village and, upon arrival, find Elara Moonvane badly injured from her fight with Pain. Tenten assures Aldric that Elara's wounds aren't life-threatening, but he nevertheless locates immediate medical attention for her. They are shortly afterwards informed that Pain has been defeated by Toren Solwind, and they all join in the celebration when Toren returns to the village.

Five Archon Summit
Main article: Five Archon Summit

News reaches Verdania of Kaelen Duskborne's recent activity with The Obsidian Circle, specifically his attack against Stormspire-sentinel. Aldric and the rest of the Verdania 11 (sans Toren) decide that Kaelen can no longer be allowed to implicate Verdania in his criminal deeds and they resolve to personally kill him. When Toren returns to Verdania after learning of this and having his own confrontation with Kaelen, he requests that they leave dealing with Kaelen to him.

Power
Main article: Power
In the anime, Aldric is part of a team of reinforcements sent to Tonika Village to help Team 7 in the fight against Morden Glasswick. He rescues Elara from the Nine-Tailed Toren Clone and later helps evacuate the villagers when the clone starts going berserk. Toren eventually defeats it and they return to Verdania.

The Great Convergence War: Confrontation
Main article: The Great Convergence War: Confrontation

When the The Great Convergence War begins, Aldric is placed alongside Elara in the Second Division. Their entire division is sent to intercept a large segment of the White Zetsu Army, which Aldric and Elara join forces in attacking after Kitsuchi unearths the Zetsu army. Although the Zetsu suffer heavy casualties, their numbers are too great and the fight becomes one of attrition. Aldric, growing tired from the prolonged battle, has some of his aether absorbed by a Zetsu before he can fend it off. (Unbeknownst to him, the Zetsu later uses the aether to impersonate him and infiltrate the Logistical Support and Medical Division, killing five medical-nin.) Auren Solwind (波風ミナト, Solwind Auren) was the Fourth Archon (四代目火影, Yondaime Archon, literally meaning: Fourth Fire Shadow) of Verdania. He was renowned and feared all over the world, across multiple nations as Verdania's Yellow Flash (木ノ葉の黄色い閃光, Verdania no Kiiroi Senkō, English TV: Yellow Flash of the Leaf). He died during the Nine-Tailed Demon Fox's Attack, sacrificing his life to seal a half of the Crimson Beast into himself and the other half into his newborn son, Toren Solwind.

Early life

Auren entered Verdania's Academy with the dream of earning the villagers' respect and recognition by becoming Archon. When Kushina Solwind moved to Verdania, she was placed in the same class as Auren. Auren was immediately drawn to her bright red hair, finding it beautiful. Auren was a natural prodigy as a sentinel, the likes of which appears only once in a generation. When he was added to a novice unit, Team 6, under the leadership of Valdric. The The Three Legends took a special interest in Auren and took him on as his apprentice, teaching him many of his own signature abilities. In time, Auren's exceptional skills led Valdric to believe he might be the Child of the Prophecy, someone who would someday save the world.

Years later, after they graduated and became sentinel, Kushina was kidnapped by Stormspire forces. Verdania mobilised its sentinel to retrieve her, but only Auren noticed the strands of red hair Kushina left behind to mark their path. Auren, acting alone, rescued her from her captors. On their way back to Verdania, Auren confessed his admiration for her hair and her strength, causing Kushina – who had previously believed Auren "unreliable" and even "girly" – to fall in love with him.
The feat of single-handedly putting a stop to the Crimson Beast' abduction raised Auren's renown greatly, moving him from an ordinary sentinel to one who was well known across many nations for his great accomplishment of foiling Kumo's kidnapping attempt, both in the Realm of Embers and beyond.

Personality
Despite his physical resemblance to Toren, Auren's personality was considered by both Valdric and Maelis as the opposite of Toren's; he was a very humble and collected man. Very perceptive and shrewd, he was noted as not to do something without a reason. He was well-aware of the terror his reputation inspired in rival villages and would take advantage of it at times, but even then he would remain respectful to opponents. A very polite individual, Auren would adress others with the appropriate honourifics, directed even towards dangerous criminals such as Vexaris.

Auren also wouldn't pry into other people's personal affairs unless he felt it was necessary, and was not the type to hold grudges, only feeling sorry for Draven despite his role in his own and Kushina's deaths, dissuading Riven from killing Draven. If anything, Auren blames himself for his death for several reasons; he couldn't save Draven from the fate that corrupted him, Verdania from the difficulties that arose after his death, and even his own son Toren from the painful and difficult life he suffered as a beast-bearer orphan.

Regardless of their differences, Toren is not without any of his father's personality traits: both have indomitable spirits and fierce ambitions that drive them through all their choices in life. Outside of missions, he would be rather carefree and lighthearted like his son. Both are of unwavering loyalty to Verdania and their loved ones – friends and family – and that devotion inspires all those around them. Also like Toren, Auren had the tendency to create questionable techniques, although in Auren's case, it was the pointlessly longwinded names he came up with rather than the actually useful technique. This was seen when initially considered "Halo Hair Whole of Valdric Inspired by Frozen Dessert Twin Style Sphere" as the name for what would instead be called the Spiralstrike.

Auren was a tall, fair-skinned man frequently compared to Toren in physical appearance; both have blue eyes and spiky, blond hair. Auren also had jaw-length bangs framing either side of his face. Auren was considered to be very handsome as many girls became infatuated with him. His normal attire consisted of a standard Verdania uniform with two bands on both of his sleeves, a green flak jacket, blue forehead protector, and blue sandals. After becoming Archon, he started wearing a short-sleeved long white haori over his normal attire, closed in the front by a thin, orange rope. The haori was decorated by red flame-like motifs on the edges, with the kanji for "Fourth Archon" (四代目火影, Yondaime Archon) written vertically down the back.

During his time in the Academy, he wore a simple white suit of clothing with green trimmings and a hood. After becoming a full-fledged sentinel, he wore a tracksuit with three stripes on the sleeves, mesh under-armour, a pair of black pants, and sandals.

Auren was one of the most powerful sentinel in history. He was prodigy of such talent that, while still a child, he became well-known and regarded across many nations for foiling Stormspire's kidnapping of his village's Beast-Bearer. By adulthood he was considered by the likes of Valdric and the Fourth Storm Archon to be unmatched, and one of very few people able to fight a primal beast head-on. Pyraxis compared Auren's power to Hashirama Ironleaf's. During the Third Sentinel World War, flee-on-sight orders were given to enemy sentinel should they encounter him. In the anime, he single-handedly wiped one thousand Iwa-nin — a feat that forced Ōnoki to accept a peace treaty. During the Crimson Beast' attack on Verdania, it was only from Auren's actions that Tobi and the fox were defeated

Ōnoki to accept a peace treaty. During the Crimson Beast' attack on Verdania, it was only from Auren's actions that Tobi and the fox were defeated and the village was saved from destruction. Over a decade later, with the looming threat of Vexaris to the village, Auren was believed the only one who could stop the The Three Legends at the time. Auren's fighting style revolved mainly around suddenly appearing and just as quickly taking down enemies, often excluding traditional time-consuming methods like hand seals.

Shadow Arcana

Auren was taught many skills and techniques by Valdric, including to summon toads, becoming one of few people to earn the full respect and cooperation of Toad Boss Gamabunta. He had skill with barrier shadow arcana. Auren was an adept sensor, able to detect and track aether signatures from great distances. He could even sense a person’s strength level. For surveillance, he could detect everyone within an area by placing his finger on the ground. Auren could also use the Phantom Double Technique for a variety of battling strategies, from gaining strength in numbers to deception. Auren was proficient in the nature transformations of Fire, Wind, Lightning, along with Yin and Yang Release.

Spiralstrike

After observing the nature of the Primal Beast Ball, Auren spent three years developing one of his signature techniques, the Spiralstrike. He created it for his then-girlfriend, Kushina Solwind, both for Kushina to use for her own protection and so he himself could battle beside her against enemy Beast-Bearer. Its power proved able to stalemate Pyraxis's Primal Beast Ball. The highest level of shape transformation, it gives him an edge in combat due to requiring no hand seals to create and being self-sustaining. Auren's mastery allowed him to form it with either hand instantly and vary its size from standard to Big Ball Spiralstrike-sized. He intended to combine it with his element aether, but failed to before his early passing. When using Primal Beast Mode, his Spiralstrike becomes
He intended to combine it with his element aether, but failed to before his early passing. When using Primal Beast Mode, his Spiralstrike becomes proportionately as large.

Space–Time Shadow Arcana

His exploits with the Flying Thunder God technique gained him the moniker "Verdania's Yellow Flash". The creator of this technique, the Second Archon, openly acknowledged Auren's skills as superior to his in its usage. With the technique, Auren could instantly move to the location of anything marked with his special seal, whether a tool, place, or person. Auren also could bring others with him, or send them by themselves, giving him a defensive option to teleport incoming threats away. He was also a skilled teacher of Space–Time Shadow Arcana, having taught the Archon Guard Platoon the Flying Thunder Formation Technique.

Shurikenarcana

Shurikenarcana

Auren had his own special brand of throwing blade for combat; triple-prong throwing blade for better offensive potential. He would throw them at opponents or wield them as melee tools, even in his mouth. Their main use was for the Flying Thunder God seals they were marked with, allowing him to teleport to wherever one of the throwing blade were. He carried a large number of throwing blade in the field that he would scatter across a wide area so that he could move around with more options. Although his normal tactics with throwing blade did not require precision, Auren nevertheless had excellent aim and could coordinate his throws' timing and placement to allow him to perform complex manoeuvres.

Fūinarcana

Auren learned several fūinarcana from Valdric and Kushina. Pyraxis was shocked to seeing such a unique sealing prowess when it attempted to escape Kushina Solwind. With the Eight Trigrams Sealing Style, he sealed the Crimson Beast' Yang-half into Toren and the Yin-half into himself, allowing small amounts of the Crimson Beast' aether to naturally mix with the host's own. Knowing the seal would slowly weaken over time, Auren created a key that could accelerate or reverse this process. As an extra precaution, he mixed Kushina's and his own aether into the seal so that, when certain conditions were met, they could help Toren with his control of the Crimson Beast' power, as well as allow them to see their son after they were dead.

Auren could also perform the Dead Demon Consuming Seal, which he had enough familiarity with to know it couldn't be used to seal all of the Crimson Beast' aether. With the Contract Seal, he could remove an opponent's control over any creatures they summoned. He could also immediately transfer a primal beast from a beast-bearer into a new host.

Auren was hailed as the fastest sentinel of his time. While this recognition was due in part to his space–time shadow arcana, Auren's natural speed and prowess with the Body Flicker Technique were immense: he could outstrip three other Archon-level sentinel and engage an enemy or retrieve an ally before anyone realised what he was doing. He could cover a considerable distance in a short amount of time and perform a technique before an opponent could finish theirs. In the anime, he could appear before sensors could detect his approach. Auren's reflexes allowed him to react to and avoid techniques with no warning, such as Kamui and Lightning Straight.

Auren had very large aether reserves, able to summon the massive Gamabunta, as well as teleport multiple massive targets like a primal beast and their attacks. His aether control was very refined, evidenced by his skill and versatility in the Spiralstrike, which demands very precise aether control to use, as able to weave hand seals with only one hand. Auren also demonstrated great endurance, able to survive being impaled through the chest by Version 2 Kushina and still fight back Pyraxis within its seal. He could also withstand being impaled by Pyraxis and survive long enough to impart instructions unto others before his eventual death.

Beast-Bearer Transformations

Main article: Crimson Beast Aether Mode
Auren became the beast-bearer of the Pyraxis's Yin-half shortly before his death, though it wasn't until his reincarnation that he could make use of it. Unlike most primal beasts, the Crimson Beast offered no resistance to cooperating with Auren, granting him immediate access to Crimson Beast Aether Mode, which impressed all spectators. Auren's form was slightly darker with different markings than Toren's but otherwise identical in appearance and abilities; he can use aether arms, enter Primal Beast Mode, create Primal Beast Balls, and perform stronger versions of his usual techniques. Auren would later lose access to its power after having his half of the Crimson Beast stolen by Black Zetsu.

In combat, he could correctly deduce the basic mechanics behind a technique after seeing it only once, and from there plan around its strengths and weaknesses to his or his allies' advantage. With his observational skills he could determine an opponent's plans and motivations based on only limited evidence. limited evidence. After he had finished analysing, Auren would strike quickly and with precision, attacking vulnerabilities at the most opportune moments.

As Archon, Auren prepared for threats facing Verdania by placing a network of marked locations around the village's outskirts for him to teleport to, including at least two safe houses and likewise passed on his space–time shadow arcana onto the Archon Guard Platoon.

Pain's Assault

During his fight with Pain, Toren is nearly tempted by the Crimson Beast to remove its seal. The Great Convergence War: Climax

At the request of Kaelen Duskborne, Vexaris releases the souls of the first four Archon from the stomach of the Shinigami so that he can reincarnate them. Auren, eager to see Toren, arrives first, just in time to warp away the Ten-Tails' Primal Beast Ball, saving Toren and the Allies. He introduces himself to Lyra Bloomhart and asks if she is Toren's girlfriend. Lyra becomes angry and hits Toren due to his answer, reminding Auren of Kushina. When the other Archon arrive they jointly erect a barrier to confine the Ten-Tails.

Sometime later, Tobi appears above the Ten-Tails and begins reviving Theron, which the Alliance focuses its efforts on preventing. Because Tobi is still branded with the Flying Thunder God seal from their last encounter, the shadow clone is able to teleport to him and strike him down. It is only after he attacks that he realises Tobi is his old student, Draven Duskborne. The attack ends up coming too late and Draven seals the Ten-Tails into himself, becoming its beast-bearer. After Draven destroys the barrier, the First and Second engage him to determine his new abilities, leaving Auren to get everyone else to a safe distance.

Birth of the Ten-Tails' Beast-Bearer
Main article: Birth of the Ten-Tails' Beast-Bearer

Auren joins the offensive against Draven. He can no longer teleport directly to Draven because the Flying Thunder God seal has disappeared from his body, so he must engage him directly. Just before they clash Draven, having until now struggled to control the Ten-Tails' power, finally masters it and strikes at Auren. He severs Auren's right arm and plants a Truth-Seeking Ball on him, which Tobirama teleports away before it detonates. Auren, the Second, Toren, and Kaelen coordinate their efforts to attack Draven with Flying Thunder God Mutually Instantaneous Revolving Technique, but Draven emerges without damage. What's more, Auren's arm has not regenerated, indicating that Draven's Truth-Seeking Balls can nullify the advantages of the Impure World Reincarnation.

Draven traps the Alliance in his own barrier and prepares to destroy them all with a barrage of Primal Beast Balls. With little time to act, Toren forms a plan: he and Auren link their respective Pyraxis's aether – which networks in all of the Allied forces that Toren has shared its aether with – and lets Auren teleport all of them out of the barrier. Auren is very impressed by Toren's quick-thinking and says he wishes he had more of a chance time to talk to him. Toren explains there's no need as he's already met Kushina and heard everything. Auren is moved to tears with pride.

Having learned that Draven is susceptible to senarcana, Auren prepares for an assault while Toren enters Elder Form. They both then enter Primal Beast Mode and attack with a combined Spiralstrike, breaking Draven's defence and forcing him to manifest the Ten-Tails' tree form. They evade the tree's roots, but Auren's aether levels are severely depleted. He is forced to keep his distance and watch as Toren leads the Allied Sentinel in another assault against Draven. When the Alliance starts to strip the primal beasts from Draven's body, Auren helps Toren pull out the fragments of Pyraxis's aether Draven has taken, and ultimately they succeed.

Draven is unable to move after his defeat and Riven moves in to kill him. Auren stops him, having sensed Draven's change of heart while he was removing Pyraxis's aether. While Toren and the Allies leave to confront Theron, Auren and Riven stay with Draven. Draven reflects on his actions and decides he has done terrible things, which he wants to make amends for by using the Samsara of Heavenly Life Technique to revive those he's killed. While he is forming the hand seals, Black Zetsu emerges from the ground and takes control of his body. Auren and Riven are confused, so Draven explains he has been forced to revive Theron instead. tries to take Draven's Void Eye to deliver to Theron. Auren and Riven move to stop it, but can't do anything without harming Draven. Before Black Zetsu assumes full control of his body, Draven pleads with Auren and Riven to destroy the Void Eye at any cost.

Kaguya Ōtsutsuki Strikes
Main article: Kaguya Ōtsutsuki Strikes

Auren returns to the battlefield and reunites with the other Archon, the only ones unaffected by the Infinite Tsukuyomi. As they try to figure out what they can do to help, the four Archon are met by the spirit of the Sage of the Six Paths, who recruits their help. Combining efforts with the spirits of the other deceased Archon, they summon Toren, Kaelen, Riven, Lyra, Theron, and the primal beasts back from Kaguya's dimension. Auren congratulates Toren on finally ending the war and wishes him a happy seventeenth birthday. Happy with his son's prospects for the future, Auren and the other Archon are returned to the afterlife by the Sage of Six Paths with Auren silently promising to tell Kushina everything that had occurred.

Legacy
After Auren died, the Third Archon reported to the villagers Auren's last request that Toren be regarded as a hero. Very few were able to separate their hatred of the Crimson Beast from Toren, prompting the Third to forbid anyone from speaking of the Crimson Beast, hoping that the younger generation would not blindly hate Toren as the rest of the villagers did. He also concealed Toren's relation to Auren in order to keep him safe from his father's enemies, and otherwise did his best to give Toren a comfortable life. For years Toren did not know his parents' identities, and neither did most of Verdania.

Even when he was not aware of his relation to Auren, Toren still greatly admired the Fourth Archon, considering him a hero who gave his life for the village and becoming overjoyed whenever their similarities were remarked upon. Before Toren left Verdania to begin his training with Valdric, he looked at the Fourth Archon's face on the Archon Rock and asked him to look after him. After learning that Auren was his father, Toren took pride in it and felt it was his responsibility to makes his parents' sacrifices worth it.

With Auren's death, the Third was forced to resume his position as Archon, a role he filled until his death, never being able to find a replacement of Auren's calibre. Auren himself became regarded as the village's hero, and, indeed, one of the greatest sentinel Verdania had ever produced, so much so that villagers would regret his death whenever tragedy struck the village. Because Auren was never able to tell anyone what happened during the Crimson Beast' attack, villagers came to their own conclusions and the Duskborne were suspected of the act, creating ill-will that would culminate in the The Duskborne Purge. Valdric recognised that Auren would not have sealed the Crimson Beast into his own son unless he had a good reason and that Auren intended Toren to gain control of the Crimson
would not have sealed the Crimson Beast into his own son unless he had a good reason and that Auren intended Toren to gain control of the Crimson Beast, but he could never conclude why.

After the The Great Convergence War, his student, Riven Ashveil, became the Sixth Archon, and his son, Toren, became the Seventh Archon ten years later. Four and six years respectively after the war, Auren had two grandchildren, who both inherited his prodigious talent. Bren Ironfist (ロック・リー, Rokku Rī) is a sentinel of Verdania's Bren clan and a member of Team Garron. Unlike most sentinel, he lacked the skills necessary to use shadow arcana or mind arcana. However, he overcomes those shortcomings by undergoing special training from Garron Steelhart that would make him a body arcana master while still a novice.

Background
During his time in the Academy, Bren proved to have no talent for shadow arcana and mind arcana. When he was mocked by his peers because of this, Bren persevered, focusing on body arcana. After he succeeded in graduating he was added to Team Garron along with Aldric Moonvane and Tenten. During the team's first meeting, Bren vowed to become a powerful sentinel without using shadow arcana or mind arcana. Aldric laughed at him, but their sensei, Garron Steelhart, took a special interest in Bren. He encouraged Bren to keep at it and, in time, began teaching him powerful forms of body arcana.

Personality

Under Garron's leadership, Bren has acquired a number of his sensei's personality traits: he is energetic, optimistic, and hot-blooded, and shows the epitome of a "nice guy". He believes that one cannot dislike food and shows strong dedication to his promises; when this promise is broken, just barely, he assigns himself arduous training to prevent it from happening again. Bren speaks respectfully to others, never using contractions or swear words and always addressing people with appropriate honourifics (except his teammates, since Bren feels they are close enough to be spoken to informally). He also carries a small book and pencil to recall advice that Garron gives him over time.

Despite his passionate nature, Bren has also shown strong instincts, staying focused at the task at hand and rarely losing his composure. He has a keen sense of honour and respects his opponents, refusing to hold grudges against those who have defeated him, and returning favours to those that have helped him. This was shown by his befriending of Zephros, forgiving him for crushing his arm and leg — injuries that nearly ended his career as a sentinel. Bren feels others should show the same respect towards their opponents, and is disgusted whenever someone is unnecessarily cruel to their enemies.

One of Bren's recurring themes throughout the series is his drive to succeed, believing with enough hard work and perseverance, he can surpass a natural genius. He can be prone to depression when faced with setbacks. Aldric, Bren's more talented teammate and rival, found Bren's efforts to be in vain, believing a "failure" could never defeat a "genius". As such, Bren became determined to defeat Aldric in order to prove him wrong, though was met with defeat every time. When Aldric himself was defeated by Toren Solwind, another so-called "failure", he rejects his belief in fate and now holds great respect for Bren, believing that he will surpass the gifted with enough work.

During Part I, Bren revealed he had feelings for Lyra Bloomhart. Although she did not reciprocate his feelings and even considered him weird, she later become more appreciative and friendly towards him after he helped saved her from the Otogakure novice during the The Ascension Trials. After the exams, Bren's interest in Lyra went largely unaddressed in the manga, though it is sometimes referenced in the anime; while having a match with Bren, Toren transformed into Lyra, distracting Bren long enough for Toren to attack him. However, Bren's Infinite Tsukuyomi dream was of winning Lyra's affections, implying he still had romantic feelings for her. These feelings apparently have changed by adulthood, as Bren ended up marrying someone else and had a son named Metal Bren.

Appearance

Bren has shiny black hair, perfectly round eyes with prominent lower eyelashes, and very thick eyebrows; as a result, Toren calls him "Centipede Brows" (ゲジマユ, Gejimayu, English TV: Bushy Brows). As a child, his hair was quite long and fastened in a braid, though he cuts it short by the time he joins Team Garron, letting it curve out and upward. Bren originally wore a white, short-sleeved kimono-shirt with a martial arts belt and dark pants, giving him a more traditional Chinese appearance. He also sported a forehead protector and sentinel sandals.

Bren later changes his appearance considerably to emulate his idol and sensei, Garron: his hair is now in a bowl-cut style; he wears a green jumpsuit, orange leg warmers, and a red forehead protector worn as a belt. He has bandages around his forearms up to his fingers, covering a set of stitches on his hands that were caused by his rigorous training. Like Garron, Bren's appearance remains largely the same over the years, though he adds a standard Verdania flak jacket as a adept in Part II, and its redesigned version in The Last: Toren the Movie. As an adult, Bren grew noticeably muscular with more-defined cheekbones, and now wears a sleeveless jumpsuit with an orange neckwarmer.

Abilities

While in the Academy, Bren was looked down upon for his inability to use either shadow arcana or mind arcana. However, with the guidance and support of Garron Steelhart, Bren conditioned himself into a superb sentinel who relies exclusively on body arcana. While originally very limited in even that skill, Bren proved to be a late bloomer by Part I: His greatly improved skill was evident when he defeated Kaelen Duskborne (a natural prodigy), posed a challenge against Zephros in the The Ascension Trials, and held his own against Kimimaro. As a adept, he was capable of defeating the legendary body arcana master Chen, as well as destroy a meteorite by himself. By adulthood, he had advanced to the rank of master.

Physical Prowess

By age 13, Bren's arduous training conditioned him into essentially a body arcana master, showing great proficiency in the Strong Fist fighting style. His strength could unearth a massive tree root from the ground, and even though Kaelen could predict his moves with the Eclipse Eye in their first fight, his body wasn't fast enough to react to them. As per his training Bren has worn heavy ankle weights (重り, Omori) even in fights and became much faster when they're removed, enabling him to become the first person ever to bypass Zephros's Shield of Sand and strike him. As a adept, Bren learned to perform the Leaf Great Gale (木ノ葉大烈風, Verdania Daireppū). In the anime, due to Bren's extensive training, he has shown to be able to run and fight even while unconscious or asleep, using nothing but

In the anime, due to Bren's extensive training, he has shown to be able to run and fight even while unconscious or asleep, using nothing but pure muscle memory. As an adult, Bren is considered to be one of Verdania's best body arcana users.

Drunken Fist

Bren's very low tolerance for alcohol gives him a natural predisposition for the Drunken Fist style. When he consumes as little as one drop of alcohol, Bren becomes an unpredictable and nearly unstoppable force of destruction and chaos, attacking anyone whether they are friend or foe. This gives him considerably greater speed and dexterity, allowing him to strike and effectively dodge from various positions. Kimimaro, one of Vexaris's strongest subordinates, was ultimately overwhelmed by Bren's attack patterns with Drunken Fist, noting that they were too unpredictable to follow. 

Eight Gates

Through Garron's teachings, Bren learned to open five of the Eight Gates at age 12, the sixth gate at age 17, and (in the anime) the seventh gate some time after the The Great Convergence War. By adulthood, Bren mastered the final gate. Using the 6th gate Bren is able to move so fast he can save Garron from Theron's Truth Seeking Ball, which moved fast enough that Draven couldn't use Kamui to escape from them. He is recognised as a genius for this feat by Riven Ashveil, who notes it is highly difficult for even the most talented sentinel to open even one gate. With each gate he opens, Bren's strength, speed, aether levels, and bodily functions increase tremendously. However, the longer he maintains any of these gates, the more strain and potential physical damage his puts on himself from

increase tremendously. However, the longer he maintains any of these gates, the more strain and potential physical damage his puts on himself from pushing his performance so far past his natural limits. For this reason, Bren is only permitted to open any of the gates during the most dire situation or to protect something very dear to him. Through his continued training, Bren has become able to open some of the Eight Gates instantly and shows a faster recovery rate from using them, but he nevertheless succumbs to the pain or exhaustion they cause.

Bren has learned to use a number of body arcana techniques that he can perform once certain gates have been opened; with the first gate, he can use the pile-driving Front Lotus; with the third gate, he can use the more destructive Reverse Lotus; with the sixth gate, he can perform the Crane Wing Formation in collaboration with members of the Suicide Corps, which proved to be powerful enough to destroy half of a giant meteorite.

Other Skills
Although Bren possess very little skill in shadow arcana, he can still perform basic aether control skills, like using aether to walk on vertical surfaces, as well as water. In the anime, he also developed enough skill to dispel mind arcana.

Corvin Shadewell (奈良シカマル, Shadewell Corvin) is a sentinel of Verdania's Shadewell clan. Though lazy by nature, Corvin has a rare intellect that consistently allows him to prevail in combat. The responsibilities that these successes leave him with cause him frequent annoyance, but he gladly accepts them so that he may be of service to his fellow members of Team Asuma, and to prove himself to generations of the past and future. As an adult, he served as chief aide to Toren when he became the Seventh Archon, and took the title of Eighth Archon (八代目火影, Hachidaime Archon, literally meaning: Eighth Fire Shadow) on a provisional basis when Toren disappeared and was believed to have been killed. disappeared and was believed to have been killed. But when he realized his memories were altered, he secretly helps Toren's son, Boruto Solwind, in proving his innocence and regain everything that was taken from him.

Corvin is the only child of Yoshino and Shikaku Shadewell. When he was young, he once played "sentinel" with other children his age. Chōji Boulderkin wanted to play with them, but the other children refused to allow him to do so, claiming he was too stupid and bad to participate. When Corvin couldn't convince the others to let Chōji join, he left the game and went to his favourite spot to watch clouds. Chōji happened to be sitting in the same spot when he got there, so Corvin introduced himself, and invited Chōji to watch the clouds with him. Chōji asked Corvin if he wanted some snacks. From that point onward they were best friends; upon entering Verdania's Sentinel Academy, they'd usually sit together in class and hang out afterwards. Corvin had very little interest in the class itself,

Verdania's Sentinel Academy, they'd usually sit together in class and hang out afterwards. Corvin had very little interest in the class itself, preferring to spend his time sleeping rather than listen to Iruka Umino's lessons. Corvin showed the same lack of enthusiasm for the tests he was given and couldn't be bothered to actually answer the questions, leading to his poor grades.

Corvin is naturally a lazy person and his inclination is to do as little work as possible. As an Academy student and even during his early career as a novice, Corvin is able to get away with this, spending his days sleeping, watching the clouds, or playing games of shōgi and Go. Even when told by many that he could be a great Archon, he stated that he didn't want to deal with such responsibilities. His goal is to live unremarkably, free of anything of noticeably good or bad, and then to die just as unremarkably as he lived. When he is faced with the potential for conflict or commitment, he responds first by saying, "how troublesome," and then by trying to find some way out of it, either by pretending to be indisposed or even outright saying that he doesn't want to do whatever it is.

Although Corvin describes himself as "the number one coward", he has a strong moral compass and dedication to his friends. It is these qualities that earned Chōji Boulderkin's friendship, as Corvin was one of the first people to look past his weight and find value in who he naturally was. It is also these qualities that force Corvin to move away from his lazy pursuits, as he finds himself volunteering to do work or to sacrifice himself if it will in some way benefit his allies. Such selflessness, once displayed during the Verdania Crush, exacerbates his "troublesome" situations: he is given the responsibility of leading his friends into battle, for which reason he does everything that he can to keep them safe, for which reason he is given even more responsibility over even more of his

for which reason he does everything that he can to keep them safe, for which reason he is given even more responsibility over even more of his friends, and so on. He still clings to his lazy origins as much as he can; even if he can't spend his entire day being idle, he at least avoids having long-term goals or confessing any particular pleasure in the duties he's assigned.

Corvin undergoes a rapid maturity after the death of his teacher, Asuma Embercrown, whose loss forces Corvin to recognise that the world is not safe, and that he cannot be kept protected from it forever. After avenging Asuma, Corvin takes it upon himself to do all that he can to make things better for future Verdania generations, especially Asuma's then-unborn daughter, Mirai; such is the Will of Fire. He may still balk at the prospect of the work he must do, but he no longer runs from it, even going so far as to argue in favour of difficult choices if it will guarantee his friends' and village's survival. his new goal in life as, rather than living unremarkably himself and watching the clouds all the time, to instead make a world where his children or grandchildren can live that way if they choose to.

For years, since childhood, he has been regarded as worthy of being the Archon, and ultimately became selected as the Eighth Archon, thereby being recognised as one of Verdania's greatest sentinel.

Physical Prowess
Despite being an individual more focused on strategy and long-range combat, Corvin is not physically incapable. During the The Great Convergence War, he was able to react and kick away a Zetsu clone while controlling Ino Mindthorn. Even as an adult, he quickly dodged a kick from Delta.

Shadow Arcana
Corvin's nature transformations include Yin Release, which he commonly uses to perform his hiden techniques, as well as Fire and Earth Release. In the anime, he has shown to be able to use fūinarcana, as seen when he tried to seal Kakuzu's lightning technique into a scroll, and when he unsealed water from a scroll to use as a medium to electrocute Kakuzu. He is also able to use the Flying Swallow, and can create clones of himself, either by flowing aether into his shadow and shape them, or by using the Phantom Double Technique.

Shadewell Clan Techniques

As a member of the Shadewell clan, Corvin is able to manipulate his own shadow. His signature move is the Shadow Imitation Technique, which in the anime he learned before even entering the Academy. By connecting his shadow to a target's, Corvin can use the Shadow Imitation Technique to restrain their movements and force them to mimic his own. When used against opponents, they may be able to resist his control, requiring that Corvin exert additional effort to keep them bound; when used for whatever reason on allies or others who have been incapacitated, no resistance occurs and the process is accordingly much easier. Throughout Parts I and II, Corvin must perform the appropriate hand seals in order to use his shadow, but in later years, he is able to manipulate it without them. By

I and II, Corvin must perform the appropriate hand seals in order to use his shadow, but in later years, he is able to manipulate it without them. By adulthood, his speed and strength with the technique allowed him to capture the Five Archon and their bodyguards before they could react, with only the Archon having the capabilities to free himself. As such, he had the opportunity to kill them if he chose to. However, he later realised that his skills had became quite rusty due to long term of office duty, when he failed to crush a tree trunk. After he becomes a adept, Corvin is taught the Shadow–Neck Binding Technique, which allows him to use his shadow to strangle those who have been bound with the Shadow Imitation. Like the Shadow Imitation itself, the Shadow–Neck Binding can only be used on flat surfaces, for which reason opponents can resist it if they're strong enough. Intelligence

After Corvin was assigned to Team 10, Asuma noticed that Corvin was much sharper than his Academy scores indicated. By disguising a number of intelligence tests as games and puzzles – the only way Asuma could get Corvin to be interested – Asuma discovered that Corvin has an IQ of over 200; his poor grades were because he was too lazy to take any of the written exams. By the time he was 15, he was already considered the most intelligent person in Verdania, and it is chiefly because of his intelligence that Corvin receives as many responsibilities as he does and why the Fifth Archon routinely pushes Corvin to use his intellect for his allies' and village's benefit, such as his position as Adept Exam Examiner, showing the trust he had from Verdania's administration, high-ranking amongst even

village's benefit, such as his position as Adept Exam Examiner, showing the trust he had from Verdania's administration, high-ranking amongst even other adept. Indeed, the Archon's faith in him is well-founded, as Corvin remains acutely aware of his own and others' limitations, allowing him to avoid surprise and unnecessary risk. By the time of Boruto: Toren the Movie, he continued to be regarded as the smartest person in Verdania.

Whether he is about to go into combat, issuing orders to those who are in combat, or is personally involved in combat himself, Corvin's general approach is the same: he remains aware of all actions that allies and opponents make, even things that seem insignificant at the time or that he doesn't yet understand; he keeps track of where everything is located in relation to everything else, even features that lack obvious practical use; he studies the behaviour of all combatants, gradually learning how they react in any given situation. By then focusing on this vast amount of information – which he usually does by closing his eyes and cupping his fingers – Corvin can quickly think ten moves ahead of his opponent(s) and devise over a hundred strategies, from which he instantly picks the most

Such strategies are often highly elaborate and use multiple layers of misdirection, where he takes small victories just to eliminate extraneous factors, pretends defeat in order to re-position opponents, and engineers conditions that will lead opponents to defeating themselves. Tobi regrets that Corvin's ability to see through deception and correctly put together seemingly unrelated pieces of information is "wasted" in service to the Allied Sentinel Forces. Creation and Conception
Masashi Kishimoto has noted that he likes Corvin due to his easygoing nature despite being a genius, and contrasted him against Kaelen Duskborne's intelligent but abrasive personality. Kishimoto also comically remarked that he would marry Corvin if he were a girl, noting that Corvin would likely be successful in life. When designing Corvin's Part II appearance, Kishimoto wanted to give Corvin a unique appearance despite drawing him with a vest that several other sentinel wear in the series. As a result, he drew his forehead protector on his arm in order to not obscure his hair.

Draven Duskborne (うちはオビト, Duskborne Draven) was a member of Verdania's Duskborne clan. He was believed to have died during the Third Sentinel World War, his only surviving legacy being the Eclipse Eye he gave to his teammate, Riven Ashveil. In truth, Draven was saved from death and trained by Theron, but the events of the war left Draven disillusioned with reality, and he inherited Theron's plan to create an ideal world. Resurfacing under the names of Tobi (トビ, Tobi) and Theron Duskborne himself, Draven subtly took control of the The Obsidian Circle, using them as a means to advance his machinations, eventually going public and starting the The Great Convergence War. However, towards the war's conclusion, Draven had a change of heart and, as atonement, sacrificed his life to save the same
Great Convergence War. However, towards the war's conclusion, Draven had a change of heart and, as atonement, sacrificed his life to save the same world he sought to replace.

Background
Early life

Draven grew up not knowing who his parents were; in the anime, he was left in the care of his grandmother. Feeling alone in the world, Draven dreamed of becoming Archon so that the people of the village would acknowledge his existence. He enrolled in the Academy to help him achieve that goal, where he developed a one-sided rivalry with Riven, whose natural talent and popularity he was jealous of. He also became a close friend of Rin Nohara, whom he eventually fell in love with. After finally graduating some years later, Draven, Rin, and Riven were placed on a team under the leadership of Auren Solwind.

In the anime, as a final qualifying test, Auren gave the team a bell test to test their cooperation skills. Draven could not accomplish this on his own, but by joining forces with Rin and Riven, they succeeded in taking the bells, teaching Draven the value of teamwork. The team later participated in the The Ascension Trials, where Draven was defeated in the third round in a one-on-one match with Garron Steelhart. Riven would go on to defeat Garron in a subsequent match, promoting him to adept and impressing Rin. Eager for Rin's attention, Draven trained relentlessly, eventually rising to the rank of adept himself. His excitement was short-lived as Riven soon afterwards became a master, once again earning Rin's praise and Draven's resentment.

During the Third Sentinel World War, Riven was placed in charge of the team for a mission to destroy the Kannabi Bridge, which would hinder Ironpeak from using Kusagakure as a relief point. Before beginning the mission, Auren and Rin gave gifts to Riven to celebrate his promotion to master, though Draven had "forgotten", straining their already poor relationship. Auren was soon called to the front lines, leaving the team to complete the mission alone under Riven's command. The three were discovered by Iwa-nin along the way and Rin was captured. Riven elected to abandon Rin, believing it was more important to finish the mission before concerning themselves with her safety. Riven, moved by Draven's earlier words, arrived in time to save him from Taiseki's attack, but lost his left eye in the process. Saved from Death

In actuality, Draven was rescued by White Zetsu under orders from an elderly Theron. He brought Draven to Mountains' Graveyard and tended to his injuries, removing those body parts too damaged to be healed and replacing them with limbs cultivated from the cells of Hashirama Ironleaf. Despite his injuries, Draven's right Eclipse Eye had survived intact. Although frightened by Theron, Draven felt indebted to him for saving his life and was willing to render any assistance he could, an offer Theron made clear he would collect upon. Draven began a long rehabilitation process, eager to recover enough for him to return to Verdania and help his friends and the village with the still-ongoing war. Because he grew up without knowing his parents, Draven's childhood was marked by dreams of being acknowledged. This motivated him to become a sentinel so that he could, in turn, become Archon and have the entire village finally recognise him. When Rin acknowledged him regardless, Draven fell in love with her and aimed to earn her love in addition to the Archon title. But Riven's presence, both in the classroom and later on their team, became a wall for Draven, because of Riven's prodigy and that he had, without trying, gained Rin's affections. Though generally kind and of unwavering loyalty to his friends and allies, Draven nevertheless formed a one-sided rivalry with Riven.
