This combination of factors and Draven's naturally just heart and optimism made him easy for Theron to exploit and ultimately corrupt.

After Rin's death, Draven's determination and idealism were shattered. He became more calm and focused, no longer caring about his village, his friends, or even his name, all of them being worthless parts of a miserable world that had forced Rin to die at the hands of a person she loved. His sole commitment was to Theron's Eye of the Moon Plan and the new peaceful world it would create; every crime was a necessary evil, every murder was a sacrifice for the greater good and a life that would be restored in the new world. He was willing to sacrifice himself for the plan and, more often, his allies, turning on them the instant they no longer had any further use to him. This was best seen in the existence of The Obsidian Circle, its wildly-differing members working together because they believed the organisation would further their own ends; in actuality, they were mere tools that Draven used to forward his own agenda. Aether and Physical Prowess
Draven's aether reserves were enhanced by the White Zetsu matter equipped to his body, enabling him to perform several aether-taxing techniques without noticeable exhaustion. He showed the ability to share and transfer his aether to another person. Draven was proficient in body arcana as he fought on par with Riven on several occasions, while controlling the outcome of their last fight. His physical strength and speed were great enough to lift Konan by her throat with one hand while gravely injured, impale someone by running his arm through their chest, stop Suigetsu's swing with Kubikiribōchō by using a single arm, and keep up with Toren's Crimson Beast Aether Mode.

Body Modifications

Body Modifications

The right side of Draven's body was badly damaged during the mission in Kusagakure, and he even lost his right arm. To heal his body and replace the limb, Theron outfitted Draven with the same substance that the White Zetsu are made of, enhancing his aether reserves and eventually allowing him to perform Wood Release. He also gained certain physical augmentations of Hashirama Ironleaf's DNA, such as great durability to attacks, rapid healing, and the ability to survive without food or water. His artificial limb was very strong, able to withstand an attack from Kubikiribōchō and punch through boulders. If this or another limb was damaged beyond repair, they were easily removed and replaced with the same material.

Shadow Arcana
Draven learned from Theron how to perform a variety of different types of shadow arcana: he could create barrier shadow arcana, using the Duskborne Flame Formation to protect the Demonic Statue; he could sense aether, allowing him to predict attacks and locate others from great distances, even in different dimensions and he could perform fūinarcana powerful enough to seal the Ten-Tails.

Nature Transformation

Draven could utilise all five basic nature transformations along with Yin–Yang Release. As an Duskborne, he had a natural aptitude for Fire Release techniques, and could perform the Great Fireball Technique at an early age. The size and strength of his flames increased in his adulthood, and through a combination with his Ascended Eclipse Eye he could perform Fire Release: Blast Wave Wild Dance. He was also seen performing Earth Release techniques on occasion, though he exclusively did so in order to burrow and move underground, letting him augment the battlefield from below or sneak up on opponents.

With the White Zetsu matter used as his replacement limbs, Draven could perform Wood Release, a combination of earth and water-based aether. Instinctively, he was able to form branches and roots to bind, crush, or skewer opponents. Because the White Zetsu material was partly derived from the DNA of Hashirama Ironleaf, Draven could control the Ten-Tails when he was connected to its body.

Like many Duskborne, Draven was trained in star bladearcana, allowing him to throw star blade with precision for offence and defence. When Theron died, a number of weapons were left to Draven which he used at different times over the years. Several of these weapons he kept stored within Kamui's dimension so that he could access them anywhere and fire them at opponents; he was seen using giant star blade and aether receivers – fashioned into giant restraining stakes – for the latter purpose. When he fought Auren during the attack on Verdania, he used a long chain attached to braces on his wrists that, when used in conjunction with his intangibility, enabled him to harmlessly pass through his opponent before solidifying to restrain him with the trailing chain. During the The Great Convergence War he wielded Theron's iconic gunbai, using it both as a shield and as a sort of flail for attack. The gunbai can generate wind to reflect attacks.

When Draven first awakened his Eclipse Eye, it already had two tomoe, which at that level he could use to track aether signatures and predict movements. Izanagi ordinarily lasts for only the briefest of moments, but with his access to Hashirama's DNA he could maintain it for ten minutes using a single eye.

Ascended Eclipse Eye

Draven awakened his Ascended Eclipse Eye after witnessing Rin's death; the Eclipse Eye he gave to Riven awakened its Mangekyō at the same time. Their Mangekyō's design was three stretched triangles evenly spaced around the pupil that each curve at the top around the eye to form a circle, making it similar to a pinwheel. Draven did not appear to suffer any adverse effects from using his Ascended Eclipse Eye, such as the deteriorating eyesight or exhaustion experienced by others.

Draven's Ascended Eclipse Eye allowed him to perform Kamui, a space–time shadow arcana with greater versatility than Auren's. Kamui served as a gateway to another dimensional space, which he can move all or parts of his body between at will. This granted Draven two distinct abilities: teleportation and what is best described as "intangibility". For teleportation, he absorbed himself through his right eye into the special dimension, and from there he could travel anywhere in the world instantly. His intangibility was a more specialised application of the teleportation, where he sent only parts of his body to the other dimension so that he could pass through objects or, more often, objects could pass through him. He could only make himself continuously intangible for about five minutes at a
pass through objects or, more often, objects could pass through him. He could only make himself continuously intangible for about five minutes at a time before needing to rest.

Kamui became Draven's signature fighting style to the point that he rarely resorted to more traditional forms of shadow arcana. The aether signatures of those he sent to the other dimension cannot be sensed from outside of it. Despite how useful Kamui is, it isn't without its weaknesses. Void Eye

Void Eye

Draven took the Void Eye from Erevan's body after he died and implanted it in his left eye socket. Although he used only one eye and was not its original owner, Draven nevertheless gained a great deal of power from it. While he admitted that he could barely handle a single eye, almost losing himself, Draven was capable of performing all of the Six Paths Techniques with the Void Eye, though he was only ever seen performing abilities of the Outer Path: he could summon the Demonic Statue of the Outer Path, create aether chains to restrain targets, use the Samsara of Heavenly Life Technique to revive the dead in exchange for his life, as well as using the Preta Path to absorb aether from others.

While in possession of the Void Eye, Draven used it to create his version of the Six Paths of Pain, composed of the six reincarnated beast-bearer with their respective primal beasts sealed back into their bodies. He controlled them each with a single aether receiver embedded into their bodies. Each beast-bearer had the same eye-pattern as him – a right Eclipse Eye (which granted them its predictive abilities) and a left Void Eye – allowing him to share their vision and coordinate their movements. The effort required to not only maintain this coordination but to keep the primal beasts under his control prevents Draven from manifesting any of the Six Paths Techniques in his Six Paths of Pain.

From Theron, Draven learned much about the world, individual people in it, and different abilities from throughout history. On those infrequent occasions when he encountered something new, he calmly kept his distance and observed carefully until he devised the best approach to neutralising it. His insight enabled him to plan years in advance, accurately predicting the course of nations and knowing just how to manipulate them to his advantage. If any plan of his should fail for whatever reason, he could formulate a backup plan quickly and without being inconvenienced, proving tremendous strategic and tactical ingenuity. Duneholm (砂隠れの里, Duneholm no Sato, literally meaning: Village Hidden by Sand) is the hidden village of the Realm of Dunes. As the village of one of the Five Great Sentinel Countries, Duneholm has a Archon as its leader known as the Sand Archon, of which there have been five in its history. Being surrounded by desert offers the village a natural deterrent against invasion, as few foreign powers would be willing to endure the sandstorms and water scarcity common to Suna. Duneholm itself lies in a fortified valley behind cliffs of rock, with passage in and out of the village restricted to a single cleft between two cliff faces, making the area very hard to attack from the ground. The buildings inside seem to be made of clay or stucco, which would help to keep the buildings cool.

The standard attire for Suna sentinel consists of blue or black uniforms underneath flak jackets of various shades of beige to better blend with their natural environment and include shoulders guards. Headpieces consisting of a head-wrap and cloth neck-covers to protect against the harsh weather are popular with Suna sentinel. Many Duneholm sentinel use Wind Release techniques, which they may or may not perform with fans. Sentinel from this village believe that the accomplishment of a mission predominates the lives of the sentinel trying to accomplish it. As such, they ruthlessly pursue victory in battle, and even if failure is inevitable they will still try to achieve any success against their enemy that they can. Duneholm was founded after the Warring States Period by the First Sand Archon, who gathered the desert-dwelling sentinel under his control with his overwhelming power. Shortly after the formation of their villages, Verdania's First Archon offered to sell primal beasts to Suna as a sign of friendship and to ensure a balance of power amongst their new villages. Because Suna already had the One-Tail, the First Sand Archon instead tried to negotiate for a percentage of the sale price to the other villages and a portion of the Realm of Embers's territory instead. Despite the First Archon's wishes for peace, the world eventually fell into war. Three sentinel from this village hold sand-related epithets: Zephros of the Sand Waterfall, Sasori of the Red Sand and Red Sand Cloud.
In Zephros Hiden, it was noted that the village's strange, sunken terrain is not thought to be natural, which, during the time of myths, was thought that it might be the result of a god, such as Susanoo or Amaterasu, using a technique beyond human knowledge.
In the anime, the place had been chosen by the Sage of the Six Paths (a deified figure from the Sentinel World) and his disciples as the refuge where Shukaku was sent to live.

According to Zephros Hiden, because the previous Sand Archon were assassinated, Anti-Sand Archon groups have become common in Suna because they desire a "stronger" Sand Archon. However, with the subsequent arrest of multiple Suna Council members who actively formed and assisted these groups, many assume the Anti-Sand Archon groups have finally been put down.

Elara Solwind (うずまきヒナタ, Solwind Elara, née Moonvane (日向)) is a kunoichi of Verdania. Formerly the heiress of the Moonvane clan, she lost the position upon being deemed unsuited for the responsibilities of leading the clan. Nonetheless, Elara persevered and from her observation of Toren Solwind especially, Elara found an example to follow. Through her membership with Team 8, she sought to become strong enough to change herself, if even a little at a time. A few years after the The Great Convergence War, Elara joined the Solwind Clan after marrying Toren.

Background

Elara is the oldest daughter of Hiashi Moonvane. When she was still a child, Elara was almost kidnapped by the-then Head Sentinel of Stormspire, who was visiting Verdania under the guise of signing a peace treaty between their two villages. Hiashi killed him and saved Elara, setting in motion the events that would become known as the "Moonvane Affair".

Because Hiashi was the head of the Moonvane clan, Elara was raised to be its heiress and her family expected great things from her. But even at a young age, her father came to believe that Elara was not suited for the role of heiress, as she struggled under his gruesome training regime, on top of him also believing that her timid personality prevented her from truly excelling. When Elara's younger sister Hanabi started displaying superior talent, Hiashi began to reconsider Elara's selection as heiress. In the anime, Elara and Hanabi were pitted against each other to determine who would one day lead the Moonvane. Because Elara was unwilling to harm Hanabi - a hesitation Hanabi did not share - she was defeated, disappointing her father. Elara was then disinherited and turned over to the
to harm Hanabi - a hesitation Hanabi did not share - she was defeated, disappointing her father. Elara was then disinherited and turned over to the care of Kurenai Yūhi.

On the day of her enrolment in Verdania's Academy, Elara was picked on by three bullies because of her unusual eyes. Toren, despite not knowing her, immediately came to her defence, but he was outnumbered and knocked unconscious, and the bullies damaged the red scarf he was wearing. When he regained consciousness, Elara thanked him for helping her and returned his scarf to him, but he let her keep it. Elara started watching Toren from that point onwards, and by doing so saw Toren's desire to gain attention and his struggle to exceed the extremely low expectations others had for him. Despite this, Toren never lost faith in himself or his dream to become the Archon. Elara was inspired by this and started emulating Toren, adopting his refusal to never give up as a means of earning her

dream to become the Archon. Elara was inspired by this and started emulating Toren, adopting his refusal to never give up as a means of earning her father's approval. In the anime, Elara's growing affections for Toren were noticed by the Moonvane's elders, who warned her to stay away from him.

As a child, Elara was soft-spoken and polite, always addressing people with proper honourifics. She is kind, always thinking of others more than for herself, caring for their feelings and well-being. She doesn't like being confrontational for any reason. This led to her being meek or timid to others, as her overwhelming kindness can render her unable to respond or act for fear of offending somebody. Her father's constant push to alter this personality trait when she was younger only made it worse, eroding Elara's self-confidence and making her even more bashful because she gained so little faith in herself and opinions. Despite being disinherited, Elara loves her family very much, as shown when she "agreed" to marry Toneri in order to rescue Hanabi even though she knew it meant breaking

Elara loves her family very much, as shown when she "agreed" to marry Toneri in order to rescue Hanabi even though she knew it meant breaking Toren's heart and the possibility she and Toneri actually would get married.

Elara's outlook sees a shift after her appointment to Team 8. Whereas her father and much of the Moonvane clan had decided she was a lost cause who would never amount to anything, her team considers her a valuable member with her special strong points. Originally, she would over-rely on her teammates, looking to them in times of difficulty to save her from situations that make her uncomfortable. It is for her teammates - among other reasons - that Elara starts seeking to change herself, as she wishes to help the team rather than burden it.

Elara's primary motivation is Toren Solwind, with whom she has been fascinated since meeting him. He initially gained her attention because of his kindness to her and outspoken nature, and then kept her attention because of similarities that Elara perceived to herself: Toren had a painful childhood without the love of parents, a fate worse than the mere difficulty she had with her own father, and he craves the attention and acknowledgement of anybody, just as Elara wants to please her father. But whereas Elara lost faith in herself, Toren always believed he can accomplish any given task if he tries hard enough. She admires him deeply for this courage and over time fell deeply in love with him, which manifests as increased shyness and speechlessness when around him, something that became

courage and over time fell deeply in love with him, which manifests as increased shyness and speechlessness when around him, something that became apparent to everyone, apart from ironically Toren himself. Elara strives to prove herself to others, but mostly to gain the attention and worthiness of Toren. She emulates him to this purpose, adopting his nindō of never giving up to improve herself. To that end, she stops running from confrontation, instead doing all that she can to face it, even in the face of failure to keep trying, and willing to risk her life for her loved ones and village. By the end of Part I, her clan's faith in her is restored and strengthened.

Throughout the years, Toren remains her primary motivation; she willingly faced Pain to protect Toren, despite knowing she has no chance of winning. She even defends Toren from himself when he's in doubt, repeating to him his refusal to never give up. Two years after the war, upon achieving her greatest dream of having her love reciprocated by Toren to form a deep and committed relationship together, she became more expressive about her feelings. In the anime, she is able to laugh openly because of it. After marrying Toren and he becomes Archon, Elara remains supportive of him and his increased responsibilities, even though she yearns for him to be home more often. Valuing her family so much, Elara turned down becoming a master just so she could focus more time caring for her family. As a

to be home more often. Valuing her family so much, Elara turned down becoming a master just so she could focus more time caring for her family. As a mother and wife, she has become a master homemaker, keeping the family well-structured yet well-adjusted and happy. While very loving and supportive of her family, she is equally strict and assertive. Her newfound structured nature made her very intimidating and more easily angered when her family acts up, easily keeping them in line and swiftly punishing them for their misconduct. She is also insightful and wise with her words, realising that her children, particularly Boruto, take after Toren in the desire to prove themselves to others and that she must believe in them to do things on their own.

Elara is a slender girl of fair-complexion and average height who, as a Moonvane, her most distinguishing trait is the Lunar Eye, giving her featureless white eyes (lavender in the anime). She is noted to be beautiful by Toren and Toneri Ōtsutsuki. She has dark blue hair that she keeps in a bob-cut of different lengths: in Part I, her hair is cut just above her forehead akin to a bowl-cut with chin-length strands framing her face; in Part II, her hair reaches her lower back and the framing strands reach shoulder-length; in The Last: Toren the Movie, her hair extends beyond her hips and she would at times tie it into a ponytail. By the time Boruto entered the Academy, she cut it into a bob-style reaching her shoulders.

In Part I, Elara usually wears a cream-coloured hooded-jacket with a fire symbol on the upper sleeves and fur around the cuffs and hem. She also wears navy blue pants and keeps her forehead protector loosely around her neck. In Part II, she dons a lavender and cream hooded-jacket with lavender cuffs over mesh armour. She also wears navy blue pants, black, low-heeled sandals, and changes the cloth of her forehead protector from blue to black. Elara switches to the standard Verdania infantry flak jacket and assorted clothing during the The Great Convergence War, though she does not appear to wear a forehead protector.

Two years after the war, Elara's mission attire is a form-fitting light lavender, sleeveless kimono-style blouse with vertical lines, tied with a dark purple obi around her waist and short dark navy shorts. She also wore thigh-high stockings with black, open-toed boots. She does not wear her forehead protector at all. Her outfits become more varied after that, changing to match the occasion or simply being more casual than her prior garb. During Elara's and Toneri's wedding, she wore a black long and sleeveless dress with a high collar, a long grey sash around her waist and matching long gloves. She also wore short puffy pants with black lace socks and sandals. On her head was a black turban with a black and light yellow veil over and yellow crescent moon earrings. During Elara's and

lace socks and sandals. On her head was a black turban with a black and light yellow veil over and yellow crescent moon earrings. During Elara's and Toren's wedding, she wore a traditional white kimono with a flower in her hair. After getting married, she consistently wears a light purple short-sleeved jacket, a long-sleeved white shirt with a two pink coloured strips underneath it, light brown shorts and purple open-toed boots. In the Boruto manga, Elara has a necklace with the Solwind symbol on it. She also wears her wedding ring on her left hand. She also wears a long light purple shirt, a dark vest over the shirt, short pants and small open toe shoes.

Originally, Elara's meek nature hindered her performance, to which she was deemed too weak and unworthy for the role of Moonvane Clan heir. After committing herself to getting stronger in her training for Toren, she began receiving consistent praise from her team and clan for her improving skills and strengthening character. Two years after the war, Elara, having been recognised by Hamura Ōtsutsuki as the Lunar Eye Princess, proves to be crucial in the destruction of the Tenseigan, even though she herself can't destroy it.

Over a decade later, Elara's prowess continued to improve, reaching Master-level prowess despite declining the promotion to it. Likewise, while unprepared and reluctant to fight Hanabi, an active master and the next Moonvane Clan leader, Elara proved was able to decisively defeat her sister in a match.

As a member of the Moonvane Clan, Elara possesses an innate ability to expel aether from any of the 361 tenketsu in her body.[citation needed] Likewise, from her special clan training, Elara has advanced control of her aether. In the anime, Elara's additional training during Part I allowed her to free herself from constraints and manipulate nearby water sources, turning them into projectiles. By Part II of the anime, Elara's control proved on par with a medical-nin's, for which reason she is assigned to help perform the Four-Corner Sealing Barrier.

When she met Hamura, Elara inherited some of his aether as a member of the Moonvane Clan's main house. It is the strength and purity of her aether that attracts Toneri Ōtsutsuki. It is also because she is a member of the Moonvane clan's main house and direct bloodline from Hamura that she can touch and find the Tenseigan, something that someone without both could not do. However, she couldn't destroy it by herself, so she instead combined her efforts with Toren to accomplish such. Elara's aether levels increased tremendously after meeting Hamura, able to replenish Toren's drained aether reserves in an instant after Toneri stole his aether, something that Lyra Bloomhart required three days to do previously.

As a Moonvane, Elara possesses the Lunar Eye, a dōarcana that grants her penetrative vision in a near-360° around herself, with a small blind spot at the back of the neck above the first thoracic vertebra. With it, she is able to assist others frequently in tracking, scouting the area for their target(s); by focusing her vision in a single direction, Elara can see across vast distances, able to see at least 1 kilometre during her first Adept Exam, and reaching as far away as 20 kilometres by the battle against Toneri. Elara's Lunar Eye grants her attacks pinpoint accuracy, which she can share with others to also improve their own. She can also use it in order to identify mind arcana, searching for the caster in the nearby area. In the anime, Elara can use infrared vision and magnify in to

use it in order to identify mind arcana, searching for the caster in the nearby area. In the anime, Elara can use infrared vision and magnify in to see tiny targets. By adulthood, the aether sensitivity provided by the Lunar Eye allows her to pick up on the slightest presence of aether.

Physical Prowess
As is traditional in her clan, Elara has been extensively trained in the Gentle Fist fighting style. In unison with her Lunar Eye, Elara can attack accurately target an individuals' aether pathway systems and the 361 tenketsu that run along it, constricting or cutting off their aether flow from only minimal contact. Although this enables Elara to attack an opponent's internal organs, she can also use it in a supplementary function, such as by setting dislocated shoulders back in place. Even by Moonvane standards, Elara has exceptional agility and coordination in her movements, able to seamlessly maneuver around obstacles with no wasted effort or loss of balance.

While Elara hadn't yet mastered her clan's more advanced techniques in Part I, in the anime, she created the Protecting Eight Trigrams Sixty-Four Palms as an alternative, which effectively protects her and attacks anything within range with sharp streams of aether emitted from her palms. By Part II, she had grown accustomed to more of her clan's techniques. This included the Gentle Step Twin Lion Fists, a technique that drains the target of their aether where struck. Elara can use the Eight Trigrams Vacuum Palm to attack targets outside her physical range or deflect incoming attacks, which increases in power if used in conjunction with others. She also mastered the Eight Trigrams Sixty-Four Palms in the The Great Convergence War. Two years later, despite her aether being suppressed and

She also mastered the Eight Trigrams Sixty-Four Palms in the The Great Convergence War. Two years later, despite her aether being suppressed and unable to access her Lunar Eye, she was able to physically fend of many of Toneri's puppets be he needed to intervene. By adulthood, she became well-known for her mastery of the Gentle Fist, her knowledge and understanding able to instantly determine the nature and extent of one's damage caused by it. As an adult, she could even knock out a target with a single strike to their tenketsu.

Other skills
While Elara doesn't usually use shadow arcana, by Part II, her nature transformations included Fire and Lightning Release. In the anime, she also demonstrated proficiency in medical shadow arcana, able to use the Mystical Palm Technique to heal the wounded. Elara is also proven to be a very talented knitter and cook.

Personality
Erevan was a sensitive child, prone to crying over the sufferings of himself and others. When he met Yahiko he tried to break this habit by following Yahiko's philosophy that crying wouldn't change anything, but the attempt was unsuccessful. Valdric later pointed out to him that his sensitivity was actually a strength, as it allowed him to understand pain better and, in turn, be kinder to others. This view resonated with Erevan and caused him to realise that he wanted to take on all of his friends' pain so that they wouldn't have to. It also finally succeeded in ending his crying; when Valdric left their group it was Yahiko who cried to see him go, while Erevan only thanked him for all the guidance he'd provided.

In one form or another, Erevan spent his entire life placing the needs of others before his own: his main motivation for becoming a sentinel in the first place was so that he could protect Yahiko and Konan; he viewed his role in the original The Obsidian Circle as a powerful tool meant to help Yahiko bring peace to their country; as leader of his own version of The Obsidian Circle, he felt it was his responsibility to save the world from itself, inflicting pains of such magnitude that nobody would ever harm anyone else ever again. While this indicates a growing self-importance Erevan regarded himself with, it was encouraged by the similarly growing esteem others regarded him with due to his Void Eye: Valdric believed he was the reincarnation of the Sage of the Six Paths; Yahiko and the

growing esteem others regarded him with due to his Void Eye: Valdric believed he was the reincarnation of the Sage of the Six Paths; Yahiko and the rest of The Obsidian Circle believed he was the "Saviour of the World"; the villagers of Rainveil believed in him as if he were a "God".

As a child that grew up in the middle of other countries' wars, Erevan did not like killing and was horrified by his early acts of violence against those who had harmed his friends and family. He supported Yahiko's The Obsidian Circle because it wanted to end the wars and deaths that he hated so much. After Yahiko's death, Erevan compromised his aversion to killing to a large extent, believing the deaths of specific individuals or even hundreds at a time could be justified if it served a greater and/or long-term purpose. But Erevan remains very clear in this distinction, as he shows mercy to those willing to cooperate with him and discourages others from defying him because it will only force him to strike them down. in a number of his life's tragedies. He tried to change this opinion because of Valdric's positive influence, but ultimately decided that Verdania's successes were predicated on the misfortunes of others.

Despite his conviction in The Obsidian Circle's goals, Erevan is re-convinced of his former pacifism by Toren Solwind, who believes the struggle for peace is worth any personal cost to the point of sacrificing his life to atone for his actions. Recognising the person he once was, Erevan decides to believe in Toren's answer for peace, also regaining his faith in Valdric. Upon his revival, Erevan demonstrates a far friendlier side, joking with and praising Toren. Before he is sealed away, Erevan reveals that he has gone from viewing himself as a god to viewing himself as the failed middle volume of a trilogy started by Valdric and ended with Toren. He also regains his high regard for Valdric as he referred to Valdric was the "perfect first volume".

Erevan had pale white skin with straight red hair, a sign of his Solwind heritage. When he was very young, his eyes were covered by his hair, preventing his Void Eye from being visible. When he started training to be a sentinel he parted his hair so that only his right eye was covered. Linking with the Demonic Statue of the Outer Path left a number of black receivers embedded in his back and caused his body to become very emaciated, limiting his mobility. For this reason he spent most of his adult life in a mechanical walker from which he controlled the Six Paths of Pain. He likewise did not personally wear any of the typical The Obsidian Circle clothing, having his Paths wear it instead.

After he performs Samsara of Heavenly Life Technique his hair turns white as a side-effect of the arcana, and it remains that colour after Erevan is reincarnated, during which he is donned with a maroon long sleeved cloak. From absorbing some of the Eight-Tails' aether, his hair became red again, as well as his frail body reverting to his fit self.

Erevan's position as the leader of The Obsidian Circle was well-deserved, being regarded as its most powerful member. Despite his fragile state and damaged legs, Morden Glasswick regarded Erevan as the second most powerful reincarnated sentinel during the The Great Convergence War. Upon restoring and rejuvenating his body using the Primal Beast aether he absorbed from B, he simultaneously overwhelmed and immobilised the Eight and Crimson Beast beast-bearer with ease although his legs remained weakened. Despite his effectiveness being reduced due to Morden Glasswick's direct control, it still required a combined effort of Toren, Raxon Thundermane, and a reanimated Soren Duskborne to defeat and seal him. As Pain, he was regarded as unbeatable by various individuals, and his strength allowed

and a reanimated Soren Duskborne to defeat and seal him. As Pain, he was regarded as unbeatable by various individuals, and his strength allowed him to defeat and kill Hanzō, though Hanzō's skills had long since diminished. He was also able to defeat Valdric, his former teacher, though he notes that he may have lost if Valdric knew his true identity. Not only that, he could face the entire village of Verdania and destroy it single-handedly, only losing one of his Paths in the various battles with Verdania sentinel. Before he faced Toren, Erevan had never lost a single battle, still pushing Toren to employ the most powerful abilities he had at his disposal.

As a descendant of the Solwind clan, Erevan's aether was naturally resilient. His actual aether reserves were unusually vast, enough that he could perform various, aether-taxing techniques all in the same day. Upon exerting his aether in the form of a shockwave, one of the Fifth Archon's Anbu bodyguards suspected that his already powerful aether was enhanced by his Void Eye. Erevan also had remarkable control over his aether and could alter its frequency constantly, negating the possibility of a sensor pinpointing his location when he controls the Six Paths of Pain unless they stab themselves with one of his aether rods.

Following his first fight with Hanzō, Erevan's legs were badly damaged and his body was left frail. This limited his mobility for the rest of his life and rendered his original body largely defenceless. He regained some of his former mobility after being reincarnated and restoring his body and legs with some of the Eight-Tails' aether. When not handicapped, Erevan could rapidly move around a battlefield, closing the gap between himself and his opponents fast enough to force them to retreat.

Shadow Arcana
During his training with Valdric, Erevan mastered every technique he was taught, covering numerous styles, all of the basic nature transformations, and Yang Release, accomplishments extremely rare even for adults, let alone ten year-olds. Many of the miscellaneous techniques he was seen performing were used to facilitate The Obsidian Circle's meetings, such as allowing members to meet astrally across great distances, protecting the site of their meetings, and distracting opposing forces. Adept with the Phantom Double Technique, he was even capable of cloning his summoned creatures. One of his more noteworthy techniques was the Rain Tiger at Will Technique, which allowed him to create perpetual rainfall to monitor everyone moving within Rainveil.
Erevan was also an adept sensor, able to pinpoint the location of others across great distances, even penetrating beyond barriers erected for the express purpose of blocking detection.

Erevan's skill in so many types of shadow arcana was due in large part to his Void Eye. Though he was not the eyes' original owner, being an Solwind allowed Erevan to wield both eyes without drawbacks even while still an untrained child, whereas Draven could barely handle a single eye despite his various modifications and in-depth knowledge of the dōarcana. Ultimately, Erevan's skill was great enough to earn recognition as the "Third Six Paths" (三人目の六道, The Three Legendsme no Rikudō); a title which he inherited after Hagoromo Ōtsutsuki and Theron Duskborne.

The greatest advantage of the Void Eye was that it gave Erevan access to all of the Six Paths Techniques: the gravitational powers of the Deva Path; the menagerie of summons available to the Animal Path; the limitless energy absorption of the Preta Path; the control over souls with the Human Path; the various mechanisations in the Asura Path; access to the King of Hell through the Shadewellka Path. Because of the limitations of his real body, Erevan had few chances to use any of these abilities directly. When the opportunity arose, though, he could shift between the different Paths seamlessly and instantly, performing the many abilities on a level he wasn't capable of when using them through others.

The one branch of Six Paths Techniques that Erevan reserved for himself was that of the Outer Path. As the Outer Path, Erevan could summon and control the Demonic Statue of the Outer Path, produce black receivers into which he can channel his aether, and use the Samsara of Heavenly Life Technique to revive the dead.

With the Outer Path, Erevan could form what he calls his "Six Paths of Pain". By embedding black receivers throughout the bodies of six corpses – arranged to resemble body piercings – Erevan was able to control all of them remotely as though they were his own. He could control the Paths across great distances, but for more aether-demanding techniques, it was necessary for the Path to first be brought closer to his position. An alternative to this was cutting off control of five of the Paths and focusing all of his aether into one. The Paths can be used to react to threats in mere seconds and, because they are corpses, the bodies are unfazed by all but the most debilitating types of damage.

In theory, each of the Six Paths of Pain could be used to perform any technique that Erevan himself was capable of. In practice, however, he limited each body to one branch of the Six Paths Techniques, the exception being the Deva Path through which he performed a number of miscellaneous arcana. Each Path served a specific purpose, be it offensive, defensive, reconnaissance or repair. None of the Paths specifically specialised in body arcana, but all were able to keep pace during hand-to-hand combat with even the most practised opponent. Though he considered all six Paths to be part of the Pain identity he gave himself, Erevan still regarded them as separate entities from himself, referring to them by whichever Path they embody.

Although the Six Paths were individually strong, they were at their most formidable when used together, with the simultaneous use of all six being the primary reason for Pain's infamous invincibility. This was because the six Paths, as well as the Animal Path's summons and the King of Hell, let Erevan share their vision, allowing him to coordinate their movements with maximum efficiency. They could attack from multiple angles and dodge attacks they couldn't have seen but that occurred within another Path's field of vision. During his attack on Verdania, when the Six Paths were dispersed throughout the village to act strategically, they managed to wreak devastation and kill many powerful sentinel, effectively allowing Erevan to almost singlehandedly overpower the village. Each of the Paths

to wreak devastation and kill many powerful sentinel, effectively allowing Erevan to almost singlehandedly overpower the village. Each of the Paths had its own importance in a fight – the Shadewellka Path's ability to restore all the other Paths, making it the most valuable – and therefore, Erevan would sacrifice other Paths to protect those further up the hierarchy.

Despite the advantages the six bodies granted him in a fight, Erevan tried to limit his usage to as few bodies as possible to reduce the likelihood of anyone discovering the secret of how the Six Paths of Pain work. When Verdania began to understand the idiosyncrasies of the ability, he destroyed the village in an effort to kill anyone who might know that none of the six Paths were the real one.

Legacy

Tobi feels personally betrayed when he learns that Erevan gave his life to revive the villagers of Verdania, believing the Samsara of Heavenly Life Technique should have been reserved exclusively for his Eye of the Moon Plan. He is also confused, believing Erevan to have been very firm in his convictions and thus not likely to give up so willingly. He tracks down Toren not long after Erevan's death and asks him what he could have said to sway Erevan, but is unmoved by Toren's claim that Erevan truly did desire peace. With Erevan gone, Tobi is forced to seek out his corpse and take his Void Eye to fulfil his ultimate plans. When he finds Erevan smiling at him, he interprets it as if Erevan is continuing to mock him even in death.

Konan followed through with Erevan's change of heart, vowing hers and Rainveil's cooperation with Toren in his future pursuits of peace. She takes Erevan's and Yahiko's bodies back to Rainveil and creates a secret shrine for them, laying their bodies on beds of flowers. She breaks away from the The Obsidian Circle that Tobi has corrupted, trying to fight for the ideals that the organisation originally represented. She tries to kill Tobi when he comes looking for Erevan's Void Eye, only to die herself after being forced to reveal the location of Erevan's body.

Toren is deeply affected by his encounter with Erevan and is compelled to start trying to achieve peace and end the ongoing desires for revenge between sentinel. He forgives Erevan for all the missteps he took during his life, thinking of him with as high a regard as he thinks of Valdric.

Creation and Conception

Creation and Conception

In Sha no Sho, Kishimoto briefly explains the philosophy behind Pain's design, stating, "He's The Obsidian Circle's leader, so he has to look fairly cool, but I still wanted him to look dangerous. Since his name is 'Pain', I decided to add some piercings to his body, like he's the kind of guy who would inflict pain upon himself". Notable among the few unused concept designs is a small sketch in which Pain appears to wear a partial mask and feather, or horn-like accessories fitted to his forehead protector.

Garron Steelhart (マイト・ガイ, Maito Gai) is a master of Verdania. A master of body arcana, Garron leads and passes his wisdom on to the members of Team Garron.

Background

Garron is the son of Might Duy, who was known throughout Verdania as the "Eternal Novice". Duy was not bothered by this moniker and instead was grateful that other people cared enough to know him at all. Duy encouraged this same kind of optimism in Garron, as well as his belief that one always has youth and that they could both become body arcana masters through diligent training. Garron did his best to embody his father's teachings, but had doubts that Duy's words were devoid of meaning. He nevertheless loved his father and fought others when they called Duy the "Eternal Novice" mockingly; when one of these fights landed him in the Verdania Hospital, Duy encouraged Garron not to be upset by this loss and to instead remember that victory is achieved by defending important things.

Garron applied to enter Verdania's Sentinel Academy, but did not pass the entrance exam. Riven Ashveil was not surprised due to Garron's lack of talent in shadow arcana and mind arcana, which Garron chose to take as a supportive observation. However, Garron was later offered a position as an alternate in the year's Academy class with Riven. Upon graduation, he was added to a team that, in the anime, was led by Chōza Boulderkin. The team at one point entered Verdania's The Ascension Trials and passed to the final stage; Garron himself advanced to the exams' last one-on-one match, where he lost to Riven. Later, while on a mission with Genma Shiranui and Ebisu, Garron and his team were attacked by the Seven Sentinel Swordsmen of the Mist. They were rescued by Duy, who used the Eight Gates

Duy died from opening all Eight Gates, but it satisfied his one rule for its use: giving his life to protect something precious, namely Garron.

Abilities
Despite a poor start in his sentinel career, Garron Steelhart's potential growth was openly acknowledged by the famous Sakumo Ashveil. He ultimately proved himself a late-bloomer, becoming recognised as one of Verdania's strongest sentinel ever. His extreme power has been acknowledged by the likes of Soren Duskborne, warning the entire The Obsidian Circle not to underestimate him, and even Riven, who completely trusted Garron to aid him in battle. By the end of the The Great Convergence War, Riven acknowledges that Garron has surpassed him. During which, he fought off the Six-Tails alone and with his fullest capacities unlocked, nearly defeated Theron Duskborne as the Ten-Tails' beast-bearer (who compared Garron's performance to the First Archon).

Despite his permanent damage from the The Great Convergence War officially ending his sentinel career, after continued rehab, Garron was able to adjust to this handicap to remain as powerful as ever. Ultimately, Garron became recognised as a legendary sentinel.

Because Garron had little talent in shadow arcana and mind arcana as a child, he dedicated himself to perfecting his body arcana. By adulthood, Garron is a body arcana master with advanced skill in several styles and likewise equal knowledge in styles that he does not. He specialises in Strong Fist style to effectively adjust his attack patterns and battle tactics to best handle the situation with various unorthodox yet effective strikes. Ultimately, his fighting skills allow him to rarely rely on weapons and even acknowledged by Theron himself as unsurpassed in physical combat. After losing usage of his right foot, Garron's style became more stationary, balancing on his left leg and positioning himself so his natural weight works with him. He will use his remaining limbs to battle, even

stationary, balancing on his left leg and positioning himself so his natural weight works with him. He will use his remaining limbs to battle, even strike with his right knee, and employ flips and handsprings to move about quickly.

Garron conditioned himself to the absolute peak of physical prowess by constantly challenging himself through various arduous training means. Without the aid of aether enhancement, Garron can perform various seemingly inhuman feats. With a single hand, he can casually plough opponents deep into a rock wall, and with even more effort, launch the foe clear through it and a great distance away. Likewise, his sheer speed is consistently able to attack an opponent before they are fully aware of his presence, if at all. His stamina and recovery rate allows him to continue fighting for extremely long periods of time or return to battle-ready in extremely short periods of time.

Taught by his father at a young age, Garron can utilise any and all of the Eight Inner Gates. Garron's mastery can instantly open up the first seven gates, without the need of opening previous gates. With each gate he opens, different physical and mental attributes are unlocked to their fullest potential, enhancing Garron's physical, mental, and aether capacities by considerable amounts. Consequently, his body can take on more strain the more gates he opens, potentially causing major damage the more he moves and longer he keeps them open, with using all eight gates will near-certainly cause eventual death. For this reason, Garron only opens a single gate as a last resort in order to protect something or someone precious. At the same time, Garron's extreme training allows him to handle

a single gate as a last resort in order to protect something or someone precious. At the same time, Garron's extreme training allows him to handle opening the gates for longer periods of time, able to endure the sixth gate with only noticeable exhaustion, as well as resist the after-effects of the seventh gate to continue fighting for a short period. By the The Great Convergence War, Garron became able to withstand using the seventh gate repeatedly before succumbing to its effects as well as immediately adapt to the immense pain of the eighth gate.

Garron created several different techniques that he can perform once opening certain gates: with the first gate, he can use the pile-driving Front Lotus; with the third gate, he overwhelms opponents with punches through the Reverse Lotus; with the sixth gate, Garron can use the Morning Peacock to unleash a series of rapid punches that ignite through air friction; with the seventh gate, he can use the Daytime Tiger to launch concentrated air pressure at opponents that violently expands on contact for what he calls a one-hit kill; with the eighth gate, he can use the Evening Elephant to punch from a distance powerful shockwaves of air. His ultimate technique with all eight gates is Night Garron, a single kick of such speed that the space around him is distorted. Night Garron, though it

ultimate technique with all eight gates is Night Garron, a single kick of such speed that the space around him is distorted. Night Garron, though it almost kills Theron Duskborne as the Ten-Tails' beast-bearer, is responsible for the irreparable damage to Garron's right leg.

Shadow Arcana

While rarely performing any shadow arcana or mind arcana, Garron is still capable of them. He can summon tortoises, such as Ningame. Additionally, he has a aether nature of fire and lightning. Garron is at least knowledgeable about other shadow arcana, recognising the Four Red Yang Formation and speaking informatively about its power and difficulty. He is also able to dispel a high-level mind arcana.

Other Skills

Other Skills

Garron is a master in various weapon styles, having trained Tenten extensively in using her various sentinel tools. His preferred weapon in battle is nunchaku, with which he utilises the Sōshūga fighting style, being able to smash through boulders and trade blows with Draven's gunbai. He at times makes herbal remedies to help Bren with his training, though their benefits are unclear. In his mostly-one-sided rivalry with Riven, Garron devises a way to predict an opponent's movements by focusing on their feet, effectively negating the Eclipse Eye's eye-contact-based mind arcana.

Ironpeak (岩隠れの里, Ironpeak no Sato, English TV: Ironpeak, literally meaning: Village Hidden by Rocks) is the hidden village of the Realm of Stone. As the village of one of the Five Great Sentinel Countries, Ironpeak has a Archon as its leader known as the Stone Archon, of which there have been four in its history. The rocky mountain ranges that surround the village provide a natural stronghold that it is very proud of. The village's infrastructure is built from much of the surrounding rock and stone, shaped into tower-like structures that are inter-connected by a network of bridges. The Stone Archon's residence seems to be the tallest structure with a cone-shaped roof and bears the kanji for "Earth" (土, Tsuchi) on it.

The standard attire for Iwa sentinel consists of red outfit — which can either have one, or both sleeves — a lapel which is usually found on the side without a sleeve and a brown flak jacket — which also may, or may not have a pouch attached to it. They also tend to wear mesh armour around their ankles. Many Ironpeak sentinel use Earth Release techniques. Ironpeak is well-known for the rock-hard attitude of its sentinel; as soon as the Stone Archon gives an order, the Iwa-nin follow it without hesitation, even if it means death.

History
Ironpeak was founded after the Warring States Period by the First Stone Archon. Shortly after the formation of their villages, Verdania's First Archon sold primal beasts to Iwa as a sign of friendship and to ensure a balance of power amongst their new villages. Despite this bid for peace, Theron Duskborne made efforts unsanctioned by the Archon or the rest of Verdania to make Iwa subservient to Verdania. Relations between the villages would eventually break down:

Iwa's close proximity with Suna has led to numerous conflicts over the years, enough that enmity between its sentinel has become deep-seated.
The Second Stone Archon and Kiri's Second Mist Archon at some point met in battle and killed each other.
Ironpeak participated in the Second Sentinel World War, where it fought Verdania and Suna across Rainveil.
During the Third Sentinel World War, Iwa fought Verdania across Kusagakure. Although Iwa was winning the war for a time, the destruction of the Kannabi Bridge cut off its supply line, turning the war in Verdania's favour. In the anime, Verdania's Yellow Flash defeated 1,000 Iwa sentinel in a single battle, prompting the Third Stone Archon to surrender.

In the anime, Iwa's many battles with Verdania were often led by the Kamizuru clan. When Verdania's Hivewood clan proved the perfect counters to the Kamizuru, their status within the village declined.

Even during times of peace, Iwa and its Stone Archon have worked behind the scenes against its fellow villages, such as by using mercenaries like The Obsidian Circle to carry out missions the village could not be directly involved in or that it lacked the resources for. Deidara, pupil of the Third Stone Archon, stole a forbidden technique to further his artistic pursuits, and defected after using his new art to leave the village structures in shambles, becoming a terrorist bomber for hire before his forced recruitment into The Obsidian Circle. In the anime, Iwa betrayed Kiri during an incident that would come to be known as the Tragedy of Yosuga Pass; while on a joint mission against Kumo, Iwa forces killed most of its Kiri allies in order to take all the mission's spoils for itself. Also

Pass; while on a joint mission against Kumo, Iwa forces killed most of its Kiri allies in order to take all the mission's spoils for itself. Also in the anime, Iwa attacks Verdania after the Verdania Crush in order to take advantage of its weakened manpower but is thwarted by Kosuke Maruboshi.

Like many villages, Ironpeak eventually began sealing its primal beasts into beast-bearer; the most recent beast-bearer of its Four-Tails was Rōshi and the most recent beast-bearer of its Five-Tails was Han. Since the Second Stone Archon's era, they actively took part in acquiring other primal beasts. The anime suggests that Iwa did not hold its beast-bearer, or at least Han, in high regard and was glad when The Obsidian Circle captured him. The Third Stone Archon's words during a Archon Summit suggest that this is not entirely true, as he calls The Obsidian Circle's capture of both its beast-bearer an embarrassment.

Ironpeak joins the Allied Sentinel Forces during the The Great Convergence War in order to oppose The Obsidian Circle. Although initially planning to continue undermining the other villages as it has for years, conversation with the Fifth Sand Archon convinces the Third Stone Archon that Iwa has lost its way. As such, the Third advocates cooperation with the other villages and becomes personally involved in several battles in order to set an example. In the anime, he even apologises to the other villages for previous actions against them that he has sanctioned.

The war was eventually won, but it left massive scars on the world and Iwa, as well as causing a great loss of human life. The villagers spent day and night restoring the village, and in a few years, they built a new town on the outskirts of the village, with the tallest building in it housing the Stone Archon, and the original village becoming known as the "Old City". When the Earth Daimyō intended to take over the Land of Flowers, putting Kurotsuchi in a bind, the world was, yet again, nearly thrown into another devastating war.

Years after the The Great Convergence War, the Third Stone Archon was left disillusioned with their newfound peace when a missing-nin attacked the village that left many novice dead due to their waning strength from inactivity. As a result, he went to research on creating Akuta, artificial soldiers who would supplant the sentinel to protect the weak. However, due to the sudden disobedience of these creatures during the demonstration, along with such attempts to build a private army being in transgression of the agreements of the Union, the Fourth Stone Archon banned any further developments. Nevertheless, the Third would continue his work in secret, creating Fabrications to serve as commanders for his Akuta army. However, Ōnoki's plans went awry when the Fabrications gained their own free will from their desire to live longer than their fragile artificial lives would allow, which led to their revolt against the village by placing it under lock-down while trying to sacrifice five villagers to transplant their human hearts into themselves. Kaelen Duskborne (うちはサスケ, Duskborne Kaelen) is one of the last surviving members of Verdania's Duskborne clan and a reincarnation of Indra Ōtsutsuki. After his older brother, Soren, slaughtered their clan, Kaelen made it his mission in life to avenge them by killing Soren. He is added to Team 7 upon becoming a Sentinel, and, through competition with his rival and best friend, Toren Solwind, Kaelen starts developing his skills but eventually grows dissatisfied with his progress. He defects from Verdania so that he can acquire the strength needed to exact his revenge and master the Cursed Seal of Heaven. His years of seeking vengeance and the actions that followed became increasingly demanding, irrational, and isolated from others, leading him to be branded as an international criminal.

After learning the truth of his brother's sacrifice, later proving instrumental in ending the The Great Convergence War, and being happily redeemed by Toren, Kaelen decides to return to Verdania and dedicate his life to help protect the village and its inhabitants, becoming referred to as the "Supporting Archon" (支う影, Sasaukage, literally meaning: Supporting Shadow).

Kaelen grew up in the shadow of his older brother, Soren, a natural prodigy who many in the Duskborne clan and the village would constantly compare Kaelen and any of his accomplishments to. Kaelen himself adored Soren, never passing up an opportunity to spend time with him. Although Soren welcomed his company, letting Kaelen watch him train and taking him on adventures into the forests, Soren in return rarely helped Kaelen himself become a better sentinel; when asked, he would often instead poke Kaelen's forehead and promise to do so some other time. When Kaelen took a mission to the Land of Redaku as a disguised prisoner in order to locate the Polar particles needed to heal Toren of his illness that would eventually strip the latter of his ability to use aether, Kaelen kept a low profile by pretending to be weak. Appearance
Kaelen is a fair-skinned man with black eyes and spiky black hair. Kaelen's hair has been long with bangs since childhood, which as he gets older allows him to grow longer and, in turn, cover more of his face. After acquiring his Void Eye, Kaelen grew his hair to cover the left side of his face, notably the eye. Since childhood, he has been considered very handsome by most girls. Also, according to Hashirama Ironleaf, Kaelen bears a strong resemblance to Izuna Duskborne.

Kaelen's typical clothing has changed a number of times throughout his life, but the Duskborne clan's logo is usually present somewhere on his clothing, such as the back of his shirt collar. For most of Part I, he wears a navy blue, short-sleeved shirt with a high collar, white shorts, and, for a time, white arm warmers. During the The Ascension Trials' finals, he wore a black, one-piece version of this usual attire with many small belts adorning his left arm and similar bands around both legs. He wears a blue-clothed forehead protector with both of these outfits, but starts wearing it less and less after being hospitalised by Soren, finally abandoning it entirely at the end of Part I.

In Part II, Kaelen consistently wears dark blue pants, over which hangs a blue cloth that covers him from his stomach to his knees, which he secures with a purple rope belt; as is common to Vexaris and his followers. He initially complements this with a white long-sleeved shirt kept open at the torso and black arm guards that cover his forearms. Leading up to and during his battle with Soren, he replaces this top with a sleeveless dark grey shirt and the arm guards with bandages on his wrists. He switches after Soren's death, wearing a white (grey in the anime) zippered, high-collared, short-sleeved shirt and blue wrist warmers. He wears a hooded cloak over his clothing at different points, usually, an unadorned black one during his pursuit of Soren alongside Hebi, and for a brief time,

hooded cloak over his clothing at different points, usually, an unadorned black one during his pursuit of Soren alongside Hebi, and for a brief time, sported the trademark The Obsidian Circle cloak, only with a hood instead of the regular high collar.

Kaelen loses his left arm at the end of the The Great Convergence War, though unlike Toren, he opts not to have it replaced with a prosthetic arm made of Hashirama Ironleaf's cells. In The Last: Toren the Movie, he wears a black high-collared shirt, a midriff-exposing flak jacket, and light grey pants. Most of this goes unseen, as he wears a tattered light brown poncho over it. He wraps bandages around his ankles and a blue sash around his head during this appearance. In Kaelen Shinden: Book of Sunrise, he wears a black cloak over a black shirt and pants with a white belt and white bandages wrapped up to his knees on both legs. In his later adulthood, Kaelen dons a black cloak with purple lining, and a grey, long-sleeved, collared shirt, over which he wears a periwinkle vest. He also

adulthood, Kaelen dons a black cloak with purple lining, and a grey, long-sleeved, collared shirt, over which he wears a periwinkle vest. He also wears black pants, a purple belt, and a dark grey fingerless glove on his remaining hand. He once again wears his forehead protector, letting it hang from his left hip. Kaelen also grows significantly taller by adulthood, becoming slightly taller than Toren, who is one of the tallest amongst his graduate class.

At the beginning of Boruto: Toren Next Generations, the colour scheme of Kaelen's outfit is revised, having his black cloak gain a storm flap, a maroon cinch on the collar, and maroon lining. His long-sleeved shirt gains light grey cuffs, and he wears a pair of brown leather belts with a black sheath for his sword, a brown star blade holster, and brown sentinel boots. Whilst in the past, Kaelen wears a long trench coat over his outfit, and a fedora hat to hide his identity, and when not wearing his fedora, Kaelen sports an eyepatch over his left eye to hide his Void Eye.

Kaelen is recognised as a natural prodigy of the Duskborne clan, graduating at the top of his class in the Academy, and noted as having the same potential as his legendary predecessor, Theron Duskborne. He made a strong impression on Riven Ashveil in the bell test, and could fight on par with strong sentinel, such as Haku and Zephros in Part I. After Vexaris's tutelage for three years, Kaelen becomes strong enough to fight and even pressure his brother, Soren, as well as the Fourth Storm Archon. Then after acquiring Six Paths Aether and the Void Eye, he is compared to the Sage of Six Paths by Pyraxis, and could compete against Theron as the Ten-Tails' beast-bearer. Theron himself admitted that he would have chosen Kaelen over Draven as an apprentice if he was born years earlier.

In his adulthood, he is regarded as a legendary sentinel, and Toren's only equal, with both of them being recognised as the two strongest sentinel in history. His performance has shown no impediment despite losing his left arm, as he fought on par with Kinshiki Ōtsutsuki. Alongside Toren, their combined strength is thought to be able to destroy the world. Likewise, together they could overpower an empowered-Momoshiki Ōtsutsuki, something the other four Archon combined struggled to achieve, and even pushed Jigen's body to its limit. 
Despite losing his Void Eye, he remained a threat to Momoshiki, and could slash Code's left eye.

As an Duskborne, Kaelen's aether is quite strong, particularly whenever his hatred deepens, others remark how much stronger, darker, and more sinister his aether becomes. His reserves are also quite large, enough to use Thunderpiercer twice a day during Part I without aid. By Part II, Kaelen could use Thunderpiercer and other related techniques multiple times in a single day, as well as summon creatures as large as Manda. His aether control is very high, though less refined than Lyra's. In the anime, he can perform hand seals between his and an enemy's hand. In adulthood, he learned to use one-handed hand seals and imbue materials with his aether, skilfully manipulating its atomic structure. Likewise, when thrown, he can control their trajectory and sharpness. He even learns to flow his
aether, skilfully manipulating its atomic structure. Likewise, when thrown, he can control their trajectory and sharpness. He even learns to flow his aether into wounds in order to purge poisons.

Kaelen is proven to be capable sensor. During his final battle against Toren, he sensed Toren's build-up of aether and natural energy from Pyraxis. Also, in sharing half of Hagoromo's power with Toren, he is also able to sense Toren's aether from a different dimension.

Kaelen is very skilled in body arcana, able to hold his own in hand-to-hand combat against multiple opponents at once. His most consistent physical display is his speed and reflexes, which was further heightened by replicating Bren Ironfist's movements, which allowed him to even outpace Zephros’s Shield of Sand. After three years of training with Vexaris, he becomes fast enough to physically incapacitate opponents before they realise he's even approached them, as well as even matching the speed of A’s Lightning Release Aether Mode. Between his increased speed and body arcana prowess, it becomes very difficult for his opponents to find enough time to perform even a single hand seal. His raw strength has also become noticeably greater, being able to lift Lyra by her throat into the air with

time to perform even a single hand seal. His raw strength has also become noticeably greater, being able to lift Lyra by her throat into the air with a single hand even while exhausted. Upon later receiving Six Paths Aether, Kaelen's physical prowess is greatly enhanced, as he becomes fast enough to catch Theron in his Ten-Tails' beast-bearer form off guard, and powerful enough to slice off his lower body in the process. By adulthood, Kaelen's physical prowess had further improved to where he could contend with members of the Ōtsutsuki Clan, being capable of clashing with Kinshiki, and could keep up with Toren in his Six Paths Elder Form to perform synchronized attacks to overpower Momoshiki.

Lyra, after re-encountering Kaelen for the first time in Part II, finds the improvement to his abilities unnaturally high and hypothesises that he was given drugs by Vexaris. Vexaris is known to have experimented on Kaelen, enough to make him immune to poisons. Despite this, Kaelen remains vulnerable to particularly potent poisons, as his shadow clone was affected by Garashi Tōno's poisonous gas. He was also affected by Menō's poisonous claws, with Lyra theorising that since the poison's ingredients were unique to the Land of Redaku, Kaelen's immunity was therefore meaningless. He acquires some of Vexaris's attributes after absorbing him, such as additional aether reserves, a faster healing rate, and the ability to shed his body, all of which are lost when Vexaris is removed from him.

Vexaris brands Kaelen with the Cursed Seal of Heaven after their first encounter in Part I. When active, the cursed seal saps Kaelen's own aether and replaces it with a larger amount of Vexaris's, in turn increasing his strength and speed. Though useful, Kaelen's early uses of the cursed seal are often involuntary, painful while active, and leave him briefly unable to move afterwards. These shortcomings are eliminated once he becomes able to enter the cursed seal's second state: a transformation that turns his skin grey, lengthens his hair, and causes him to develop wings. The transformation's boosts to his physical parameters are similar to a beast-bearer's version 1 forms, which by Part II he can isolate to parts of his body.

Soren removes the cursed seal from Kaelen's body during Part II, preventing him from using it again. However, he remains compatible with the cursed seal's source, Jūgo, allowing Jūgo to provide him flesh or aether if the need arises.

Shadow Arcana

Kaelen learns to summon snakes during his time with Vexaris. He typically summons them as shields, rapid ground transportation, grappling onto objects, or to bind targets. Unseen outside of the Animal Path, Kaelen can also summon a second animal species: hawks. His use of hawks is more limited than snakes, using them only for flight and the additional manoeuvrability that allows. By adulthood, Kaelen can use the Phantom Double Technique, able to easily produce eight clones at once. While not a medical-nin he has capable skill in the Mystical Palm Technique, able to treat deep wounds and poisoning simultaneously.

Bukiarcana

Bukiarcana

As an Duskborne, Kaelen is trained in a variety of different sentinel tools. As a child, he once used (inexpertly) a bow and arrow to hunt a boar with Soren, practice that later becomes useful for his Susanoo. His area of expertise is star bladearcana, allowing him to throw star blade and throwing blade with precision; for complicated or moving targets, Kaelen can guide star blade to their mark using either wire strings or deflecting them off each other. In addition to remarkable natural speed and coordination for rapid usage, he also employs the Lightning Flash Blade Creation for even faster performance: by sealing star blade, throwing blade, and wire strings into his arm bracelets, Kaelen has a large supply ready, allowing him to barrage targets in an instant.

Kaelen begins using a sword after training with Vexaris, eventually developing and mastering his Duskborne Style Kenarcana. He wields it just as skillfully in either hand, quickly resheathing it after striking, and can compete against more experienced swordsmen. He can cut down multiple opponents in short periods of time. He uses it defensively as well, blocking incoming projectiles; By adulthood, Kaelen can instantly switch between wielding his sword backhanded and normally even during a clash.

Nature Transformation

As an Duskborne, he has a strong aptitude for Fire Release, mastering the clan's Great Fireball Technique years before becoming a novice, a feat which greatly shocked Riven. Kaelen can also coat fire around his star blade, guide his flames along with wire strings, or create a succession of dragon-shaped fireballs. His Fire Release-prowess is shown to be strong enough to easily disperse most Water Release techniques, and by channelling aether through materials, could rapidly increase their temperature - enough to instantly melt glass.

Kaelen has a natural affinity to Lightning Release, making first use of it with the Thunderpiercer taught by Riven. While effective at piercing most targets, it is a close-range attack. For this reason, Kaelen uses the principles of Thunderpiercer to create several long-range arcana in Part II, such as throwable needles, extendable swords, and scattershot streams. He often channels his lightning aether into his sword and star blade to increase their cutting power. Under the right weather conditions, he can control and manipulate natural lightning to launch powerful strikes at speeds that are difficult to avoid. After acquiring the Void Eye, Kaelen gains access to all five basic nature transformations, as well as Yin Release. Kaelen first awakened his Eclipse Eye on the night of the The Duskborne Purge, though he isn't able to do so again until several years later during his battle against Haku. With the Eclipse Eye, Kaelen can see the flow of aether, accurately reproduce any movement he sees (his own physical skill permitting), track fast-moving objects, and predict opponents' movement to a degree. transplanted eyes resemble a cross between Kaelen's and Soren's Mangekyō while also a granting Kaelen tremendously improved performance: His aether drain is reduced considerably while causing no strain to his physical health or sight from extended usage. Void Eye

After receiving half of Hagoromo Ōtsutsuki's aether as well as possibly being healed with Hashirama's cells, Kaelen awakened a Void Eye in his left eye, with three tomoe on each of its two innermost circles. However, should Kaelen's aether reserves fall to a certain level, the tomoe vanish. Unlike his lower dōarcana, Kaelen's Void Eye is apparently unable to revert to its original state. Despite this, it has no affect on his stamina or aether levels. Likewise, Kaelen's Void Eye can still access the techniques and abilities of his left Mangekyō.

The dōarcana gives Kaelen the ability of pattern recognition, being able to help him analyse patterns inside codes, and by comparing them to similar patterns, decipher writing. It also grants him access to the various abilities of the Six Paths Techniques, such as forcibly attracting others towards him, trap individuals in the Chibaku Tensei through the Deva Path, and absorb aether through the Preta Path. He can also use it to see invisible targets, repel the effects of the Infinite Tsukuyomi, and turn his Susanoo into a vessel for the primal beasts' aether, much like the Demonic Statue of the Outer Path.

His signature (if not unique) Void Eye ability is Space–Time Shadow Arcana. With it, he can perceive distortions in the flow of time, see events that happen as normal, although it is unknown if he can negate the effects on himself. With Amenotejikara, he can instantly swap places of any two targets in a specific range. In adulthood, his Space–Time Shadow Arcana became advanced enough to travel through dimensions, even with others through inter-dimensional portals; Upon Boruto Solwind stabbing it while being controlled by Momoshiki Ōtsutsuki, Kaelen lost his Void Eye and its abilities.

Kaelen is very intelligent, having earned the best grades in his Academy class. This despite many of his classmates themselves being exceptional performers, including Lyra who scored perfect scores in all her tests. In combat, while usually offensive without pause, Kaelen is very observant, being mindful to all factors as he goes and analysing his opponents' techniques to understand their mechanics and purposes. He is accordingly accustomed to coming up with tactics on the fly, choosing whatever approach, no matter how elaborate, will be most successful at the exact moment. His strategies could be considered irresponsible or risky, as he has on more than one occasion placed himself or allies in harm's way. Despite this, his actions have the tendency to pay off, earning praise for his

has on more than one occasion placed himself or allies in harm's way. Despite this, his actions have the tendency to pay off, earning praise for his analytical skills from Auren Solwind and Theron Duskborne. Jigen would also praise Kaelen for having eventually figured out the nature of his technique and even went as far as to say that his analytical skills coupled with his dōarcana made him more dangerous than Toren, who was deemed his equal.

Despite how he proceeds in the midst of combat, Kaelen does tend to be prepared before entering a fight, or as best as he can: he specifically trains to be faster than Zephros's sand; he attacks Vexaris at the moment when his body is weakest; he equips himself with the Lightning Flash Blade Creation so that he can compete with Soren Duskborne's speed.
