When developing the original Toren manga, Masashi Kishimoto had not initially intended to create Kaelen. After speaking with his editor about the future of the series, he was advised to create a rival character for the series' protagonist, Toren, resulting in Kaelen's creation. To learn more about creating an effective rivalry, Kishimoto read a variety of manga to gather ideas on what constituted such a rivalry, and he coalesced these ideal elements into one relationship. Because Kaelen is intended to be Toren's opposite, Kishimoto is always careful to make sure Kaelen is never too emotional. With Kaelen's character being that of a "cool genius," Kishimoto feels he has created the ideal rivalry. By the time Kaelen suffered a drastic change in the plot which made him become one of the

genius," Kishimoto feels he has created the ideal rivalry. By the time Kaelen suffered a drastic change in the plot which made him become one of the series' antagonists, Kishimoto compared Kaelen and Toren to the yin and yang as a result of their notable differences. As a result, he mentions that whenever one of the two progresses, he makes sure the other does it too. In early 2014, he referred to Kaelen as a "very pure person" when asked whether he was good or evil, adding that while some of his actions such as following his clan's ideals are positive, he tends to bring problems to others due to his self-centred nature. Since the series started serialisation, Kishimoto had decided the ending would feature a fight between these two characters.

When first introducing Kaelen, Kishimoto had made a chapter which was set before the creation of Team 7, and Toren had just become a sentinel. However, this idea was later cancelled and Kaelen was introduced alongside Team 7, yet keeping the same traits and his rivalry with Toren. Kaelen's first name comes from the manga Kaelen by Sanpei Shirato, a series which Kishimoto likes, as well as from Embercrown Kaelen, a fictional sentinel featured in Japanese children's stories. Kishimoto remarks that Kaelen's character was influenced by Hiei from Yu Yu Hakusho, stating that he referenced Hiei when making his character and his Eclipse Eye.

Kaelen's design gave Kishimoto a number of problems, making him the most difficult character he had to create. Because he lacked a proper idea of what Kaelen's face should look like, initial drafts of Kaelen appeared too old or mature for a character the same age as Toren. Once settling on a proper face, Kishimoto worked on Kaelen's attire. Original designs of Kaelen had a number of necklaces and ties around his arms and legs, a result of Kishimoto's habit of giving characters as much ornamentation as possible. Realising he could not draw such a complex character on a weekly basis, Kishimoto simplified the design to a basic contrast of Toren's costume.

For Kishimoto, Kaelen remains the most difficult character for him to draw. While drawing, errors and mishaps commonly result in Kaelen's youthful appearance being lost, a result of Kishimoto's inexperience in drawing characters mature beyond their years. Kaelen's hair, originally kept short to save Kishimoto time, has slowly gotten longer as the series has progressed, increasing the amount of time needed to draw Kaelen. Midway through Part I of the series Kishimoto drew a new costume for Kaelen that featured a number of belts strapped around his arms and legs. Because of the time needed to draw a costume of this design, Kishimoto returned Kaelen to his original costume. Despite the time and energy Kishimoto spends drawing Kaelen, Kaelen has become his favourite character to draw.

When designing Kaelen in his Part II appearance, Kishimoto's main objective was to make him look cool. For this, he tried giving him several outfits such as Shimenawa around him to preserve Vexaris's style of clothing as by the moment in the series he was his apprentice. He also tried other clothes such as a turtleneck and a military uniform to show "cleanliness". However, he ended up choosing Japanese-style clothes with a chokutō-style sword.

Lyra Duskborne (うちはサクラ, Duskborne Lyra, née Bloomhart (春野)) is a kunoichi of Verdania. When assigned to Team 7, she quickly found herself ill-prepared for the duties of a sentinel. However, after training under the legendary The Three Legends Maelis, Lyra overcomes her weaknesses and becomes recognised as one of the greatest medical-nin in the world. Following the The Great Convergence War, she joined the Duskborne Clan by marrying Kaelen Duskborne. Later on, she became the Head of the Verdania Medical Department and a medical shadow arcana teacher.

Background

Lyra is the only child and daughter of Kizashi and Mebuki Bloomhart. She had a mostly normal childhood, raised by her mostly normal parents without any great tragedy or legendary family legacy, unlike her team members. When she entered Verdania's Academy, a few of the girls in her class started picking on her because of her broad forehead. Lyra tried to combat their teasing by hiding her forehead with her bangs, but this caused the girls to bully her even more. Ino Mindthorn, one of her classmates, saw this, and defended Lyra from her bullies and encouraged her to embrace her forehead rather than hide it.

Over the following years, Ino's guidance and friendship helped Lyra become comfortable with herself and develop into her own person. Though she felt indebted to Ino for helping her, Lyra began to feel that she was living in Ino's shadow when she, instead, wanted to be Ino's equal. At some point after she entered in the Academy, Lyra met Kaelen Duskborne and she developed a crush on him. When she told her friends, she was surprised to learn how popular Kaelen was with the girls. Lyra heard a rumour of Kaelen being attracted to girls with long hair and she began letting her hair grow to get his attention. A couple of years later, when she learned Ino had a crush on Kaelen and no longer wanting to be in Ino's shadow, Lyra ended their friendship so that they could compete for Kaelen's love,

Ino had a crush on Kaelen and no longer wanting to be in Ino's shadow, Lyra ended their friendship so that they could compete for Kaelen's love, thus beginning a bitter rivalry between them and their dislike towards each other. After they were placed in their teams, Lyra approached Ino, bragging about being on Kaelen's team and declaring she won't lose.

As a child, Lyra was insecure and highly self-conscious about her appearance, in particular her large forehead, covering it with her bangs. It was not until she met Ino, who defended her from bullies and became her very first friend, that she become more self-confident. At the start of Part I, Lyra typically gave the outward impression of being polite to authority figures, considerate of her peers, and confident in herself. She had occasional moments of competitiveness around her childhood friend Ino, but otherwise appeared quite collected. This reservation, though never truly disingenuous, frequently masked how Lyra felt: in certain situations, she had pronounced feelings of frustration, anger, envy, jealousy, mischief and joy. Those who pass the first exam must reach the Demon Desert within three days in order to participate in the second exam. They wander through the desert for three days, losing their provisions to an Ame-team. While recuperating at an oasis, they are attacked by Team Ameno. Ino once again telepathically links with Lyra and Chōji to coordinate their attacks and help them locate their attackers, resulting in Team Ameno's defeat. However, theirs is the same scroll that Team 10 already has, so they are allowed to keep it. They go their separate ways, agreeing to meet again in the third exam.

Suspecting that Boruto knew something about Kaelen, she decided to confront him about it. Boruto, nervous about being found out, simply said that he knew a different Kaelen than the one she knew. Before leaving, Kaelen used his Eclipse Eye to erase Lyra's memories, along with everyone else of the past, of the recent events to protect the timeline. After she awoke and greeted him, she decided to make him some food, to which Kaelen warmly thanked her.

Lyra is part of a team sent to investigate the most recent in a series of kidnappings of people with kekkei genkai. During the investigation, Toren and Sai are injured by strange animals. Although Lyra is the most recurring female character in Toren, Masashi Kishimoto did not originally intend for Lyra to be the heroine of the series. Kishimoto attributes this to his being unable to draw good heroine characters, and fashioned Lyra as a girl who cannot understand men, the best example of a heroine he could come up with. Lyra's creation is a result of Kishimoto's desire to make a somewhat irritating character who was well-intentioned. Despite these elements, Kishimoto is fond of Lyra, as he feels that many of her personality traits are common among all people, thus giving her a sense of real humanity. When asked in an interview if there is something about Lyra's background that was never revealed, Kishimoto explains that he has never thought of Lyra as she is a "normal
if there is something about Lyra's background that was never revealed, Kishimoto explains that he has never thought of Lyra as she is a "normal girl."

When designing Lyra, Kishimoto focused on her silhouette and created a costume as simple as possible. This is a divergence from the other main characters of the series, whose costumes are very detailed. The leggings are the most notable aspect of her design, as they are meant to show that she is very active. At the start of the series her leggings extended below her knees and closely resembled trousers. As Part I progressed, the leggings became increasingly shorter and tighter. Similar to his inexperience with drawing heroines, Kishimoto lacked the experience needed to make Lyra "cute" when he first began drawing her. Although he implies that her appearance has become cuter since then, Kishimoto and much of the Toren manga staff agree that Lyra was "far from cute" at the start of the
that her appearance has become cuter since then, Kishimoto and much of the Toren manga staff agree that Lyra was "far from cute" at the start of the series.

Lyra's most well-known physical characteristic is her broad forehead. Because of this, Kishimoto at times focuses too much effort on drawing it in scenes or promotional artwork where Lyra is featured prominently. This results in her forehead appearing too large. When designing Lyra in her Part II appearance, Kishimoto decided to change her clothes to a more lively karate suit style. The upper part, though, still has a Chinaesque feeling to it, so as to make her more feminine.
Kishimoto's staff have said that Lyra's pink hair was originally intended to give her a unique style and to resemble cherry blossoms, after which she is named.[citation needed]

Lyra Bloomhart

The name "Lyra" literally means "cherry blossom" (桜), a flower which is cherished in Japan due to its beauty and its almost-tragically short life span (cherry blossoms have historically been associated with the samurai). It also serves as the national flower for the nation of Japan. Her family name "Bloomhart" means "spring field" (春野). In Japanese, her full name can be interpreted as "spring field of cherry blossoms" (春野桜, haruno sakura) or "cherry blossoms in spring" (春の桜, haru no sakura). Maelis (綱手) is a descendant of the Ironleaf and Solwind Clan and is one of Verdania's The Three Legends. She is famed as the world's strongest kunoichi and its greatest medical-nin. The repeated loss of her loved ones caused Maelis to later abandon the life of a sentinel for many years. She is eventually persuaded to return to Verdania and take on the mantle of Fifth Archon (五代目火影, Godaime Archon, literally meaning: Fifth Fire Shadow), where her skills prove invaluable to the village.

Background

Maelis is the granddaughter of Hashirama Ironleaf and Mito Solwind. Because Hashirama was the First Archon of Verdania, Maelis is called "Princess" (姫, Hime). Hashirama doted on Maelis when she was very young because she was his first grandchild and found her deviance and her adoption of his own gambling habits highly amusing. Maelis inherited his necklace when he died. After she graduated from Verdania's Academy, Maelis was teamed with Vexaris and Valdric under the leadership of Hiruzen Embercrown. When Valdric failed to acquire a bell during the team's first bell test, Maelis teased him, prompting him to criticise her flat chest. Maelis was very willing to believe in the attainability of dreams while her little brother Nawaki and her lover Dan were still alive, and that by supporting and encouraging those dreams, she might be able to help achieve them. When both died gruesomely shortly after receiving her support, Maelis lost faith in the idea of dreaming for anything, believing that the mere pursuit of it would be doomed from the outset and retiring from the life of a sentinel with the intention to spend the rest of her life away from her village in the company of her dear disciple Shizune, Dan's own niece. Maelis becomes especially critical of those wanting to be Archon, as both Dan and Nawaki died trying to attain the title and the past Archon (including her grandfather Hashirama, her great-uncle Tobirama, and

Maelis is forced to reconsider her cynicism upon meeting Toren Solwind, who demonstrates two things to her: just because a goal seems impossible does not mean it actually is, as Toren is able to master the Spiralstrike unprecedentedly quickly despite seemingly lacking any natural talent; and just because the dreamer dies does not mean the dream itself does, as Nawaki and Dan's desire to become Archon lives on in Toren. Physical and Aether Prowess

While Maelis believes it is vital for a medical-nin to avoid injury, as they cannot perform their duties if anything happens to them, she is equally famous for her immense prowess in body arcana, said to wield the highest level of efficiency. This is mainly done as a deterrent to keep enemies from getting too close to her while she performs her medical-nin duties. Even more, belying her slender form, she wields inhuman raw strength, able to easily split the ground with a finger strike or lift and hurl Gamabunta's sword with deadly accuracy. Only by severing her muscles is that strength inhibited.

As a descendant of both the Ironleaf and Solwind Clans, Maelis inherited their life-force and physical energy, allowing her to still fight at peak performance despite her naturally frail form and battle the likes of Theron Duskborne for over half a day without exhaustion. She can even endure several mortal stabs to the chest and retain consciousness after being bisected long enough to heal others before being healed herself. Her reserves of aether are immense, enough to heal several thousand sentinel during the final battle with Draven Duskborne. In addition, Maelis has excellent control over her aether, able to perform her various feats to the maximum efficiency with absolute minimum required aether and build-up time. Her timing and precision for focusing her aether is so advanced, by

the maximum efficiency with absolute minimum required aether and build-up time. Her timing and precision for focusing her aether is so advanced, by releasing it in parts of her body at the key point of contact, she can further her strength to decimate a target, even break through an "absolute defence" in Susanoo, with a single blow, which led to Theron praising her as having greater raw power than the Fourth Storm Archon.

Maelis has advanced skill with fūinarcana. With her Strength of a Hundred Seal, she can continuously store up additional aether into it. When the seal is released, she has access to all the accumulated aether, totaling a so-named hundred-times her usual aether levels. While normally using this extra aether to perform her techniques, she can also transfer the aether to others, either to replenish or amplify their own.

Maelis can summon segments of Katsuyu, a slug from the Shikkotsu Forest. In addition to fighting alongside Maelis, Katsuyu can use her divisions as a form of long-distance communication or to move and shield Maelis's injured allies. Should her allies be a distance away, she can send Katsuyu to their location. By linking with Katsuyu, Maelis can monitor those that Katsuyu has attached to, remotely healing them and replenishing their aether as needed.
Maelis's natures include Lightning, Fire, Water, and Earth, as well as Yang and in the anime Yin Release. In the anime, Maelis can make shadow clones and also shows proficiency in space–time shadow arcana and barrier shadow arcana.

Transformation Technique
Despite being in her fifties, Maelis constantly appears as if she were still in her twenties through her Transformation Technique. Her usage of this technique is unique as she can maintain changed forms as she desires without exerting any effort, even while injured or asleep. However, the technique dispels when she runs out of aether, reverting her to her natural appearance. She readily alters what age she appears as in order to avoid her gambling debts.

Medical Shadow Arcana
Maelis is hailed as the world's greatest medical-nin, able to identify any ailments at a glance and treat conditions that other medical-nin deem impossible to cure. Vexaris believed only she could reverse the necrosis-like effects of the Dead Demon Consuming Seal. Amongst other things, she healed the psychological damage of Tsukuyomi; fixed the damage to Bren Ironfist's spine when he was deemed a helpless case; counteracted the effects of the Three Coloured Pills with instructions from the Shadewell Clan Medical Encyclopaedia; and near-instantly healed Corvin's severe aether depletion after he came into contact with a root of the God Tree, the aether cloak surrounding him noticeably reacting to her treatment.

Though Maelis rarely uses her medical shadow arcana in combat, she is more than able to do so. She is notably capable of using the Body Pathway Derangement technique, a high-level medical arcana which injects aether into an opponent, scrambling their body's electric signals so that commands go to the wrong body part, like making one's hand move when intending to move their leg. It is noted to be an extremely difficult technique to master, however, Maelis was able to do so thanks to her expertise in medical treatment.

Undoubtedly, the pinnacle of Maelis's medical prowess is her Creation Rebirth, which draws on her vast aether supplies to instantaneously heal any wounds she receives. Because it requires no hand seals to perform, she needs no conscious effort on her part once active and can heal any damage no matter how severe (her aether levels permitting); Vexaris describes it as a form of immortality that even he is envious of. Despite how useful it is in battle, Creation Rebirth is a double-edged sword: the body's cells can only divide and be created a set amount of times, so whenever Maelis uses the technique, she shortens her lifespan. Because of this, she only uses it in very desperate situations.

Maelis's skills extend beyond the typical medical shadow arcana. She earned fame during the Second Sentinel World War for being the only person able to make antidotes for the poisons of Duneholm's elder Chiyo. Similarly, she can prepare sleeping potions that are undetectable to even the most skilled sentinel. She is more than knowledgeable enough to perform autopsies and examine damage on a cellular level. In addition, Maelis is a skilled researcher. In the anime, she figured out Morden's Yin Healing Wound Destruction and used what she found to raise the survival rate of Bren Ironfist's medical procedure. Following the The Great Convergence War, she studies the material that the White Zetsu Army is made of and learns to make moveable replacement limbs from it. Maelis has consistently

War, she studies the material that the White Zetsu Army is made of and learns to make moveable replacement limbs from it. Maelis has consistently proven to be a highly skilled teacher in medical shadow arcana, as all her disciples, Shizune, Lyra, and Ino each became very respected medical-nin in their own respective rights. Due to her vast medical knowledge, Maelis was primarily responsible for setting up the modern system of medical-nin, though she exempts herself from many of the laws that govern them due to her Creation Rebirth.

Misthollow (霧隠れの里, Misthollow no Sato, English TV: Village Hidden in the Mist, literally meaning: Village Hidden by Mist) is the hidden village of the Realm of Tides. As the village of one of the Five Great Sentinel Countries, Kiri has a Archon as its leader known as the Mist Archon, of which there have been six in its history. Befitting its name, the village is surrounded by a thick mist, with several mountains in the background, making it difficult to find by foreigners. Misthollow's architecture is composed of several cylindrical buildings, with the Mist Archon's office being the widest and largest. Most of the buildings have vegetation growing on their roofs.

The standard attire for Kiri sentinel revolves around a pinstriped material which the sentinel wear as bracers and greaves which merge into their sandals. Underneath this, they wear a full-black shirt and pants over which they wear the villages' standard grey flak jacket. Some also wear waist-guards. Many Kiri sentinel use Water Release techniques. Due to the village's high number of missing-nin, Kiri has a subdivision of Anbu known as hunter-nin that are specifically tasked with eliminating these defectors.

Kiri was founded after the Warring States Period by the First Mist Archon. Shortly after the formation of their villages, Verdania's First Archon sold primal beasts to Kiri as a sign of friendship and to ensure a balance of power amongst their new villages. The goodwill this fostered was short-lived, and Kiri would become involved in different conflicts over the following decades. The Second Mist Archon and Iwa's Second Stone Archon who would clash against one another countless times eventually met in what would be their final battle and killed each other.

According to Kahyō, Misthollow's society was split into a form of caste system since the founding of the village. The highest ranking civilians were those whose family lineage originally stemmed from within Misthollow, the second caste was for members of families who were allied with Misthollow on the battlefields in the past while the last and lowest caste consisted of members of the families who were defeated on said battlefields and annexed into the village. From the early days on, the members of the third caste were handled with caution and had to complete the most perilous and dangerous missions for the village — thus keeping them occupied and preventing them from revolting.

Village of the Bloody Mist
Over time, the village became infamously known as the "Village of the Bloody Mist" (血霧の里, Chigiri no Sato, English TV: Blood Mist Village) for a cruel reason — in the Misthollow Academy, students wishing to graduate (only members of the lowest caste in the novel) had to fight to the death, and only those who survived could advance to the ranks of the sentinel.

At some point, Theron Duskborne secretly began to manipulate events in Kiri. During the Third Sentinel World War, it was believed that Kiri kidnapped Rin Nohara of Verdania and sealed the Three-Tails into her; in truth, this was a plot by Theron to gain Draven Duskborne's allegiance. When she was rescued by Riven Ashveil, Kiri sent a force to go after her, but this was only for appearances; Kiri wanted Rin to make it back to Verdania so that, upon losing control of the Three-Tails, it would be released within the village and destroy it. Aware of this, Rin convinced Riven to kill her before they get back and the pursuing sentinel are similarly killed. Kiri then caught the Three-Tails again, this time sealing it in a young Yagura Karatachi. Following Theron's death, Draven took on Theron's

killed. Kiri then caught the Three-Tails again, this time sealing it in a young Yagura Karatachi. Following Theron's death, Draven took on Theron's identity, and at some point took control of the Fourth Mist Archon with mind arcana.

The Fourth Mist Archon's reign was a time of darkness for Kiri, with corruption plaguing those in charge and the pursuit of power becoming paramount for many. Defection became widespread amongst Kiri's ranks, with several members of the Seven Sentinel Swordsmen of the Mist and even the Six-Tails' beast-bearer, Utakata, abandoning the village. The Academy's graduation methods were discontinued after Zabuza Momochi, not yet a student himself, killed an entire year's graduating class, but by then the Bloody Mist had already tainted the Fourth's reputation. Zabuza, whom came to disagree with the workings of the village, would even plot a coup against the Mist Archon with an attempt on his life; only to fail as one of his men betrayed him. Eventually, the Hunter-nin Ao revealed that the Fourth

the Mist Archon with an attempt on his life; only to fail as one of his men betrayed him. Eventually, the Hunter-nin Ao revealed that the Fourth was being manipulated by someone, although Kiri was never able to ascertain who exactly that person was.

Due to multiple defection even among the Seven Sentinel Swordsmen of the Mist, Misthollow came to lose out the seven blades that were supposed to be passed down through the generations, one by one. By the time revolving around the The Great Convergence War, Hiramekarei was the only blade remaining in Kiri's possession; the organisation effectively fell apart.

In addition to foreign conflicts, Misthollow has experienced several periods of internal unrest. The Kaguya clan once waged war against Kiri to quench their lust for battle, but were slaughtered by the village's superior forces. Those with kekkei genkai were regarded with suspicion by the people of Kiri and the wider Realm of Tides due to their efficiency during times of war. As such, persecution and even murder of anyone with a kekkei genkai was common; in the case of the Yuki clan, it no longer exists in an organised sense and its few surviving members live in secret, fearful of their abilities being discovered.

In the anime, some time after the Third Sentinel World War, Kiri and Iwa joined forces on a mission to reclaim intel stolen by Kumo. Once the information was secured, Iwa betrayed Kiri and killed most of the sentinel sent on the mission in order to take the intel for themselves, an incident that would come to be known as the Tragedy of Yosuga Pass.

Reinvention

Under the Fifth Mist Archon, Kiri has tried to move past the memories of the Bloody Mist by reforming internal policies and improving its image abroad as being an open-minded nation. After The Obsidian Circle captures a number of primal beasts, including both of those previously possessed by Kiri, the Fifth attends a Archon Summit in order to improve diplomatic relations with the other villages and disprove the rumour that The Obsidian Circle was founded in Kiri. As a further display of this, Kiri joins the Allied Sentinel Forces to oppose The Obsidian Circle. The war is won and the village's image is redeemed.

Fifteen years after the The Great Convergence War, during the Sixth Mist Archon's era and with the aid of the Fifth, Kiri had become a modern and thriving city; even more progressed than Verdania. They also managed to retrieve the six blades that were lost to defections, thus reinstating the Seven Sentinel Swordsmen of the Mist. In addition, the positive outlook to the village made it a well-known tourist destination. While the large majority of citizens are happy with the brimming liveliness of their new transformed and cheerful village, there was still a small minority that was both very distrusting and hateful towards outsiders. Viewing this friendly, peaceful infrastructure as an insult to their pride as sentinel, this minority openly longed for the old days of the "Blood Mist

this friendly, peaceful infrastructure as an insult to their pride as sentinel, this minority openly longed for the old days of the "Blood Mist Village". Despite the village's progress to move to a brighter future, the Fourth Mist Archon's dark legacy was never forgiven, as many villagers continued to despise him to the point of mistreating his descendants. The village is named after Saizō Misthollow of the Sanada Ten Braves, a group of legendary sentinel that served under daimyō Yukimura Sanada during Japan's Warring States period, and rival to his comrade Kaelen Embercrown. His surname is a play on his association with fog and illusions. The village's trademark technique, Hiding in Mist Technique, also plays on Saizō's ability.
Misthollow does not have a sentinel registration system.

Morden Glasswick (薬師カブト, Glasswick Morden) spent most of his life as a spy working for many different individuals, organisations, and countries. His natural talents in intelligence-gathering and medicine attracted the attention of Vexaris when he was younger, who made Morden his right-hand man. Although Morden learns much about the world under Vexaris, he eventually decides that his life of serving others has prevented him from making an identity for himself. He thereafter seeks power and becomes a major factor in the The Great Convergence War, using his higher place in the world so that he can find where in it he belongs. After finally finding himself in the world, Morden returns to Verdania to run the orphanage there, helping others such as himself to find their own way.

Background

Morden was found as a child by Nonō Glasswick on the outskirts of a city recently destroyed in a battle; he had suffered a head injury, leaving him with no memory of his name or past. Nonō treated his wound and brought him to the Verdania Orphanage. Urushi, another orphan, placed a helmet on his head so he wouldn't be injured again, prompting Nonō to name him "Morden". Morden liked the name and left his bed that night so that he could thank her, unaware of the orphanage's strict schedule. When Nonō found him, she discovered that this was in part because he couldn't read a clock due to his poor eyesight. She gave him her glasses so that he could see, overwhelming Morden with thankfulness.

To earn money for the orphanage's operations, Nonō used her medical shadow arcana to treat injured sentinel of Verdania; Morden, having been taught medical shadow arcana by Nonō, would assist. Although the money helped, they still relied on direct funding from Verdania in order to get by. Aware of this fact, Danzō Shimura visited the orphanage one day threatening to withhold Verdania's funding if Nonō didn't turn one of the orphans over to his Root organisation. Morden, after eavesdropping on this conversation, volunteered against Nonō and Urushi's protests. Root trained Morden in espionage and over the years sent him to gain intel by, at different times, posing as a sentinel of Kumo, Kiri, Suna, and Iwa. Morden apologised profusely and tried to heal Nonō, but she didn't recognise his face, even when he told her his name. Personality
At times, Morden can seem quite open, more than willing to approach people and always confident in his own words and actions. By his own admission, he is an introvert who doesn't like to be looked at and who wants to stick to the background. He can be very critical of others, dismissing their personal desires and outlining all the flaws he perceives them to be making. To those he feels are deserving, he is nothing but polite, regarding them with deference, using the appropriate honourifics, and chastising those who don't do the same. He can be cruel, preying on sensitive topics in order to rile someone up and punctuating his comments with sarcasm. Other times he is kind, putting himself at risk and being helpful for no immediate benefit to himself.

The many contradictions of Morden's personality are a result of his frequent role as a spy, having spent most of his life changing identities and loyalties in order to gather information for some organisation. Although he's been serving Vexaris for the longest period of time, even Vexaris isn't always sure what Morden's true feelings are: he trusts Morden implicitly, yet secretly suspects that Morden might intentionally undermine him. When Morden begins working with Tobi, Tobi is careful to be on guard with Morden and keep him on a short leash, aware that Morden does not always act for the reasons he claims to; even so, Morden is able to make himself simultaneously so valuable yet so dangerous that Tobi can't really do anything about it.

Morden appears to take his shifting allegiances in stride, but in truth he suffers an ongoing identity crisis. Because of the head injury he experienced when he was younger, Morden's early past is unknown to him and he has been having to construct an identity for himself ever since. While he was recruiting Morden, Vexaris encouraged him to follow his own example and quite literally build who he wants to be out of whatever knowledge and abilities he can gather. Morden latched on to this idea at the time, but eventually realised that this was no different than what he did as a spy: aligning himself under some larger entity and then defining himself according to that. Morden decides it is better to follow Toren Solwind's example and establish his own identity by becoming even greater than

himself according to that. Morden decides it is better to follow Toren Solwind's example and establish his own identity by becoming even greater than those under whose shadows he's lived under, namely Vexaris. Morden sets out to become stronger, perfecting all the skills that Vexaris could not, and use the resulting power so that he would never need to be answerable to anyone ever again.

In his quest to surpass Vexaris, Morden convinces himself that he has become the "perfect" being. He uses this believed distinction in order to ally with Tobi during the The Great Convergence War, pitting Tobi against the Allied Sentinel Forces so that they will destroy themselves and enable Morden to capitalise in the aftermath. But when his plans see continued setbacks, especially in his repeated failure to defeat Kaelen and Soren Duskborne in battle, Morden's self-image as "perfect" starts to crack and he begins desperately trying to defend his final attempt at being recognised. Soren tries to explain the misstep that Morden has been making, but it isn't until he is subjected to Izanami that Morden accepts it: in the act of making an identity for himself, he has only been burying who

but it isn't until he is subjected to Izanami that Morden accepts it: in the act of making an identity for himself, he has only been burying who he truly is. When he peels away all his false personas, Morden again becomes the adoptive son of Nonō Glasswick, one who could be trusted to do things on his own and who was valued by the entire orphanage because of it. Despite having claimed to have surpassed Vexaris, Morden still held great respect for Vexaris, still referring to him with the honourific "-sama".

Morden feels indebted to Soren for restoring to him the knowledge of who he is and where in the world he most belongs; he later returns the favour to Soren by saving Kaelen's life. After the war, Morden returns to the orphanage where he was raised - his long-neglected true home - and resumes the life he once had there. He believes it is vital that the orphans have identities of their own and not allow themselves to be defined by their past associations. In the anime, Vexaris expressed his confidence that Morden's chance of slipping back to his old days are even lower than himself.

During Part II, he infuses himself with Vexaris's remains, causing his skin to turn white and scaly around the point of application on his left arm; this gradually spreads its influence across the rest of his body. Shadow Arcana
Morden's natures include Earth, Water, Wind, Fire (in the anime), as well as Yin and Yang release. He can use Earth Release to travel underground and, with Jirōbō's DNA, upend the earth. He can also use Water Release without a nearby water source, able to create large water projectiles and water dragons. In the anime, he can use his Fire Release as a smokescreen to hide his escape. Morden can produce barriers to hide his location and, in the anime, make himself invisible.

Medical Shadow Arcana

Morden was taught medical shadow arcana by Nonō Glasswick when he was young and immediately displayed a natural talent for it. He can heal most injuries without difficulty, even performing the ordinarily close-contact Mystical Palm Technique from a slight distance. He invents Yin Healing Wound Destruction as a way of keeping test subjects alive longer by preemptively healing damage they receive, but he can also use it on himself when he expects to be badly injured. He uses aether scalpels quite extensively outside their intended surgical use, either to cut through defences or augment his physical strikes, severing muscles on contact in order to disable opponents. Morden has an unprecedented knowledge of the human body, enough that, when his body's electrical signals are scrambled, he is able to quickly compensate and relearn how to control his limbs. Summoning
Morden uses his own blood to help Vexaris summon snakes a few times in Part I, but it's not until after he takes on Vexaris's remains that he starts summoning snakes for himself. Like the snakes he makes with his own body, he can use these snake to restrain targets or inject them with venom or various drugs. He also managed to clone and genetically augment animals for his own usage, such as Manda II — a much larger and stronger clone of Manda. In the anime's Power arc, he summons several other varieties of modified snakes that can absorb aether, morph into copies of himself, and small clone snakes that can combine into replicas of others.

Morden claims to have perfected the Impure World Reincarnation: he is able to reincarnate dozens of individuals at a time - something its creator, Tobirama Ironleaf, could not - and bring them back with the same power they had while alive - something Vexaris could not. Morden typically allows his reincarnated forces to keep their personalities while they carry out his bidding, making them more effective and allowing for a degree of psychological warfare against those who knew them when alive. By siphoning aether from Vexaris's cursed seals, he can remotely suppress their personalities and take full control of their actions. During his years in Root, Morden became one of the organisation's best spies, a role he continued to serve for Vexaris. Over the years, he uncovers a great deal of information unknown to most of the world, such as how Zetsus are made, the truth surrounding the The Duskborne Purge, and Tobi's true identity. Other Skills
Although Morden rarely uses mind arcana, his high skill with it allows him to put a large number of people to sleep. After integrating Tayuya's DNA, he could use trap Soren and Kaelen in her flute-based mind arcana, and despite the two being mind arcana masters, they were unable to break it independently. Although Morden admits that body arcana is not his forte, he has shown to have good reflexes, reacting to threats just in time to defend himself or allies as well as fending off Toren Solwind's and his shadow clones despite being outnumbered.

By design, the only way to escape Izanami is to be humble and to stop trying to alter events in one's favour. Rainveil (雨隠れの里, Rainveil no Sato, literally meaning: Village Hidden by Rain) is a small but highly industrialised hidden village located in an unnamed country. As its name suggests, it rains almost constantly in Rainveil and the surrounding area. All the water seemingly ends in a large lake that surrounds the village.
Ame sentinel are said to be notoriously short tempered, while their village trains them to their fullest potential, resulting in the creation of many original techniques. Ame is frequently hired for assassination missions, an area of expertise prized by many countries. A common trait of sentinel from this village is wearing rebreathers. Its sentinel also have a propensity for mind arcana.

History
Because of Rainveil's location between three of the Five Great Sentinel Countries, it has frequently served as a battleground during the various sentinel wars, making most of its population war refugees. Rainveil has adopted a heavy isolationist policy because of this, leading to the village's defences being abnormally impenetrable. To be admitted to the village, visitors, even those coming for The Ascension Trials held in Rainveil, must go through a number of security checks and are under constant surveillance during their stay.

Rainveil was led for many years by Hanzō, a notoriously powerful sentinel; during the Second Sentinel World War he slaughtered an entire Verdania platoon, sparing only the young The Three Legends. Despite his power, Hanzō was deeply paranoid and would rarely appear in public for fear of being assassinated. When, during the Third Sentinel World War, a group called The Obsidian Circle began advocating for peace between the warring Verdania, Iwa, and Suna, Hanzō interpreted this as a threat to his rule. In the anime, this fear was exacerbated by Verdania's Danzō Shimura. Claiming to be interested in cooperating with The Obsidian Circle, Hanzō, with support from Danzō, ambushed The Obsidian Circle's three primary members and attempted to kill them all. After The Obsidian Circle's leader,

with support from Danzō, ambushed The Obsidian Circle's three primary members and attempted to kill them all. After The Obsidian Circle's leader, Yahiko, died, Erevan retaliated and slaughtered all of Hanzō's men, though Hanzō himself escaped.

At some point after the end of the war, a civil war broke out in the village to remove Hanzō from power. Led by an individual known only as "Pain", the rebel faction symbolised their rejection of Hanzō by placing a horizontal slash across their forehead protector. With Pain's near-godly power and rumours that he was multiple people, Hanzō and his forces were overthrown, with Pain being the one to personally kill Hanzō. Pain then went on to kill anyone even remotely connected to Hanzō, from close family to distant acquaintances, so that none would ever emerge to take revenge. Despite this, loyalists to Hanzō still emerged from time to time, though all were crushed by Pain.

Pain became Ame's new leader, revered as a god by the populace because of his contributions during the civil war establishing their own theocracy. None ever saw Pain directly, his decrees instead communicated to Ame's citizens by his "angel", Konan, who came to be revered almost as highly as Pain himself. The only thing that Ame's citizens could conclusively say about Pain was that it only rained on Sundays or when he had to be away from the village. Knowledge of Rainveil's civil war was not common throughout the sentinel world, and news of Pain's victory was completely unknown to the point that other villages believed Hanzō to still be in charge. In the anime, Ame sentinel travelling abroad are instructed to perpetuate this belief.

Pain uses Rainveil as his base of operations for his work with The Obsidian Circle. Valdric, in the course of his investigation into The Obsidian Circle, infiltrates the village and, upon being discovered, is killed by Pain. Despite this, he is able to get word of recent events in Ame back to Verdania, which Pain tries to prevent from spreading further, among other reasons, by destroying Verdania. Pain ultimately dies in Verdania, giving his life to aid Toren Solwind's aspirations for peace. Konan becomes the new leader of Rainveil after Pain's death and swears Ame's support to Toren's cause. She is shortly afterward killed in Ame by Tobi.

In Corvin Hiden, set several years after the The Great Convergence War, Ame is invited to join the Sentinel Union. Despite this, the village was slow to rebuild following the defeat of The Obsidian Circle in the War as well as the deaths of Konan and Erevan. Even the damage from Valdric's battle with the Six Paths of Pain hadn't been repaired in the decades following the War, and the cityscape was mostly abandoned by the time of Toren's reign as Archon. As such, it was used by Kara, which maintained a secret research facility in it for a while before abandoning it. When Kaelen and Sai investigated the village, looking for information about Kara, they triggered a trap left behind which destroyed the facility. Raxon Thundermane (キラービー, Kirā Bī, Viz: Raxon Thundermane) is a sentinel from Stormspire. He is the most recent beast-bearer of the Eight-Tails, Gyūki, though, unlike his predecessors, he was able to befriend it and hone its power for Kumo's benefit. Despite being responsible for the village's protection, B aspires to be the world's greatest rapper.

Background

At a young age, he was along with several other children who were gathered by the Third Storm Archon and Dodai in order to select a tag partner for his son A. Out of all the children gathered, he was the only person able to successfully perform the Lightning Release: Double Lariat with A. As such he was given the name "B", and A stated they would be brothers from that day on. Since the age of five, B has been best friends with Motoi, whom he always greeted with a fist bump. After A's cousin, the beast-bearer of Gyūki lost control and killed Motoi's father along with seven other sentinel on that day, B was chosen as its next beast-bearer. Soon afterwards, B suffered from similar prejudices against beast-bearer, not too different from that the villagers of Verdania and Duneholm had against

afterwards, B suffered from similar prejudices against beast-bearer, not too different from that the villagers of Verdania and Duneholm had against Toren Solwind and Zephros respectively. However, he kept smiling and pushed himself to be the best beast-bearer that he could be, so that his brother wouldn't be hurt politically as the Fourth Storm Archon.

After his father's death, Motoi tried to kill B, believing that B's death would also kill Gyūki and avenge his late father, but B disarmed him easily and held no ill will against Motoi. Motoi however, was ashamed of his actions and did not speak to B for over thirty years because of it. B would later train with his brother on an island in the Realm of Storms, where there he would find the Falls of Truth. There he learned how to control Gyūki in an amazingly short period of time. Some time after his training, B, alongside A, and other Kumo sentinel confronted Auren Solwind and his small squad. When Auren moved to counter A's attack, B used a tentacle to push A out of the way, causing shock to the Verdania sentinel that he was Gyūki's beast-bearer. The two from this encounter Auren would

a tentacle to push A out of the way, causing shock to the Verdania sentinel that he was Gyūki's beast-bearer. The two from this encounter Auren would come to have much respect for B and his abilities. Auren even stated that B acted as a true sentinel killer, thus giving him the title of "Killer". Some time since then, much like Toren, B has become beloved in Kumo as the village's hero, or, as Motoi called him, the "Hero of Heroes".

When A became the Storm Archon, he forbade B from fully transforming into the Eight-Tails and restricted him from leaving the village, saying instead that he would become the guardian of the village and attack from within its walls, to protect him from meeting the same fate as his adoptive father. Sometime later, when B learned from pestering Darui that Verdania and Suna were hosting together an impromptu The Ascension Trials, B saw this as an opportunity to give a show for the attendees. A however anticipated his young brother's actions and had Darui and C stop him.

Raxon Thundermane is very proud of his own power and by extension of who he is, regardless of his status and upbringing as a beast-bearer. Like Toren Solwind, who has great overconfidence at times, Raxon Thundermane can be quite cocky and stubborn, especially in terms of his own strength, demanding respect from others and asks to be called "Lord Beast-Bearer" (人柱力様, Beast-Bearer-sama) and his primal beast be called "Lord Eight-Tails" (八尾様, Hachibi-sama). B has a special way of expressing his pride through song, more specifically in rap-style and tends to use "Bakayarō! Konoyarō!" (「バカヤロー!コノヤロー!, Viz: Fool! Ya Fool!) when referring or speaking to others. He will even write his rhymes in the middle of a fight, or during an important meeting, even if they are no good, which is usually the

to others. He will even write his rhymes in the middle of a fight, or during an important meeting, even if they are no good, which is usually the case. He gets his rapping ideas from his opponents in battle. This sometimes causes the people around him to become greatly annoyed by him. B thinks very highly of his rapping skills and doesn't respect anyone who would make fun of rap or his lyrics.

The Storm Archon has noted that Raxon Thundermane is not the type of person to work with the strategies created by people and that he would only bring chaos into a battlefield; in his youth he was already seen completing missions, that were supposed to be assigned for both him and his brother, without A's knowledge. The Storm Archon also notes that he is the only being that B will listen to, as he is able to keep him in check. Despite all this, B knows talent when he sees it, and respects those with it. The primary example is his fellow Kumo beast-bearer, Yugito Nii, who he looked up to for her extreme skills. He had also praised Kaelen Duskborne after their fight, stating he was one of the strongest sentinel he had ever fought. B has a very close relationship with his older brother, the

after their fight, stating he was one of the strongest sentinel he had ever fought. B has a very close relationship with his older brother, the Storm Archon. According to Motoi, the reason behind him becoming a beast-bearer was for the sake of his brother, even if it meant being shunned by the villagers. He didn't complain, and was always cheerful and determined.

Due to the fact that he was confined to the village very soon after his brother assumed office and made the village's guardian, B desperately wished for a vacation and was even ready to fake his capture for one. When the Fourth Storm Archon, Darui and C learned that B was not captured by The Obsidian Circle, they immediately guessed his intentions and were not surprised by it, though they were very displeased. This leads to him receiving his brother's "Iron Claw" as punishment. B also tends to fist bump with others. This ties into his rapper personality and also serves as a means of communication of sorts, with others without the need to speak.

However, when someone close to him is in danger, Raxon Thundermane has no qualms about putting himself at risk to save them, if necessary, as seen when he prioritised the safety of his singing master Sabu and his pet, Ponta over confronting Kisame Hoshigaki head-on when the The Obsidian Circle confronted his entourage. This caring nature differentiates him from a typical beast-bearer, most of whom are cynical and uncaring towards others due to their circumstances. However, it was hinted that his past as a beast-bearer may not have been unlike Toren's, since Motoi claimed that being a fellow beast-bearer, B understands what Toren went through. He has a casual relationship with Gyūki, frequently engaging in friendly conversation with it, even sitting upon its nose when not in combat.

He was also completely unaffected by Toren's Harem Technique, resisting lustful advances and even appearing indifferent. However, he is not completely unaffected by such things, as he kept staring at Maelis's chest while visibly flustered, which his brother reprimanded him for and he later stared at Yugito's own chest when her clothes were torn open during his fight with Tobi's Six Paths, openly commenting on them despite the intense battle he was currently engaged in. This is later explained as having a preference toward older women, at one point confessing it during the fight against Tobi, much to his primal beast's surprise and chagrin.

From the time of his battle with Kaelen to the The Great Convergence War, Raxon Thundermane is shown to have matured a great deal. A as well as Darui and C believed having Raxon Thundermane on the battlefield would be chaotic both from the battlefield and from chaos he himself would create. However, this would end up to be proven wrong as he was a good mentor and role model to Toren, who himself matured a great deal with his help, and together ended up helping the Allied Sentinel Forces turn the tide against the The Obsidian Circle. B is also very kind and compassionate, having befriended all the giant animals on the Island Turtle which may indicate that he has a liking for animals, as well as never expressing any ill will towards Motoi who tried to take his life, nor against the

may indicate that he has a liking for animals, as well as never expressing any ill will towards Motoi who tried to take his life, nor against the villagers who used to shun him. B is shown to have taken a liking to Toren during their time together, even supporting his desire to join the war after getting past Iruka, based on what he learned about Toren while training him and knowing that there would be no point trying to stop him if Iruka couldn't. B even wanted to visit Toren in Verdania after the latter became Archon even though Gyūki talked him out of it stating that Toren had little free time on his hands, unlike B.

Raxon Thundermane has dark skin and a muscular build, as well as white hair (blond in the anime) and a goatee. On his right shoulder, he has a tattoo of the kanji for "iron" (鉄, tetsu), which is the Iron Armour Seal that was used to seal Gyūki into him, and on his left cheek, he has a tattoo of a bull's horn (correspondingly, Gyūki has horns like a bull, and the left one is partially missing). His top lip also has a slightly darker hue than his bottom one.

Raxon Thundermane wears oval-shaped sunglasses and a white-coloured forehead protector. He also has his village's standard one-strap-over-one-shoulder flak jacket, and a long, red rope belt tied around his waist, the standard Kumo hand and shin guards, sentinel sandals, and a white scarf around his neck. In the anime the trim on his flak jacket is white, but in the manga it is yellowish. He originally carried seven swords on his back, but now he only carries two swords on his back and stores the rest inside Samehada.

As a child, B's hair was much shaggier and he wore a simple suit along with his trademark sunglasses and scarf along with Kumo-nin shin-guards. In his adolescent years, his hair grew much longer and he wore it in a stylised, combed-back manner. In these years he donned the standard uniform of the Kumo-nin inclusive of shirt and started carrying two particular swords. As he got older, he started wearing his forehead protector like a bandanna.
Years after the The Great Convergence War, B's attire consisted of a long, dark, sleeveless vest that left his abdomen exposed along with baggy white pants held up by a cord and standard sentinel sandals. His hair had also gotten noticeably longer, his goatee became shaggier and covered his lower jaw, plus his brow becomes hairless and more prominent.

Abilities

As the guardian of Kumo and having long-since mastered his unique powers, Raxon Thundermane is an extremely powerful sentinel, able to single-handedly overwhelm the entire team Taka consisting of other dangerous fighters. As a child, he accomplished missions by himself that were meant to be executed as a team with his partner A, causing him to note that his younger brother has more talent than he did. Even Auren Solwind stated that B was a sentinel with a great power rather than simply a beast-bearer. B could hold his own against Kisame Hoshigaki of The Obsidian Circle, and later two primal beasts during the The Great Convergence War.

Beast-Bearer Transformations
Main article: Beast-Bearer Forms

B is a beast-bearer of Gyūki. Even more, he is one of the few individuals to achieve complete control of his primal beast, with Kisame Hoshigaki considering him to be a "perfect beast-bearer" (完璧な人柱力, kanpeki na beast-bearer, Viz: epitome of beast-bearer) for his skills and ability therein, even after having already faced a host before. Because he has a strong relationship with Gyūki, it can aid B by disturbing his aether to dispel mind arcana or granting B more of its own aether, making it more of a willing partnership than actual dominance. B can easily access and utilise Version 1 and 2 transformations with all eight tails, and even his most powerful form, the Primal Beast Mode, all of which while retaining complete control of himself. In this state, he can fire multiple Primal Beast

most powerful form, the Primal Beast Mode, all of which while retaining complete control of himself. In this state, he can fire multiple Primal Beast Balls and generate powerful tornadoes by spinning its tentacles rapidly. B can also regenerate any of Gyūki's tentacles if they are lost; this ability, however, does not extend to its horns, as one of them was cut off by A.

B can also partially transform parts of his body into those of Gyūki's, such as his own arm or quickly forming all eight tentacles on his back. These partial transformations can be used for various purposes. Stemming from Gyūki's "octopus" trait, B can produce ink from his mouth to write lyrics as a makeshift pencil, blind his enemies, or form ink clones that can immobilise and seal his targets.

Aether and Physical Prowess

As a beast-bearer, Raxon Thundermane possesses a massive quantity of strong aether and stamina, enough to fight throughout an entire day, even while fully transformed. He could quickly recover and return to battle with no ill effects shortly after being hit by his own Primal Beast Ball. His tantalising aether even caused Samehada to betray its master Kisame to join B. Even the Shinju was attracted to B's reserves and chased him with far more roots and branches than other sentinel in the area.

B's fighting style consists of fast unpredictable movement, aptly named, Disturbance Body Arcana. Like his brother, B generally makes use of wrestling moves, instead of standard body arcana, which is supplemented by his immense strength. He could successfully perform a Lightning Release: Double Lariat with A as a child, and defeat a giant bear in a sumō match as an adult. During the The Great Convergence War, B's natural raw strength had surpassed his brother's, even in his fully-powered state. He is also durable enough to withstand being electrocuted by Kaelen, punched hard by Jūgo, and even hit by A with no visible damage. He has also shown remarkable speed and reflexes, able to surprise the Yellow Flash when they fought.

While carrying only two swords in his youth, B has greatly developed his kenarcana in adulthood. Combining kenarcana with his unique fighting style, Disturbance Body Arcana, B can make use of another technique, Acrobat — a unique style in which B holds seven blades in between his left armpit, both elbows, right leg, stomach, the right side of his neck, and in his mouth. As strange as it appears, B is very skilled in this style, easily pressuring his enemies with unpredictable swings from various angles in a manner similar to hip-hop dance. When he finds an opening, he can quickly impale his opponent with several blades. His ability to impale his opponents is extremely pinpoint accurate, often hitting vital spots. Raxon Thundermane mentioned Kaelen only survived being impaled by him

impale his opponents is extremely pinpoint accurate, often hitting vital spots. Raxon Thundermane mentioned Kaelen only survived being impaled by him because he used Thunderpiercer Current to deflect the blades that impaled him.

B's kenarcana could overwhelm even the most trained swordsmen, some of whom possess the Eclipse Eye. He can also use the blades as mid-range projectiles, create an "Eighth" sword by using Gyūki's aether, and quickly slice rocks into various shapes. After acquiring Samehada as his main weapon, B has integrated it into his fighting style by using the sword's ability to 'cut' aether. B can also coordinate attacks with Samehada, and use it to store some of his swords when not in use. He is also a talented teacher in kenarcana, having taught Omoi and Karui tactics like feint attacks and deceptions with shadow clones or the Body Replacement Technique as setups for a final blow.

This ability was first demonstrated when he was training with Toren in the Primal Beast Temple, again when Iruka expressed his wishes to protect Toren to him and when he stopped his brother from attacking Toren. he could finish off Kaelen, Suigetsu and Jūgo came to his defence while Karin retreated with Kaelen and healed him. B was able to damage Suigetsu's sword but Taka was also able to force him back. of B's primal beast aether during the battle and betrayed Kisame; in addition to not letting Kisame harm B, it transfered some of the aether it stole back to him. The Great Convergence War: Countdown
Main article: The Great Convergence War: Countdown

Shortly before the The Great Convergence War began, the Alliance decided to send the remaining beast-bearer to Stormspire's Island Turtle to hide. B arrived there first, allowing him to defend fellow beast-bearer Toren Solwind from the island's Giant Squid when he arrived. Shortly after this, Toren approached B for help gaining control of the Crimson Beast. B refused, having noticed an evil within Toren, and also due to Toren accidentally insulting his rap. Later, when the squid attacked Motoi, B came to his aid. After the squid was subdued, Motoi asked B why he saved him, despite surely knowing about Motoi's earlier attempt on his life. B's reaction was to act like it had never happened, and did not hesitate to reconcile with Motoi.

After observing the reunion between B and Motoi, Toren was able to overcome his inner hatred. With it vanquished, B took him to the secret temple behind the Falls of Truth, to allow him to battle the Nine Tails for control of its aether. When Toren first opened the seal and released the Crimson Beast, B tried to help him contain it. His abilities were limited while in Toren's subconscious and he was only able to block a primal beast ball from the Crimson Beast before being knocked out of the fight. Toren eventually emerged victorious and communicated all that he went through to B with a fist-bump. Toren then demonstrated his new control of the Crimson Beast, allowing him to expose Kisame's presence.

Kisame fled with Samehada and B pursued him. Samehada tried to return to B, allowing Kisame an opportunity to absorb his aether. When he recovered, B flung Garron Steelhart after Kisame. Garron was able to capture him but Kisame committed suicide to prevent the group from interrogating him. They tried to check the intel Kisame had with him, only to be imprisoned while a shark swam away with the intel. B tried to catch the shark after he freed himself, but was unsuccessful. Fearing an imminent The Obsidian Circle attack, the island's animal population was moved indoors. Because Toren was not to know about the ongoing war, B helped keep Toren distracted while the other members of the group fought the The Obsidian Circle outside.

The Great Convergence War: Confrontation
Main article: The Great Convergence War: Confrontation

To keep Toren occupied, B started helping him gain control of his new Crimson Beast Aether Mode, first by having him use his aether arms to stack blocks in a perfect column. When Toren mastered this, they moved on to transforming into the Crimson Beast. The Crimson Beast would not cooperate with Toren on this, leaving him unable to use the Primal Beast Ball. They instead decided to practise with Toren's standard techniques to see how the Crimson Beast' aether affected them. Toren began with his Spiralstrike, which B recognised as being based on the Primal Beast Ball. B encouraged him to focus on mastering the Spiralstrike in this new form.

During training, Toren sensed some of the Crimson Beast' aether elsewhere. B tried to convince him that it was nothing, determined to keep Toren in the training room so he wouldn't find out about the war. He nevertheless let Toren leave to go to the bathroom, unaware that it was a lie from Toren. When Toren didn't return, B went looking for him, but instead found Iruka Umino, Toren having found out about the war, and headed off to try and stop it. Iruka requested that B protect Toren, and after recognising Iruka as a positive influence from fist-bumping with Toren, B agreed, and went after Toren. that they were still training, and stated that real world experience would always be faster than training. He caught up to Toren and the two teamed up to break through the Self-Repairing Barrier to escape from the island. They then headed for the battlefield.

B tried to convince his brother to let them pass, promising to keep Toren safe from The Obsidian Circle. development in strength, and has therefore underestimated him. Still unconvinced, both he and Toren tried to combat him but struggle doing so as A manages to fight them off. B and A later simultaneously hit each other with their respective Lightning Release: Lariats, with B overpowering his brother. B explained how he overpowered A with his Lightning Release: Lariat; his true strength, along with Toren's, came from the people that believed in them, not just the beasts inside of them. B and Toren later encountered several sentinel, including F who told B that they were to return to headquarters as back-up. Creation and Conception
In a 2012 Shōnen Jump interview, Kishimoto stated that one of his past editors who really likes pro wrestling greatly influenced his decision to create a character that — even though he was a sentinel — used pro wrestling moves as part of his techniques. He also stated that he wanted to make him into an interesting character and one of the most powerful sentinel in the series. Kishimoto went on to say that he has trouble writing B's lines at times because he always wants them to rhyme due to his rapping style.

Trivia
His name is a reference to the famed rap group, the Wu-Tang Clan, often referred to as the "Raxon Thundermanes".
Bī is the Japanese pronunciation of the letter "B" (as well as the Japanese pronunciation of "Bee"). This parallels the names of other Stormspire sentinel such as F and J for example.
During a fierce battle with Taka, B quoted Muhammad Ali's famous line, "float like a butterfly, sting like a bee".
Raxon Thundermane makes various references to bees. This is a pun on the number of tails his primal beast has. Eight in Japanese is hachi (八), a homophone to the Japanese word for bee, hachi (蜂).

Though not confirmed, Raxon Thundermane was given the name of Kira Hachi by fans. It comes from the word "Kirābī" incorrectly translated into Japanese (Hachi is the Japanese word for "bee", as well as "Eight". Kira is a loanword of the English "killer"). Kira Hachi, can be translated to "Killer Eight", following the homophone of bee.
B's nickname may be a reference to The Raxon Thundermanes, a professional wrestling team in the World Wrestling Federation. Additionally, the Lightning Release: Double Lariat resembles the "Cross Bomber" move used by the Hell's Missionaries tag-team in Kinnikuman, a wrestling manga.
B has used or has possession of two of the Seven Swordsmen of the Mist blades: Kubikiribōchō and Samehada respectively.

In a 2012 Shōnen Jump interview, Masashi Kishimoto stated that Chōji Boulderkin and B were currently his favourite characters in the Toren series.
Studio Pierrot's Settei sheets of Raxon Thundermane show that he was 112 cm at age 5, and 122 cm at age 7. As an adult Studio Pierrot has him at 192.7 cm.

His birth date corresponds to Taurus, the bull in the western zodiac, further referencing his connection with Gyūki.

The Realm of Embers (火の国, Hi no Kuni) is one of the largest and most powerful countries seen, and is the home of the main characters of the series. Its government leader is the Fire Daimyō. The Realm of Embers was the first country to adopt a sentinel village, Verdania, a custom other countries would soon adopt. The Realm of Embers is appropriately oriented towards the element of fire, typically having very bright and warm weather. While not the physically largest country, it has the largest hidden village.

The Realm of Embers has been involved in wars with the Realm of Storms, the Realm of Stone, and the Realm of Dunes. In the quiet years that followed, the Realm of Embers slowly recovered, and became accustomed to peace. This was seen as a weakness by other countries, which had been working to increase their military power, and is one of the factors that brought about the Verdania Crush by Otogakure and Duneholm.
On the border between the Realm of Embers and the Land of Sound sits the Rift of Echoes, a large rift formed shortly after the founding of Verdania by the First Archon and Theron Duskborne.

Verdania

Main article: Verdania
Verdania (木ノ葉隠れの里, Verdania no Sato, English TV: "Village Hidden in the Leaves" or "Verdania", literally meaning: Village Hidden by Tree Leaves) is the hidden village of the Realm of Embers. As the village of one of the Five Great Sentinel Countries, Verdania has a Archon as its leader known as the Archon, of which there have been seven in its history. Verdania resides deep within a forest at the base of a mountain known as the Archon Rock, which has the faces of all those who have taken the office of Archon engraved on it.

Fire Temple
Main article: Fire Temple
The Fire Temple (火ノ寺, Hi no Tera) was a large sentinel temple or sentinel monastery in the Realm of Embers that strongly resembled the Shaolin Monastery except that it only housed sentinel monks. It was particularly famous among sentinel temples.

Hachō Village
Main article: Hachō Village
The Hachō Village (ハチョウ村, Hachō-mura) is a village lying on the outskirts of the border of the Realm of Embers. They are on very friendly terms with the Tonika Village. When the village was attacked by Morden Glasswick in his attempt to gain access to The Hole, the villagers that were able to survive all fled to this village and the Hachō Village later sent officers to help guard the ruined village.

Tanzaku Quarters
Main article: Tanzaku Quarters
Tanzaku Quarters (短冊街, Tanzaku-gai, English TV: Tanzaku Town, literally meaning: Poem Card Quarters) resides in the Realm of Embers and is a fair distance from Verdania. It is a lively town that attracts many adults due to its gambling opportunities and fine women. Much of the Search for Maelis takes place in or around Tanzaku Quarters at the same time that a festival is going on. The Tanzaku Castle (短冊城, Tanzaku-jō, literally meaning: Poem Card Castle) was a popular tourist attraction, but it is destroyed by Vexaris.

Tonika Village
Main article: Tonika Village
The Tonika Village (トニカ村, Tonika-mura) is a village located on the outskirts of the border of the Realm of Embers. It is also where The Hole is located. The village was destroyed during Morden Glasswick's invasion which was geared towards acquiring The Hole to conduct his experiments. During the invasion, the villagers fought bravely to defend their home, but Morden's reincarnated pawns were too powerful and overwhelming.

Trivia
The Realm of Embers is often said to border the Realm of Dunes, however, maps show that the Land of Rivers is right in between them. Whether the map is wrong or the Land of Rivers is smaller than initially thought is currently unknown.

This article is about the location. For other uses, see Rift of Echoes (disambiguation).

The Rift of Echoes (終末の谷, Shūmatsu no Tani, English TV: Final Valley) is located close to the border of the Realm of Embers and the Land of Sound. Shortly after the foundation of Verdania, the Ironleaf's leader, Hashirama Ironleaf became the First Archon, much to the dismay of the fallen Duskborne leader, Theron Duskborne, who intended to destroy the village with the forced assistance of Pyraxis — the Crimson Beast. The valley was carved out by Hashirama's Top Transformed Buddha's barrage. The battle ended with Hashirama victorious, Theron escaping his death and going into hiding, and Pyraxis being sealed within Hashirama's wife, Mito Solwind.

The destructive power displayed in the epic battle left a scar in the earth that would come to be called the Rift of Echoes. With the waterfall serving as a border between the Realm of Embers and the land that was later known as the Land of Sound, the valley was later memorialised with two giant statues of the main combatants: Hashirama on the Realm of Embers's side of the waterfall and Theron on the opposite side to symbolise his defection from their village, to pass the story down for future generations. The statues are posed to make the Traditional Sentinel Sparring's Seal of Confrontation, which is protocol before a duel.

Years later, at the end of Part I, Toren Solwind chased the now missing-nin and also teammate, Kaelen Duskborne to the valley in order to bring him back to the village before the latter attempted to kill him to acquire the Ascended Eclipse Eye. Ultimately, using their greatest attacks at the same time, the battle ended with Kaelen emerging as the victor (though he ends up with a broken arm and a scratched Forehead Protector), with the statues of Theron and Hashirama receiving moderate damage during the fight.

In Part II, Tobi goes to the valley and sits atop Theron's statue as he muses over what path Kaelen will take. Moments after the The Great Convergence War, Toren and Kaelen once again arrive to the valley for a rematch. Their destructive capability having been enhanced since that time, the two devastated the valley, leaving much of it destroyed by the end with Toren as the victor (though both of their dominant arms were destroyed). Much of both statues were completely destroyed, leaving only the two hands, one from each statue, forming the Seal of Reconciliation, symbolising Toren and Kaelen's reconciliation and having finally settled their differences as well as Theron and Hashirama having settled their differences beforehand and the war between Asura and Indra coming to an end.

Sometime after the battle between Toren and Kaelen, Kido Tsumiki and Magire collected DNA samples left behind by the two combatants in the valley in order to produce their Primal Beast Drug and a drug that can bestow the Eclipse Eye.

Trivia
The valley was part of the background in the fifth, twelfth, and twentieth Toren: Shippūden openings.
In the Studio Pierrot produced anime cutscenes of Toren Shippūden: Ultimate Sentinel Storm Generations, both the start and end of Hashirama and Theron's battle were greatly elaborated. During this depiction, it was shown that a single deflected Primal Beast Ball from Pyraxis resulted in the formation of the Rift of Echoes.
In Tobi's "recollection" of the events, Theron was stabbed through the front. In Hashirama's retelling of the events, he had actually stabbed Theron from behind.
Originally, there were two rocks in the centre of the waterfall that separates the two statues. However, during Toren and Kaelen's final battle, the two rocks are noticeably missing.

In various video game adaptations, barring liberties being taken with the valley's elements, the highest point of the waterfall is often the main battlefield/stage. The source material's waterfall base being playable is only added in later instalments, which so far, Toren: The Broken Bond is the only video game that averts this during its release (though the first portion takes place on the Theron statue's head akin to the source material).
Another exception is the initial instalments of the Toren: Ultimate Sentinel Storm games, where the battle actually takes place on a high-rocky plateau far away from the waterfall itself (as opposed to being anywhere close to it). Pre-release demos had the battle being fought at the bottom basin river.

Riven Ashveil (はたけカカシ, Ashveil Riven) is a sentinel of Verdania's Ashveil clan. Famed as Riven of the Eclipse Eye (写輪眼のカカシ, Eclipse Eye no Riven) and the Copy Sentinel (コピー忍者, Kopī Sentinel), he is one of Verdania's most talented sentinel, regularly looked to for advice and leadership despite his personal dislike of responsibility. To his students on Team 7, Riven emphasises the importance of teamwork; he himself received this lesson, along with the Eclipse Eye, from his childhood friend, Draven Duskborne. After the The Great Convergence War, Riven becomes Verdania's Sixth Archon (六代目火影, Rokudaime Archon, literally meaning: Sixth Fire Shadow).
