Personality

Riven has been very independent, perceptive, and self-confident since early childhood, and tends to broach difficult conversations with blunt pragmatism. He carries himself with a relaxed, almost bored disposition and is known for being solitary and aloof, with an occasional tendency to ignore his peers. These qualities lead some to perceive him as arrogant or condescending; however, Riven is truthfully quite modest about himself, even in the face of his growing reputation as a sentinel and leader. He is also habitually tardy, showing up at his leisure with excuses that convince nobody, and later leaving for equally poor reasons. Though Riven wants others to believe this is how he always acts, he only does so for matters that aren't of particular importance. In his role as Archon, Riven

wants others to believe this is how he always acts, he only does so for matters that aren't of particular importance. In his role as Archon, Riven dutifully worked for the village's progress. He also believes that even in times of peace, no one should become a sentinel without appreciating the importance of it.

Riven's life was shaped by the death of his childhood squadmates. He spends hours of his free time visiting Rin's grave and the Memorial Stone where Draven's name is engraved, telling them about his life, recent events in Verdania, and others they knew. Most of all, he shares his regrets that they cannot be with him and that their deaths were his fault. In the anime, after Rin died, Riven struggled to cope with post-traumatic stress disorder, having nightmares about her death and growing depressed whenever others mentioned her. Over time, Riven comes to accept that her choice to sacrifice herself and his guilt became more about his broken promise to Draven to keep her safe. This causes Draven's apparent death to weigh more heavily on him, compounded by regrets about his behaviour when

promise to Draven to keep her safe. This causes Draven's apparent death to weigh more heavily on him, compounded by regrets about his behaviour when they last spoke. Riven feels that, had he cared about teamwork and friendship in the same way that Draven did, Draven's "death" might have been avoided. Thinking it would ease his pain, Auren convinced Riven to join the Anbu. During his time in the Anbu however, Riven gained a reputation for his cold-bloodedness. Kurenai Yūhi noted that Riven suffered with suicidal thoughts during his Anbu career, with his reckless fighting style and lack of self-care being deemed as Riven being in a hurry to die.

After his father's death, Riven initially became stern and cold toward others, chastising any who disobeyed orders and being willing to abandon his comrades to finish missions. However, Draven's apparent death profoundly changed him; he became committed to teamwork and always places teammates' well-being above the mission's. He believes goals can be accomplished more effectively together, asking for help when he needs it, providing help when it is requested of him, and praising allies when they deserve it. An abuse of one's teammates is the only thing that can make Riven cast aside his normally stoic demeanour, causing him to attack without mercy or his usual sense of sportsmanship. Abilities

Riven is one of the strongest sentinel Verdania ever produced, with his advanced skills earning him the title of a genius (天才, tensei). A prodigy of such innate talent and intellect, he showcased highly advanced skill from a young age and even performed official missions while still in the Academy. From which, he rapidly rose through the sentinel ranks. His prowess is said to rival an entire country, something that earned him recognition on sight by various high-level sentinel. The S-Rank members of The Obsidian Circle acknowledge his might; he outmaneuvered Soren Duskborne (albeit he couldn't use his Ascended Eclipse Eye at the time), fought Kisame Hoshigaki and Kakuzu to a standstill, and was deemed a major threat by Pain. He even fought on par with the adult Draven Duskborne, whose
Kisame Hoshigaki and Kakuzu to a standstill, and was deemed a major threat by Pain. He even fought on par with the adult Draven Duskborne, whose prowess was comparable to Theron Duskborne.

Riven is very versatile with advanced proficiency in countless areas including mastery of all three main sentinel skills; noted as smarter than Corvin Shadewell, having a better sense of smell than Kiba Fangcrest, more adept with the Eclipse Eye than Kaelen Duskborne, and more skilled in body arcana than Bren Ironfist—even as each of them are well-known for their high capacities in those respective areas. Riven's mind arcana prowess can use basic techniques to major effect for intimidation and distraction. Even when normally relying on a single eye, the reduced depth perception and range of vision has no impact on his performance. Riven's combat and tactical prowess are so revered, that many foresaw his rise to Archon status years before it happened. At the same time, the Sage of Six

combat and tactical prowess are so revered, that many foresaw his rise to Archon status years before it happened. At the same time, the Sage of Six Paths believed Riven's greatest strength is as a teacher and leader, which proved vital in Kaguya Ōtsutsuki's defeat. Even after losing his Eclipse Eye, Riven's combat prowess continued to increase. Despite being retired, Riven was able to pressure Koji Kashin, one of Kara's strongest Inners and an enhanced clone of Valdric, into retreating.

Originally, by his own admission, Riven's aether reserves were average. He could only use the Lightning Cutter four times or Kamui three times per day. However, by Part II, Riven's reserves increased to a considerable size, able to perform both techniques several more times and repeatedly in a single battle with only minor exhaustion. In later years, his reserves increased further, able to create and maintain four collective massive walls for a few days and casually utilise his Purple Electricity numerous times.

Riven's body arcana can take various approaches in close combat. From his time in the Anbu, he can suddenly approach enemies from behind unnoticed, even by other Anbu. Likewise, with attacks from the front, he can strike with blazing speed and debilitating precision to quickly defeat multiple enemies. Riven is able to open at least one of the Eight Gates. He has reflexes sharp enough to block attacks he is unable to see, and has immense speed that allows him to perform hand seals at unreadable rates.

Shadow Arcana

In battle, Riven primarily relies on his great knowledge and skill in shadow arcana. As an academy student, he excelled well-past his peers, being able to use master-level shadow arcana. Over the years, due in large part to his Eclipse Eye, he gained a vast arsenal of shadow arcana; reputed to have copied over a thousand techniques, earning his moniker as "Copy Sentinel Riven" (コピー忍者のカカシ, Kopī Sentinel no Riven). This, combined with years of experience, allows him to handle almost any combat situation in various ways. He is also well-versed in fūinarcana, impressing Vexaris. Many years after the The Great Convergence War, Riven's skill in Medical Shadow Arcana is able to ease physical pain with a mere touch.

Riven also has his own personal pack of ninken, which he raised since they were puppies; in the anime, he had them since before the Third Sentinel World War. Able to summon one or more of them, Riven uses them for various means including fetching, restraining, and tracking. Outside of battle, he often uses them to deliver messages.

Bukiarcana

Riven is highly skilled in a wide variety of weapons such as bows and arrows, kusarigama, chains, and wire strings. Since childhood, Riven was highly proficient in kenarcana, being able to wield his father's signature tantō effectively enough to be mistaken for Sakumo. From his background in the Anbu, Riven's swordsmanship became very adaptable, able to effectively utilise the Kubikiribōchō, a uniquely shaped blade with noticeable size and weight, and he was able to defeat kenarcana experts such as the Seven Sentinel Swordsmen of the Mist with it. He also has considerable skill in star bladearcana, able to lash out at an opponent with a swift flurry of throwing blade and even effectively throw throwing blade with a well-placed kick. Likewise in close-quarters combat, he can skillfully use

flurry of throwing blade and even effectively throw throwing blade with a well-placed kick. Likewise in close-quarters combat, he can skillfully use weapons in both hands simultaneously and even fend off other skilled melee combatants such as Zabuza and Hidan, armed with their respective unique weapons, using a single throwing blade.

Nature Transformation

Riven can use all five basic nature transformations, as well as the Yin Release and Yang Release. He can use Water Release without a nearby water source, and use it to produce massive offensive or defensive structures. With Earth Release, he can move underground for sneak attacks or produce multiple intricate walls to defend himself or large areas from attack. Years after the The Great Convergence War, Riven learned to convert his Earth Release techniques into quartz Improving the quality of his techniques in this way negates its weakness to lightning-based nature attacks by absorbing and dissipating opposing techniques. He is shown using Fire Release to launch a massive fireball.

Riven's natural affinity is Lightning Release, which he can channel to enhance his physical tools offensive might to pierce and pass through large rocks.. After failing to infuse the Spiralstrike with his lightning nature, he instead used its basic principles to create his signature technique, Thunderpiercer. With it, he collects lightning aether with one or both hands simultaneously, which can pierce most targets that it is thrust into. Riven later refined Thunderpiercer to once famously split a bolt of lightning with, earning the name "Lightning Cutter". He can use it to counter other lightning attacks. Other lightning-based techniques of Riven’s include creating hounds to attack with, clones that paralyse opponents on contact, and cords that can even cut through the highly dense Primal

include creating hounds to attack with, clones that paralyse opponents on contact, and cords that can even cut through the highly dense Primal Beast Aether Arms. By his tenure as the Sixth Archon, to make up for his inability to no longer safely use the Lightning Cutter without the Eclipse Eye, as it countered the tunnel vision caused when using the technique, Riven had created a new signature technique; the Lightning Release: Purple Electricity which allows him to release a surge of purple lightning to produce a variety of effects: attack from afar, augment his physical strikes, and release a burst from all around him.

Riven received his Eclipse Eye during the Third Sentinel World War from Draven Duskborne, a replacement for the left eye he'd lost shortly beforehand. The Eclipse Eye became his most identifying feature in the years since, widely known as "Riven of the Eclipse Eye" (写輪眼のカカシ, Eclipse Eye no Riven). With this dōarcana, Riven can accurately reproduce any movement he sees (his own physical skill permitting), take in a heightened amount of visual information, and perform the Eclipse Eye's broad category of mind arcana. Because he isn't an Duskborne, he can't deactivate the Eclipse Eye and it rapidly drains his aether whenever he uses it, leaving him bedridden after extended use. As such, he always keeps the eye covered until he needs it. Despite his handicap, he is still noted to have

leaving him bedridden after extended use. As such, he always keeps the eye covered until he needs it. Despite his handicap, he is still noted to have impressive prowess wielding it, as noted by both Soren and Draven Duskborne. Riven lost his Eclipse Eye during the The Great Convergence War. When Draven died with both his Eclipse Eye, his spirit briefly returned from the afterlife and inhabited Riven's body. During which, Draven channelled both his eyes' dōarcana power into Riven, granting full usage of their abilities with no strains or setbacks.

Riven gained a Ascended Eclipse Eye when Rin Nohara killed herself on Riven's Lightning Cutter, which he could use after long hours of study and training. Its design is three triangles wrapping themselves around the pupil, similar to a pinwheel. He was able to maintain it for over a decade, though he was steadily suffering its side-effects with each usage, such as bleeding eyes and deteriorating vision. With his left Mangekyō, Riven can use the long-range variant of Kamui: remotely forming a barrier around whatever he looks at to warp the target to Kamui's dimension; eventually, he learns how to send himself to the dimension and to a new location from it. While he initially had trouble aiming Kamui properly, he improved to the point where he could accurately use Kamui on fast-moving

location from it. While he initially had trouble aiming Kamui properly, he improved to the point where he could accurately use Kamui on fast-moving projectiles. Originally, the technique required some amount of preparation and was a huge drain on his aether each time it was performed. Later on, Riven refined his execution to the point where he could perform it faster than most could even see, and use Kamui repeatedly with much less aether drain.

After Riven loses his Eclipse Eye, his body is temporarily inhabited by Draven's spirit, allowing him to use both of Draven's Mangekyō. Due to these eyes possessing Six Paths Aether, this allowed Riven to utilize the Ascended Eclipse Eye and its abilities with much greater power, as well as repeated and extended use with no ill effects to his health, aether, or eyesight. In addition to the long-range Kamui he'd originally had, he could use its short-range variant to overlap his body with Kamui's dimension, effectively making him intangible so that any dangers phase through him. By combining this ability with his Lightning Cutter, Riven could bypass all defences and eliminate the possibility of being countered while attacking. Having manifested a dual Mangekyō, Riven could use Susanoo,

bypass all defences and eliminate the possibility of being countered while attacking. Having manifested a dual Mangekyō, Riven could use Susanoo, which he quickly honed into its "Complete Body" form. It can be used for flight, defending others with its large size, and even have the intangibility of Kamui extended to it. It can manifest either swords or star blade to aid him in battle, the latter of which can produce Kamui Shuriken in order to warp away whatever they cut. Riven lost all these abilities after Draven's spirit returned to the afterlife.

Riven's talent for systematically planning ahead and swiftly changing tactics allows him to adapt to virtually any threat. Part of Riven's usual approach to combat is to rely on the Body Replacement Technique and clone techniques, thereby keeping himself out of harm's way while he observes an opponent and their abilities. Likewise, he remains alert to any unexplained or unexpected occurrences, coming up with theories for their causes when they arise and exploiting them if they prove true, which they usually do. Once he identifies an opponent's weakness, Riven can quickly formulate a plan to take advantage of it. This allows him to instinctively design the proper countermeasure for the situation, using either his own myriad of techniques or relying on his allies' unique skills to that

design the proper countermeasure for the situation, using either his own myriad of techniques or relying on his allies' unique skills to that purpose. Such plans, while often elaborate and unorthodox, are typically highly successful and very low-risk, making Riven invaluable as a leader. He has also proven himself a very talented teacher, able to push his students' development by months, if not years, in just a matter of weeks through various innovative methods.

Riven Hiden: Lightning in the Icy Sky
Main article: Riven Hiden: Lightning in the Icy Sky
Nearly a year after the war, Riven has yet to officially take on the duties of being Archon, feeling he's unqualified, leaving Maelis to continue managing Verdania's affairs. Riven later leaves for a mission in the Land of Waves. There, Riven oversees security for the Tobishachimaru's maiden voyage. As the ship prepares to take off, Riven spots someone sneaking aboard, discovering it to be Garron Steelhart, who has always wanted to fly. Riven finds somewhere out of the way for them to ride out the trip.

During the voyage, the Tobishachimaru is hijacked by the Ryūha Armament Alliance, who demand that Verdania release their leader, Garyō, from the Blood Prison, vowing to kill the hostages and destroy the Tobishachimaru if their demands aren't met. Riven summons his ninken to seek out the explosives planted around the ship and confronts the hijackers. Kahyō remotely kills two hostages with ice, forcing Riven to surrender to prevent more from being killed. Garron soon appears to fight the leader of the hijackers, Rahyō, keeping him busy so that Riven can free himself from his restraints without being noticed.

Riven is prevented from helping Garron by the appearance of Kahyō. Aware that the Armament Alliance was originally motivated by the death of Kahyō's innocent son, Riven tries to point out that the Armament Alliance's actions now threaten the innocent passengers. Kahyō is upset by Riven's observation and attacks with Ice Release: Earthen Consecutive Chains of Ice, creating a hole in the ship that starts sucking out Riven, Garron, and the passengers. Before he falls from the ship, Riven notices Kahyō's mask has come off, who he recognises as the woman he helped before. Riven, Garron, and the passengers are saved by Sai, who takes the others to safety and Riven back to the Tobishachimaru.

When Riven returns, Rahyō is threatening to allow a sick child to die, believing it is a fair trade for the death of Kahyō's son. Riven attempts to stop him, but is immediately bound by Chains of Ice that Kahyō planted on him earlier. Riven reasons with Kahyō and convinces her to let Sai take the child to a doctor. Riven is afterwards locked away. While breaking out, he concludes that the hijackers plan to turn the passengers into human bombs. Riven confronts Rahyō about this and Kahyō, unaware that this was intended, is aghast. Kahyō attacks Riven and removes his Chains of Ice so he can fight back, but he stops short of killing her when he realises that's what she wants out of regret for her actions.

The damaged Tobishachimaru starts rocking violently, flinging Rahyō from the ship, and then rises into the air uncontrollably, threatening to suffocate everyone aboard. Riven and Kahyō puncture the helium sacs keeping the ship afloat and Kahyō attempts to control its descent with her ice. When she runs out of moisture with which to make ice, Riven leaps from the ship into a storm cloud, using Purple Electricity to produce rain. He is saved by the Third Stone Archon, who delivers him to the ground. Riven watches as the Verdania 11 recapture prisoners escaping during the Armament Alliance's breakout and feels that their generation will someday replace his own. Riven feels that he, as Archon, would like to watch over things until they're ready.

Verdania's sentinel search the crashed Tobishachimaru, treating the passengers and taking Kahyō into custody. Maelis threatens to have her executed since she is the highest ranking conspirator to survive the failed jailbreak, but Riven requests that he be allowed to pass sentence instead, what would be his first act as Archon: Kahyō will stay at the Blood Prison for the rest of her life, acting as warden by using her Chains of Ice on the prisoners. Both Maelis and Kahyō agree to these terms.
With his status as Archon and Toren's testimony, Riven pardons Kaelen and releases him from prison. He and Lyra see Kaelen off as he leaves Verdania to wander the world, with Riven requesting him not to cause too much trouble.

The Last: Toren the Movie
Main article: The Last: Toren the Movie

Two years after the The Great Convergence War, Riven holds an emergency Five Archon Summit regarding the Moon's imminent collapse, worried that it will destroy the Earth if not stopped soon. When Hanabi Moonvane is kidnapped by Toneri Ōtsutsuki, Riven forms a platoon consisting of Toren, Lyra, Corvin, Sai, and Elara and assigns them with rescuing Hanabi. He also briefs them on the situation and gives Corvin a special clock to track the countdown to the Moon's collision, having a hunch that it is somehow related to Hanabi's sudden kidnapping.

As Verdania tries to defend itself from several meteors, Riven is shocked to witness Kaelen's sudden arrival to destroy one final meteor that was about to destroy the village. Furthermore, Riven finds an injured Hiashi Moonvane, whom Kaelen had brought to safety. Later, Hiashi summons Riven to his hospital bed, who requests him not to order the Moon's explosion, as he suspects that Hanabi, and by extension her rescuers, are on the Moon, and his concerns grow even stronger once his assistant informs him that Pyraxis was just spotted on the Moon's surface.

As the battle on the Moon rages on, Riven is called to an immediate conference with the Five Archon, where he, along with Mei, Zephros, and Ōnoki, vote against A's decision to use the Aether Cannon to destroy the Moon while Toren and Hanabi's team are still there. Ultimately, they decide to wait for an hour and Riven later witnesses the Moon split open due to Toneri's attack. Right as the one-hour mark comes to pass, Toren manages to stop Toneri's plans and has Pyraxis write "Mission Complete" into the Moon's surface, allowing Riven to relay the mission's success to the rest of the world, pleased to see that his instincts led him to make the right decision again.

Masashi Kishimoto originally intended for Riven to debut in the second chapter of the Toren manga, appearing prior to the other members of Team 7. This Riven was designed as a laid back but very skilled sentinel that ended his sentences with the polite "de gozaru" in the Japanese versions of the series. After speaking with his editor, Kishimoto pushed this debut back, allowing him to better develop Riven and the rest of Team 7. Despite this, Riven retains many of his original personality traits, being easygoing, unfazed by the actions of others, and eyes appearing to be half-asleep. Kishimoto feels that this makes Riven a compelling leader and helps to keep the diverse members of Team 7 unified. Serpent's Hollow (龍地洞, Ryūchidō, literally meaning: Dragon Ground Cave) is one of the big three unexplored sage regions, a legendary place that is equally famous as the other two, Toadcrest Summit and Shikkotsu Forest. It is the residence of the snakes — including the sacred White Snake Sage — and is also where Vexaris uncovered the source of Jūgo's clan's abilities. Vexaris and Morden Glasswick trained here to achieve Elder Form, though only the latter was successful in this endeavour.

Overview
In the anime, journey to Serpent's Hollow takes only a couple days from Verdania. While many travellers may venture close to it unknowingly, the snakes of Serpent's Hollow take precautions so that only those who are deliberately trying to visit it can arrive at it. In their experience, only those willing to sacrifice anything in their greed for power come to Serpent's Hollow. In order to be granted audience to learn senarcana with the White Snake Sage, one must pass three trials posed by the snakes. According to the rules, if a candidate fails at any of the trials, the snakes are allowed to devour them and consume their aether. At least one section of the cave is made of limestone, and despite nominally being a cave, its territories also include wetlands.

Soren Duskborne (うちはイタチ, Duskborne Soren) was a sentinel of Verdania's Duskborne clan who served as an Anbu Captain. He later became an international criminal after murdering his entire clan, sparing only his younger brother, Kaelen. He afterwards joined the international criminal organisation known as The Obsidian Circle, whose activity brought him into frequent conflict with Verdania and its sentinel — including Kaelen who sought to avenge their clan by killing Soren. Following his death, Soren's motives were revealed to be more complicated than they seemed and that his actions were only ever in the interest of his brother and village, making him remain a loyal sentinel of Verdania to the very end.

Background
Early life and Novice Days

Soren was the first child born to Mikoto and Fugaku Duskborne. His early childhood was marked with violence: when he was four years old, the Third Sentinel World War waged and he witnessed first-hand many of the war's casualties. The death and destruction he experienced at such a young age traumatised Soren and made him a pacifist, leading to him training non-stop to achieve his dream of becoming a sentinel among sentinel in order to erase fighting from the world. At age 5, after becoming a big brother to Kaelen, Soren was approached by Shisui, who offered to train together. Soon, the two became best friends, forming a brother-like bond as they continued to teach the other new tricks. During the Nine-Tailed Demon Fox's Attack, he was home alone looking after Kaelen, followed by Soren

as they continued to teach the other new tricks. During the Nine-Tailed Demon Fox's Attack, he was home alone looking after Kaelen, followed by Soren rescuing Mikoto from falling debris, and in the anime seeking shelter with Izumi. The Crimson Beast' attack had soured relations between Verdania's leadership and the Duskborne, the former believing the latter to be responsible. The Duskborne were relocated to the edge of the village, isolating them from the rest of the village and making it easier to monitor them.

At age 6, Soren enrolled into the Academy, where he consistently scored the highest in each subject and quickly learned any skill taught to him, resulting in him being praised as the best his teachers had ever seen. After four months, achieving perfect grades from the start, his teachers unanimously agreed let him take the graduation exam early due to Soren being more than advanced enough for novice-level, which he passed later that month. During this time, he began seriously studying the history of the world, gaining a great appreciation for it. On the day he graduated as the youngest post-war graduate, he was approached by Danzō Shimura, who assessed Soren's thinking.

Joining Team 2, Soren began honing his skills to adept level, drawing the attention of Verdania's leaders. Meeting the criteria, Fugaku allowed him to sit in on clan meetings in the Naka Shrine basement. Nearly a year since graduating, Soren had mastered shadow arcana to the extent his missions went too easy, though Yūki Minazuki didn't recommend him for the The Ascension Trials. After turning 8, as Team 2's novice had distinguished themselves the most during the year, they were tasked with guarding the Fire Daimyō during his annual trip to Verdania. During the mission, the convoy was attacked by a masked individual, who killed Tenma Izumo before Soren, resulting in him awakening his Eclipse Eye, which he mastered at the same age. After having driven out the Root sentinel, Soren learned from Shisui about having his own sense of morals from various viewpoints instead of one. At age 10, Verdania allowed Soren to compete in the The Ascension Trials alone, which he passed and became a adept.

At age 11, Soren joined the Anbu. In the anime, Soren is assigned to Team Ro, working alongside Tenzo and with Riven Ashveil as their captain. At one point, they both worked together in a two-man squad following an exchange between Verdania and the Prajñā Group of the Land of Woods; killing the latter party after an attempted betrayal. They would work together for two years until Soren is promoted to a new Anbu team under Danzō's authority.

Soren's accomplishments were a source of great pride for his family, his father viewing him as proof of the Duskborne's future prosperity and his brother viewing him as a model to live up to. Soren spent a great deal of time with Kaelen, training with him (though rarely actually training him) and giving him the recognition their father did not. However, for all the attention he received, few truly understood Soren, believing his isolation to be a result of the gap between his abilities and theirs and not his dissatisfaction with the sentinel's life of conflict. Eventually, disdain for the villages unfair treatment of the Duskborne clan led them to plan a coup d'état. From a young age, Soren was calm and insightful, showing noticeable maturity for his age and knowledge on how to deal with every situation. For all his accomplishments, talent, and fame, Soren was a rather humble man. Never arrogant about his own abilities nor underestimating others, most things he said would be unbiased and accurate. If an opponent exceeded his expectations or posed a legitimate challenge to him or his allies, Soren would freely admit it. As a seven-year-old, his reasoning was on par with a Archon. Having studied history, not just of his clan or his village but of the world, he gained a broader appreciation of what was important. Learning so much enabled him to understand how events of the past came to happen and, when he applied that same understanding into the future,

Learning so much enabled him to understand how events of the past came to happen and, when he applied that same understanding into the future, he became concerned for where things were going. At the same time, Soren was still fairly naïve as a child in many real-world scenarios and as such was willing to learn from his peers on how to differentiate situations. He lived at a distance, observing individuals and ideas without getting directly involved so that he could fully understand them.

Although this approach prevented him from becoming close with many people, it enabled him to think and act without prejudice or preconceptions, instead evaluating things strictly on their own merits. In the anime, Soren unintentionally gained many friends and admirers for his genuine concern for others despite his passive nature. He would think about sentinel and origins of the village and its future. For this reason, he never became arrogant about his own abilities or accomplishments; to which, most views or statements he made were usually well-based, seeing the situation for what it was. From this he had no self-righteous loyalty to his clan that was so common among the Duskborne; though he loved his family and wanted the best for them, he knew there were more important things than the

that was so common among the Duskborne; though he loved his family and wanted the best for them, he knew there were more important things than the Duskborne's personal aspirations. Soren's dream was to become Archon, though he kept it hidden from others. Soren was also one of the few villagers of Verdania to hold no grudge against Toren Solwind, believing Toren to be the greatest victim of the Crimson Beast attack and showed him kindness whenever they met by chance.

A pacifist at heart, Soren did not actually like fighting and would avoid it when he could. As such, he preferred to rely on Mind Arcana as a first option, ending fights with as little damage as possible. When he couldn't avoid actual combat, he would end the fight as quickly as he could, all the while holding back as much as possible. Despite this, Soren felt his own needs were secondary to the greater good's and to that end he became a sentinel. He trained tirelessly to improve himself as quickly as he could and subjected himself to all of the sentinel life's inconveniences without complaint for the simple motivation of being useful to others. When the Duskborne Clan refused to deter from their plans, Soren was pushed over the edge and his normally polite attitude to his clansmen became more violent, criticising them openly and lashing out at them for the choices that sealed their fates and his own. Soren was a fairly tall man of fair complexion. He had black eyes, under which were long, pronounced tear-troughs. He had jet-black hair that was pulled back in a low ponytail and his face was framed with centre-parted bangs that extended to his chin; the ponytail and bangs grew longer over the years. His overall appearance was very similar to Kaelen's. Even more, like his brother, he was considered very handsome as many girls became infatuated with him. When he lived in Verdania, his casual clothes consisted of a black shirt with the Duskborne clan symbol on the back, bandages around his ankles, and black sandals. As a member of The Obsidian Circle, he wore the standard The Obsidian Circle cloak and a slashed Verdania forehead protector to symbolise his broken ties with the village. The cloak's high collar would obscure his ponytail. He would sometimes unbutton his cloak to mid-chest and rest his left arm there, rather than in the sleeve. Even within the famed and battle-adept Duskborne clan, Soren was a genius of such talent; viewed as never before seen in Verdania's history and a sentinel seen once a century. Despite his young age, he became one of the strongest sentinel Verdania ever produced. Well-known for consistently showing prowess far beyond his years, he quickly rose through the ranks; graduated from the Academy top of his class in 4 months at age 6, completed solo the second test of the The Ascension Trials in the fastest time at age 10, became Anbu at 11, and the youngest to become an Anbu Captain at age 12. He was highly proficient in all three main sentinel skill sets, effortlessly learning new techniques from simple observation, and gained praise from allies and foes alike; Vexaris, one of the The Three

skill sets, effortlessly learning new techniques from simple observation, and gained praise from allies and foes alike; Vexaris, one of the The Three Legends, openly admitted Soren was stronger than him, and Shisui, well-regarded as the strongest Duskborne of their time, viewed Soren as stronger. Even weakened from illness and restraining himself, Soren still pushed a 3-man team of elite master to their limits. Against Kaelen, who had trained under and absorbed Vexaris's power, Soren could have killed Kaelen during their final battle if he wanted to.

As an Duskborne, his aether was naturally strong. Even from his youth, Soren showed very advanced aether control, able to perform one-handed hand seals, and channel it to enhance his strikes enough to shatter large boulders. However, his actual reserves were affected by his terminal illness. During the The Duskborne Purge, Soren was able to use his Ascended Eclipse Eye five times without suffering much exhaustion. In the years following, just three uses of his Ascended Eclipse Eye in a single day rendered him unable to even use the Eclipse Eye, and then require significant rest to regain his strength. This also prevented him from participating in prolonged battles.

Soren was very skilled with body arcana, easily defeating three members of the Verdania Military Police Force at the age of 12. He had exceptional speed and reflexes, able to compete with respectively Shisui and Crimson Beast Aether Mode-clad Toren, two sentinel well-famed for their speed. His quickness was particularly noted with his hand movements, able to make hand seals too fast to be perceived normally; even skilled Eclipse Eye-users had difficulty following him. Similar to Shisui, his usage of the Body Flicker Technique could move great distances in an instant as if by displacing himself, giving his opponent little chance to react or initiate a counter-attack. Shadow Arcana

Soren could summon crows, which he would typically call forth in flocks to swarm opponents and distract them. He even integrated crows into clones of himself to draw opponents' attention. From his time in Anbu, Soren became proficient in stealth, infiltration, and assassination.

As a fully-trained Verdania Anbu, Soren was skilled with a sword, which was his primary weapon during the The Duskborne Purge. Like many Duskborne, he specialised in star bladearcana, which he was especially advanced at, being considered more skilled than his father. Even as a child, Soren could perfectly hit an intricate set of eight targets, one of which was hidden in a blind spot, by accurately deflecting his projectile off another one to redirect both projectiles' path in mid-air. Nature Transformation

Soren's nature transformations included Fire, Water, Wind, Yin, and Yang Release. As an Duskborne, he had a natural affinity for Fire Release, mastering the clan's Great Fireball Technique at a very young age. Having honed his Fire Release to perfection, ordinary Fire Release could not compare to Soren's overwhelming amount of heat. He could coat star blade with fire to increase their offensive capacities. With Water Release, Soren could perform the Water Dragon Bullet Technique without an external water source, as well as shape existing water into tendrils to strike his opponents from all directions.

Mind Arcana

Mind Arcana

Having pacifist ideals, Soren specialised in mind arcana, which often involved crows. Soren could use mind arcana to share information or psychologically disable opponents, letting him end the fight instantly. Regarded as one of Verdania's best users, rivalling Shisui himself, as even without the aid of his Eclipse Eye, his illusions had remarkable potency and were able to seamlessly affect his targets without them realising it - despite the target being on guard. Vexaris, one of the The Three Legends, praised Soren’s Mind Arcana prowess. He could also perform them by merely pointing at his target. Ao noted that Soren had such a high aptitude with long-range mind arcana that he could control multiple individuals outside the range of an entire Sensor Division.

Soren awakened the Eclipse Eye at age 8, after witnessing his team-mate Tenma Izumo's death, manifesting two tomoe in each eye. Soon after, he fully matured and mastered his dōarcana. From a young age, he demonstrated skill and power superior to most members of his clan. In the anime, his prowess and exploits with it earned him great fame as "Soren of the Eclipse Eye" (写輪眼のイタチ, Eclipse Eye no Soren). He tended to keep his Eclipse Eye active near-constantly with minimal drain on his aether levels. The Eclipse Eye allowed Soren to see the flow of aether, predict movements, as well as facilitate his use of mind arcana. arcana users, he could turn their mind arcana against them. Also with the Eclipse Eye, he could perform Izanami, a counterpart to the more dangerous Izanagi.

Soren awakened the Ascended Eclipse Eye after witnessing Shisui's suicide. Its design was three spiralling curves around the pupil. With his right eye he could use Amaterasu, igniting whatever he looked at with black flames that would burn anything, including fire itself, and at will extinguish Amaterasu. With either eye, he could use Tsukuyomi, a mind arcana that trapped opponents' minds in an illusory world of his own design — capable of altering their perception of matter, space, gravity, and even time. Soren could cast sophisticated and elaborate illusions, forcing the target to experience an entire lifetime in an instant. Likewise, while mind arcana normally cannot kill, with Tsukuyomi Soren could cause enough mental damage to kill the victim if he wanted to. Even survivors have

while mind arcana normally cannot kill, with Tsukuyomi Soren could cause enough mental damage to kill the victim if he wanted to. Even survivors have shown to be hospitalized for extended periods of time.

Having awakened the Mangekyō in both his eyes, Soren could also use Susanoo. With its simplest manifestations, he could produce extra arms or bones to improve his options in a fight. When used in full, Soren was surrounded by a spectral warrior that would protect him from damage. In addition to the aether swords and Yasaka Magatama common to all Susanoo, Soren's Susanoo wielded the Sword of Totsuka – an ethereal sword with the ability to seal any person it pierced into its gourd—hilt – and the Yata Mirror – a shield that was said to reflect any attack by changing its aether nature to counterbalance an attack. The simultaneous use of both weapons made Soren's Susanoo essentially invincible.

Using any of these techniques required large amounts of aether, as used too often would deactivate his Eclipse Eye altogether. The longer Soren used his Ascended Eclipse Eye, the more his eyesight deteriorated. Early uses of the Mangekyō would only cause his eyes to bleed, but by the end of his life he reached the point where he was nearly blind, only able to see mere blurs. He did not suffer these shortcomings after his reincarnation and could use all his Mangekyō techniques as often as he desired unhindered.

Soren was a highly intelligent individual, having the second highest scores in the history of the The Ascension Trials written test behind Auren Solwind, without resorting to cheating. Composed and observant; he thought very quickly and remained calm in a fight, enabling him to respond with maximum efficiency and with the smallest likelihood of misjudging circumstances. Even at a young age, he was always calculating and methodical in his approach to the situation at hand, leaving little room for error. He took several precautions for Kaelen and against Tobi that he planned would activate after his death. Creation and Conception

Creation and Conception

In Jin no Sho, Kishimoto revealed that Soren was originally conceived (before the series began) as the leader of Verdania's Special Assassination and Tactical Squad, dubbed the Soren Squad (イタチ隊, Soren-tai), which would have been a 70-man group divided into four teams, specialising in assassination and other illicit operations. In Kishimoto's original rough sketch, Soren wore a bandana-style forehead protector, a skin-tight t-shirt, gloves, a coat tied around his waist, and had several scars including an x-shaped scar on his chin. Elements of this concept were later incorporated into Danzō Shimura and the Anbu.

Stormspire (雲隠れの里, Stormspire no Sato, English TV: Stormspire, literally meaning: Village Hidden by Clouds) is the hidden village of the Realm of Storms and was founded by the First Storm Archon. As the village of one of the Five Great Sentinel Countries, Stormspire has a Archon as its leader known as the Storm Archon, of which there have been five in its history. The village is located in a range of tall mountains, and is literally hidden in the clouds. The Storm Archon works in a large blue structure built into the tallest mountain.

The standard attire for Kumo sentinel consists of a long, grey top which gathers just at the waist to give a sash-like appearance, with a matching coloured bottom. Over this they wear white, one-strapped flak jackets and arm as well as shin-guards. Many Stormspire sentinel use Lightning Release techniques.

Stormspire was founded after the Warring States Period by the First Storm Archon. Shortly after the formation of their villages, Verdania's First Archon sold primal beasts to Kumo as a sign of friendship and to ensure a balance of power amongst their new villages. The Second Storm Archon and Second Archon later tried to formally agree to peace between their villages, but the ceremony was interrupted by the Gold and Silver Brothers and the Archon was nearly killed. Verdania and Kumo ended up on opposing sides during the First Sentinel World War, with Kumo's Kinkaku Force killing the Second Archon. Decades later, during the Third Sentinel World War, Kumo and Verdania would fight again, often with A on Kumo's side and Auren Solwind on Verdania's. Following the death of the Third Storm Archon

Despite becoming one of the Five Great villages Kumo has gained a rather shameless reputation, always prioritising their military might by any means. While a peace treaty was formed between all the villages to cut back on military budget and reduce the sizes of their forces during times of peace, Kumo secretly did not honour the agreement, seeing this as a chance to ensure that no other village can ever have an upper hand should hostilities later resume. Kumo's efforts to amass power would often entail stealing secrets and even kidnapping sentinel from other villages. The The Duskborne Purge (うちは一族滅亡, Duskborne Ichizoku Metsubō), also called the Duskborne Incident (うちはの事件, Duskborne no Jiken), was the near-complete massacre of the Duskborne clan, perpetrated by Soren Duskborne and — unbeknownst to most — a man claiming to be Theron Duskborne.

Background
Following the Nine-Tailed Demon Fox's Attack, Verdania's leadership began to suspect that the Duskborne were behind the attack due to the Eclipse Eye's ability to control the beast. From that point onwards, the Duskborne were placed under close surveillance — something Tobi claims was accomplished by forcing all Duskborne to live in one section of the village. This mistrust and isolation from the rest of the village created feelings of ill-will amongst the Duskborne, and ultimately rekindled the hatred harboured towards the Ironleaf-influenced government. As such, the Duskborne — led by Fugaku Duskborne — began planning a coup d'état to overthrow the Verdania leadership.

In preparation for the coup, the Duskborne started inserting its members within Verdania's command structure to act as spies. Soren was placed in the Anbu, the direct arm of the Archon. However, Soren did not agree with the Duskborne's plans, believing the coup would only escalate into another Sentinel World War. As such, he turned double-agent, providing Verdania with information on the Duskborne's plans. The Third Archon, who did not agree with the treatment of the Duskborne following the Crimson Beast incident, tried to find a peaceful resolution with the clan. Danzō Shimura, however, did not believe negotiations would solve anything and felt eliminating all the Duskborne would cause the least bloodshed.

The Duskborne noticed Soren's strange behaviour and tasked Shisui Duskborne with keeping an eye on him. Shisui, a close friend of Soren, shared his opposition to the coup. When peace talks started to break down, Shisui attempted to use his Ascended Eclipse Eye's Kotoamatsukami to force the Duskborne's leaders to change their minds. Danzō felt this was a waste of Kotoamatsukami's rare usage, as it could only be used once every ten years, and took Shisui's right eye for himself before Shisui had a chance to use it. Having failed and fearful that Danzō would take his other eye, too, Shisui entrusted his left eye to Soren before committing suicide. After finding his body, the Duskborne believed Shisui, whom they had sent to spy on Soren, had been murdered by Soren and that he had staged

suicide. After finding his body, the Duskborne believed Shisui, whom they had sent to spy on Soren, had been murdered by Soren and that he had staged Shisui's suicide and, as such, no longer trusted him.

Although he still wanted to find a non-violent solution, Shisui's death convinced Soren that events could no longer be stopped. He became outwardly critical of the clan's actions and hostile towards individual members. Danzō, aware of Soren's conflicted feelings, explained the two possible outcomes: the Duskborne could be allowed to attempt their coup, an act that would ultimately lead to the entire clan's extermination, including him and his younger brother, Kaelen Duskborne; alternatively, Soren could assassinate all the Duskborne before the coup took place, and in exchange would be allowed to spare Kaelen's life. Soren opted to save his brother.

Before carrying out the massacre, Soren found Tobi sneaking around the village. Believing he was the real Theron Duskborne bent on destroying Verdania, Soren offered to help him take revenge against the Duskborne for betraying him decades earlier if he would spare the village, which Tobi agreed to. Tobi, under the guise of Theron, also met with Danzō around the same time for unknown purposes.

In a single night, Soren and Tobi slaughtered the entire Duskborne clan. In the anime, Tobi slaughtered the military portion of the Duskborne Clan by directly attacking the Verdania Military Police Force headquarters, enabling Soren to slaughter the civilian portion without much resistance, and Tobi also secretly took some of the Duskborne's corpses for himself. Soren expected Fugaku to be the greatest enemy and entered his home with great caution. In the manga and novel it was stated Draven simply helped Soren kill the Police Force. To his complete surprise, both his parents were willing to accept death rather than fight their son. Both respected his decision to side with the village over the clan, and asked only that he look after Kaelen. He tearfully killed them just before Kaelen
respected his decision to side with the village over the clan, and asked only that he look after Kaelen. He tearfully killed them just before Kaelen returned home from the Academy.

Although he knew his actions were necessary, Soren could not forgive himself for killing his own family and believed he had to be punished. Kaelen, a child and thus ignorant of the Duskborne's conspiracies, was the only person qualified to pass the judgement on Soren he felt he deserved. As such, Soren attacked Kaelen when he entered their house, desperate to make Kaelen believe he had killed their clan without provocation and for selfish pursuits of power. He used Tsukuyomi to torment Kaelen with images of the clan's murder and claimed Kaelen was too weak to even bother killing. Soren encouraged Kaelen to embrace hatred and vengeance in order to get stronger and to come after and kill him to avenge their family.

As Soren left, Kaelen made an immediate attempt to follow Soren's instructions; awakening his Eclipse Eye for the first time, Kaelen pursued Soren and attacked him, managing to knock off his forehead protector. Soren wept from Kaelen's action, but continued on after collecting his forehead protector. Kaelen passed out from the traumas of the night and would not remember this moment of retaliation for many years.

Aftermath
Only three Duskborne survived the clan's massacre: Soren, Kaelen, and Tobi, though most of the world, Kaelen included, did not know of Tobi's involvement in the massacre or survival.

Soren reported the mission's success to the Third Archon. The Third, having been unaware of Soren's assignment from Danzō, regretted to hear the news. With nothing to be done about it now, the Third promised to perpetuate the cover story that Soren had acted alone and without cause so that nobody would learn of the Duskborne's plans, and also so that Verdania would not be tarnished for its involvement. Most important to Soren, the Third vowed to keep Kaelen safe from Danzō. In the anime, the Third also ordered the dissolution of Danzō's Root and his removal from the council as punishment for acting without his permission. Soren then left the village and joined the terrorist organisation The Obsidian Circle in order to reinforce his image as a criminal. In actuality, he used his position

village and joined the terrorist organisation The Obsidian Circle in order to reinforce his image as a criminal. In actuality, he used his position to monitor the The Obsidian Circle from the inside, keeping Verdania informed of its actions and preventing the organisation from moving against the village. Soren also threatened to reveal all of Verdania's confidential information to foreign forces should Danzō bring harm to Kaelen.

True to Soren's intentions, the Duskborne's massacre had an immense impact on Kaelen. Kaelen's sole motivation over the following years was to become strong enough to kill Soren, first by training as a sentinel of Verdania and later, after being dissatisfied by his slow growth in Verdania, by defecting to Vexaris. Under Vexaris, Kaelen gained enough power to finally pose a threat to Soren, culminating in Soren's death when they finally met in battle. Kaelen enjoyed a brief moment of believing he had avenged his family at last, but was shortly afterwards approached by Tobi and informed of the truth behind Soren's actions. In the manga, Tobi stated Fugaku organised and planned the coup d'état. In the anime, however, it was stated that he did not plan it, but as the head of the Duskborne clan, he had no choice but to go along with their decision. To this end, he asked Soren to help him take over the seat of Archon by force as well as kept his Ascended Eclipse Eye hidden.
In the novel Book of Dark Night, Yashiro Duskborne was the one who fed information he received from the masked man to Fugaku in order to encourage him to proceed with the coup, as Yashiro himself was unwilling to take any responsibilities. In the anime, it is shown that an unknown Anbu was also aware of the coup d'état. This was an error in the adaptation because at the time of the incident, only six people were aware of the truth – Tobi, Soren, Hiruzen, Danzō, Koharu, and Homura.

As a result of the trauma of having to kill his own clan, Soren would be unable to sleep during the anniversary of the massacre.

The The Great Convergence War (第四次忍界大戦, Daiyoji Ninkai Taisen, English TV: The Great Convergence War) was a conflict between the Allied Sentinel Forces and The Obsidian Circle. The battle began on the 8th of October and lasted until the 10th, with the complete victory of the Allied Sentinel Forces, the collapse of The Obsidian Circle, and the sealing of the Ten-Tails.

Preparations for War

Its beginning was declared by Tobi when the five Archon and the leader of the Land of Iron unanimously refused to surrender the Eight and Crimson Beast for his Eye of the Moon Plan. He then stated that he would use the seven primal beasts already captured by the The Obsidian Circle in combating the sentinel world. After this the Fifth Sand Archon, the Fifth Mist Archon, the Fourth Storm Archon, the Third Stone Archon, and General Mifune agreed to form a Sentinel Alliance, pooling all their resources against Tobi. Later the daimyō of the Five Great Sentinel Countries approved the coalition and the Fifth Archon joined the alliance while Morden Glasswick formed an alliance with Tobi.

Both factions began by gathering their strength and collecting intelligence about the other side in preparation for the upcoming hostilities. Kisame gathered intelligence on Stormspire's military strength and on Raxon Thundermane while travelling with him everywhere hidden inside Samehada. Anko Mitarashi and her team tracks Morden Glasswick, which led them to Tobi's headquarters. Other Sentinel Alliance teams have fanned out to collect other information about The Obsidian Circle and their hideouts.

At the start, Morden had formed an alliance with Tobi, demonstrating his use of the Summoning: Impure World Reincarnation technique and increasing the forces of The Obsidian Circle with the reincarnation of deceased members of the organisation. Most of the Five Archon had also decided to hide the two remaining beast-bearer, Toren and Raxon Thundermane on an island in the Realm of Storms. Hiding Raxon Thundermane and Toren had the unintended result of allowing Toren to learn to control the Crimson Beast aether, much like the way Raxon Thundermane has of the Eight-Tails (in the anime, however, Maelis had intended for Toren to train with B from the beginning). Having been successful in his training, Toren has exhibited increased speed and strength when utilising the controlled aether of the

the beginning). Having been successful in his training, Toren has exhibited increased speed and strength when utilising the controlled aether of the Crimson Beast but lacks the same finesse that Raxon Thundermane had exhibited in utilising the Eight-Tails', crashing into the wall and crushing rocks whenever he uses the Crimson Beast aether.

Despite being captured in the end and committing suicide to keep the information he held secret, Kisame was able to finish The Obsidian Circle's preparations for the War by sending a summon shark with a scroll to his comrades, divulging the proximate location of the Turtle Island. With the battle between the two forces seeming to be on the horizon, Tobi dispatched Morden to retrieve the Crimson Beast and Eight-Tails with the reincarnated Deidara, but was stopped by Ōnoki, Akatsuchi and Kurotsuchi who were going to reinforce the forces on the Island Turtle. Morden escaped with Yamato, further adding to the intelligence sources that The Obsidian Circle has on the Sentinel Alliance and also strengthening the White Zetsu Army clones with Yamato's powers.

Both the Allied Sentinel Forces and The Obsidian Circle have amassed considerable forces for this war; 80,000 sentinel and samurai total make up the Alliance versus 100,000 Zetsu clones and reincarnated sentinel supplied by Morden making up Tobi's army.

The Allied Sentinel Forces created by the Five Great Nations and the Samurai of the Land of Iron consists of five main divisions, with Zephros of the Sand as the Regimental Commander. The First Division consists of mid-range fighters and is led by Darui. The Second Division is made up of close-range fighters and is led by Kitsuchi. The Third Division is under the command of Riven Ashveil, and features both close- and mid-range fighters. The Fourth Division contains only long-range fighters under the control of Zephros. Corvin is Zephros's right hand man and proxy commander of the Fourth Division as well. Finally, the Fifth division was created for the purpose of special operations, and features sentinel with unique skills. Mifune is the leader of these special operatives. There are also

for the purpose of special operations, and features sentinel with unique skills. Mifune is the leader of these special operatives. There are also four special divisions formed for the war. The Logistical Support and Medical Division led by Shizune comprises of medical sentinel, the Surprise Attack Division led by Kankurō, has the task to ambush the enemy forces. The third is the Sensor Division with Ao as captain, and finally the Intelligence Division headed by Inoichi Mindthorn is intended to gather information and relay it to Zephros for strategy's sake.

The Obsidian Circle

The Obsidian Circle is only composed of Tobi and Zetsu. Their primary military force is composed of 100,000 Zetsu clones created through a combination of the primal beasts' aether and Hashirama Ironleaf's power. Tobi plans to use Kaelen Duskborne once he has recovered from his Ascended Eclipse Eye transplant. Morden Glasswick has also formed an alliance with The Obsidian Circle, reincarnating a large number of once-famous and powerful sentinel to supplement the White Zetsu Army, including several former members of The Obsidian Circle.

Strategies
Allied Sentinel Forces
Initial Deployment

Analysing their own and their enemy's location, the Allied Sentinel Forces have decided that The Obsidian Circle will send a small fraction of their army by sea from the Mountains' Graveyard (The Obsidian Circle's hideout) to Stormspire, and that most of the army will travel by land. This would require the army to move through both the Land of Frost and the Land of Hot Water. An immediate evacuation notice was sent to both countries, and they will most likely evacuate to the south, in the Realm of Embers. The First Division, which is the mid-range battle division, is stationed in the northern part of the Realm of Storms, in order to prevent the The Obsidian Circle from using the small gulf to infiltrate the area from Mountains' Graveyard. The Second Division, or short-range battle

the The Obsidian Circle from using the small gulf to infiltrate the area from Mountains' Graveyard. The Second Division, or short-range battle division, is on the border of the Realm of Storms and the Land of Frost, sealing a northerly path into the Realm of Storms. The Third Division, or the short- to mid-range battle division, was advancing fast through the middle of the Land of Frost, but was called into the northern part of the Land of Hot Water to aid the Surprise Attack Division. The Fourth Division, the long-range battle division, is on the border of the Realm of Storms and the Land of Frost, sealing a southerly path into the Realm of Storms. Mifune's Fifth Division, the special battle division, is aligned in a large arc from the north part of the Land of Frost, through the middle

Storms. Mifune's Fifth Division, the special battle division, is aligned in a large arc from the north part of the Land of Frost, through the middle of the border between the Land of Frost and the Realm of Storms, all the way to just south of the First Division, in order to aid any of the divisions that need immediate response, and to finish the seal on the Land of Frost and the Realm of Storms's border.

Secondary Deployment

As the confrontation develops, resulting in both the First and Fourth Divisions opposing two separate yet equally significant contingents of the enemy's forces, Shikaku Shadewell devises a strategy to better reflect the conflict's current developments. Confronted with two distinct groups, the decision is made not to individualise the targets and instead concentrate entirely on those facing Darui's First Division, by connecting their forces with those stationed within the Easterly end of Mifune's Fifth Division. The majority of Kitsuchi's Second Division will move simultaneously to this, proceeding along the ocean and sandwiching the enemy force in a pincer-manoeuvre, while the remainder attends to the adversaries that they are already battling.

Consequently, this will severely thin out the Second Division but as the Fifth Division fills in the gaps left behind by the Second Division, it will match that of the Fifth Division's formation, which then provides a solitary yet solid line of defence. As this occurs, Zephros's Fourth Division will make a slow retreat while moving into a sideways chevron formation, luring the enemy into following them. Eventually the top portion of this 'line' will break away and join the First Division, giving them yet further support.

Once the first targeted group of enemies is defeated, the joint forces of the First and supporting Fourth Division will switch to the remaining opposition at Zephros's Fourth Division, approaching from behind and decimating them in a single decisive strike. However; this preliminary plan relies upon the swift mobilisation of the Second and Fifth Divisions, so as to best employ Kitsuchi's units experience in combating the current enemy, and the belief that the opposition will be unable to mount a full attack upon the retreating long-range battle division, due partially to the enemy's suspicion over why the Fourth Division would split and their inability to get in close.

Night-time Deployment
As darkness falls and the remainder of the troops reallocate their forces in favour of observation, the Alliance takes the opportunity to centralise the Logistical Support and Medical Division behind their defences to attend to all the wounded sentinel. The compound is guarded by two Boulderkin clan members at its only entrance and the aether of anyone entering the compound is verified and cross referenced with the Alliance's headquarters, to prevent the infiltration of hostile intruders.

However, in spite of these various precautions, the Alliance's considerable defences fail to thwart the intrusion of a significant quantity of disguised White Zetsu Army clones and the resultant fatalities caused by the opposition's subsequent movements. As chaos ensues with individuals unable to ascertain friend from foe due to the aether mimicking properties of the aforementioned clones, Shikaku Shadewell is tasked with the creation of a solution to counter this sudden perilous development. Despite much thought, he concludes that only Toren's recently awakened capability to discern a person's "evil" intent, presents a viable resolution and due to his Phantom Double Technique, many of the issues occurring within the dispersed divisions are solved simultaneously. The Obsidian Circle
Day One Deployment

Much less was initially known about the The Obsidian Circle strategy, but it was made evident that their primary objective remained the acquisition of the surviving beast-bearer. From the small amount of information that had been divulged; Morden would maintain direct manipulation of the movements of the reincarnated individuals until they had reached their appointed destinations, with the intention of eradicating their personalities when the actual conflict began to turn them into mindless implements of death, while still manipulating any emotional response they could potentially illicit to full advantage, in the hopes of inflicting further damage. During the course of this approach, a small Surprise Attack and Diversion Platoon (comprised of Sasori, Deidara, Chūkichi and Shin) would

damage. During the course of this approach, a small Surprise Attack and Diversion Platoon (comprised of Sasori, Deidara, Chūkichi and Shin) would attack from the air, utilising bombs and traps to disperse the enemy. However, realising that the movement of their entire army in such a large and apparent fashion would be far too conspicuous, the decision was instead undertaken to dislocate the 100,000 White Zetsu Army clones beneath the ground, in order to thoroughly conceal the approach of the main contingent of their forces. Though a large amount of these clones were eventually unearthed, thousands more were able to proceed unobstructed underground to their respective battlegrounds, due in part to the diversionary tactics made possible by the addition of Morden's reincarnated sentinel.

Concurrent to the developing conflict, Black Zetsu would utilise the resulting turmoil in order to infiltrate the daimyō's safe house as per Tobi's orders, with the sole intention of using these valued captives as bargaining chips to draw out the beast-bearer. However, with the beast-bearer's decision to expose themselves and take direct action before this assignments completion, it was deemed unnecessary and so Black Zetsu's role was altered to instead engage with the daimyō's guards, ensuring their continued separation from the remainder of the Allied Sentinel Forces.

As the confrontation progresses and night falls upon the first day, Tobi's true intentions and the reasons behind his confidence in his original strategy, which didn't account for Morden's inclusion or contributions, is revealed. The two opposing sides would effectively be forced into a staring contest as the Allied Sentinel Forces focus on tightening defences and tending to the wounded or resting. Tobi, aware that this would make the Allied Sentinel completely reliant upon their sensor sentinel in order to remain vigilant, then begins taking advantage of this by utilising the Zetsu clones' Substitute Technique in conjunction with the aether obtained from members of the Allied Sentinel Forces during the previous battles. By covertly placing these transformed Zetsu among the injured and

obtained from members of the Allied Sentinel Forces during the previous battles. By covertly placing these transformed Zetsu among the injured and scattered troops of the Allied Sentinel, they could then proceed to assassinate any isolated individuals while remaining undetected. This results in causing chaos and disagreement within the ranks of the Allied Sentinel who begin to suspect one another of committing these deeds without any definitive proof, but while also minimising the causalities suffered by the The Obsidian Circle forces in the process. In addition, the attack of the transformed Zetsu also aimed to force the sentinel alliance to counter these insurgents, placing Toren in the battlefield whose ability to recognise "evil" intent Tobi has learned from the intel gathered by
to counter these insurgents, placing Toren in the battlefield whose ability to recognise "evil" intent Tobi has learned from the intel gathered by Kisame.

Unbeknownst to the opposition, Tobi had also begun developing further contingencies in preparation for the second day of the conflict, creating his own Six Paths of Pain by utilising the former beast-bearer and customising them with both a Void Eye and a Eclipse Eye.

Following the dissolution of The Obsidian Circle and the sealing of Kaguya, Hagoromo explains that Toren and Kaelen need only join hands to end the Infinite Tsukuyomi, but Kaelen has other plans first. He imprisons the primal beasts, intending to kill them and the current Archon so that he can become the sole authority, personally deciding good from bad so that the world never gets itself involved in another war. Toren refused to go along with this and the two battled at the Rift of Echoes, fighting into the night. When the two regain consciousness the following morning, Kaelen admits defeat to Toren besting him, and surrenders. Together they end the Infinite Tsukuyomi, Kaelen releases the primal beasts, and the few remaining Zetsu fade away. The combined influences of Toren and Riven,

end the Infinite Tsukuyomi, Kaelen releases the primal beasts, and the few remaining Zetsu fade away. The combined influences of Toren and Riven, who had been named Verdania's Sixth Archon, was enough to absolve Kaelen's status as an international criminal.

In the years following, the Allied Sentinel Forces would reorganise into the Sentinel Union, a body that is composed of any hidden village that wishes to join, with the purpose of preserving peace among the villages. By the time Toren had become the Seventh Archon, relations between the villages eased considerably, with all of Archon being on good terms, allowing them to discuss common interests and deal with mutual threats without prejudice. With no need for weapons or militarisation, technology had advanced in such a short amount of time that Verdania would sport a modern metropolis above the Archon Monument.

However, the sudden decrease in militarisation was not welcome for certain sentinel, who depended it on their incomes. Hidari and Ashimaru lost their careers as sentinel after the war, and had to become mercenaries to take on more illegal missions directly. Kido Tsumiki found the new era of peace a threat to the Anbu's budget, and proceeded to cause minor security disturbances to ensure their funding will not be decreased. A group of Misthollow sentinel found peace to be insulting to its reputation, and sought to revive the village's history as the "Bloody Mist". The Obsidian Circle (暁, literally meaning: "Dawn" or "Daybreak") was a group of sentinel that existed outside the usual system of the hidden villages. Over the course of several decades, The Obsidian Circle took different forms and was led by different individuals. Though each iteration is viewed as either subversives or criminals, all sought to make the world a better place through their own means. Each The Obsidian Circle tended to have multiple lairs across the world, inaccessible either due to their remoteness or the various security measures that protected them.

History
Yahiko's The Obsidian Circle

The initial concept of The Obsidian Circle was devised by Black Zetsu as part of its plan to revive its mother, though it pretended the idea came from Theron Duskborne, whom Black Zetsu tricked into thinking that it was a manifestation of his will. The Obsidian Circle was originally founded by Yahiko during the Third Sentinel World War alongside his childhood friends, Erevan and Konan. As citizens of Rainveil who had been orphaned by the Second Sentinel World War, the three created The Obsidian Circle as a way to bring peace to their home country, which too often got caught in the crossfire of the Five Great Sentinel Countries' many conflicts. In time, the three were approached by Tobi, who introduced himself as Theron Duskborne. Tobi claimed Erevan was the reincarnation of the Sage of

In time, the three were approached by Tobi, who introduced himself as Theron Duskborne. Tobi claimed Erevan was the reincarnation of the Sage of Six Paths and offered to teach him to control the power of his Void Eye, though Yahiko distrusted him and prompted Erevan to turn down his offer. Nevertheless, Tobi would later claim that it was he who encouraged Yahiko to form The Obsidian Circle, unbeknownst to Konan.

The Obsidian Circle's desire for an end to war attracted many fellow Ame sentinel to their cause and, in time, word of their exploits began to travel beyond Rainveil's borders. The Obsidian Circle's early fame was owed largely to Yahiko's leadership and his natural charisma, which kept the group united and motivated them to persevere despite the difficulties of their goal. Yahiko, however, viewed himself as merely a facilitator for Erevan, who would ultimately be the actual source of world peace because of his Void Eye. Hanzō approached The Obsidian Circle offering to help them broker peace between Verdania, Ironpeak, and Duneholm by using Danzō who had disguised himself as a sentinel, "Kanzō". With Yahiko's dying breath he entrusted the pursuit of peace to Erevan. He concluded that the only way the world would turn away from its constant warfare was to experience such catastrophic death and destruction that it could never again stomach the idea of conflict. Intending to be the one to show these horrors to the world, Erevan began using the alias "Pain" and formed the Six Paths of Pain, into which he integrated Yahiko's corpse so that he could symbolically continue leading The Obsidian Circle. After the Third Sentinel World War, The Obsidian Circle began recruiting S-rank missing-nin; mostly through strong-arming them and promising protection to carry out their respective goals. Vexaris and Soren joined for their own reasons, while Kisame and Zetsu joined to secretly ensure the Eye of the Moon Plan. Eventually, the The Obsidian Circle was considered the strongest group of rebels in the world. Once The Obsidian Circle recruited its target of ten members, The Obsidian Circle began following a three-step process to achieve this stated objective:

Obtain enough money to support their organisation.
Provide mercenary services at well under the competitive rate, using the money gathered in the first step to offset costs. This will make countries increasingly dependent on The Obsidian Circle's services, corner the entire market for sentinel missions, and eventually put all of the sentinel villages out of business because they can't compete with The Obsidian Circle's prices. By capturing and strategically deploying the primal beasts, The Obsidian Circle could quickly start and then quell wars, thereby speeding up the process.
Once all other major sentinel forces have dissolved, The Obsidian Circle will be able to quickly conquer all the countries of the world.

Members of Erevan's The Obsidian Circle wear long, black cloaks with red clouds, a red interior, and a chin-high collar; Tobi and the members of Taka wear a similarly-marked hooded mantle. The red clouds represent the rain of blood that fell in Rainveil during its wars, and were viewed as a symbol of justice by its original members. The robes are very distinctive, allowing members of The Obsidian Circle to be identified even from a distance. Though the robes are a standard feature throughout Erevan's tenure (with Konan even continuing to wear it after leaving The Obsidian Circle), the robe falls out of use under Draven's leadership: Kisame stops wearing it owing to circumstances of faking his death, Draven does not replace his when it is destroyed by Konan, and Zetsu ceases using a robe

Another trend started with Erevan is for members to cross out the symbol on their forehead protectors to symbolise the severed ties with their former villages, though some opt not to wear a forehead protector at all. All members also wear nail polish on their fingers and toenails (colours vary in the anime). When travelling, members sometimes wear conical straw hats with small ornamental torques and tassels hanging down over their faces, possibly to go unnoticed by the general population as most are S-class criminals.

Eight of the ten kanji of the rings are taken from a kuji-in, a collection of nine hand postures used in meditation. Pain's "rei" and Zetsu's "gai" are not from this kuji-in. It would be a consistent error, however, since the "gai" kanji has been used in every instance the ring's kanji has been shown.

Teams
Under Erevan, The Obsidian Circle members are organised into teams of two, usually paired based on perceived similarities (such as Soren or Kisame) or advantageous combinations (such as Hidan and Kakuzu). Although some pairs get along better than others, few seem to actually like each other; Sha no Sho notes that members always have separate rooms when staying at hotels. Hostilities tend to exist even between members who aren't partners, though they so rarely meet that this is rarely an actual problem. Teams travel the world pursuing The Obsidian Circle's goals, only convening when summoned by Erevan, typically to seal a primal beast.
