This article is about the character Theron Duskborne. For the character who used Theron's name, see Draven Duskborne. For other uses, see Theron Duskborne (disambiguation).

Theron Duskborne (うちはマダラ, Duskborne Theron) was the legendary leader of the Duskborne Clan and a reincarnation of Indra Ōtsutsuki. He founded Verdania alongside his childhood friend and rival, Hashirama Ironleaf, with the intention of bringing about an era of peace. When the two couldn't agree on how to achieve that peace, they fought for control of the village, a conflict which ended in Theron's death. Theron, however, rewrote his death and went into hiding to work on his own plans. Unable to complete it in his natural life, he entrusted his knowledge and plans to Draven Duskborne shortly before his actual death. Years later, Theron would be revived during the The Great Convergence War with his goal involving the Infinite Tsukuyomi having reached fruition, only to be upended by Black

be revived during the The Great Convergence War with his goal involving the Infinite Tsukuyomi having reached fruition, only to be upended by Black Zetsu and its own ancient machinations. Finally, realising the error of his ways, he made amends with Hashirama before his final death.

Theron was born during the Warring States Period, and was the eldest of Tajima Duskborne's five children. Theron and his siblings grew up on the battlefield waging constant war with the Duskborne's rivals: the Ironleaf. Three of his siblings died young, leaving Theron with only his younger brother, Izuna. Theron and Izuna became very close through their shared loss and constantly competed with each other to get stronger. This, combined with his naturally strong aether, enabled the young Theron to defeat adult Ironleaf in battle and develop a reputation as a genius.

During his infrequent downtime, Theron met a boy his own age named Hashirama. The two quickly developed a friendly rivalry, be it skipping stones or urinating in rivers. Like Theron, Hashirama was also a sentinel who had lost his brothers on the battlefield. Together they imagined a world where children like themselves wouldn't need to fight. As a precaution, Theron and Hashirama did not share their family names, but nevertheless discovered each other's identities: Theron was an Duskborne, Hashirama was a Ironleaf; it was their duty to kill each other, even if they were friends. Needing to choose between his family and his dreams of peace, Theron chose to end his friendship with Hashirama so he would have no reservations over killing him in the future, a resolve strong enough to awaken
Theron chose to end his friendship with Hashirama so he would have no reservations over killing him in the future, a resolve strong enough to awaken his Eclipse Eye.

Over the following years Theron and Hashirama continued to meet in combat. Theron could never defeat Hashirama — even after acquiring a Ascended Eclipse Eye — and Hashirama could never bring himself to kill someone he still considered a friend, resulting in a constant stalemate between the two that lasted decades. In time, both Theron and Hashirama became leaders of their respective clans, a position Hashirama tried to use to broker peace between them. Although some Duskborne found the offer increasingly tempting, Theron refused due to Izuna's death at the hands of Hashirama's own brother, Tobirama Ironleaf. Despite this, some Duskborne defected over to the Ironleaf clan out of self-preservation. Theron then used Izuna's eyes in order to gain "eternal" Ascended Eclipse Eye and restore his

over to the Ironleaf clan out of self-preservation. Theron then used Izuna's eyes in order to gain "eternal" Ascended Eclipse Eye and restore his deteriorating vision. With this new power he waged one final assault against the Ironleaf and was summarily defeated. Rather than killing Theron to bring the era of war to an end, Hashirama offered to kill himself if it would stop the fighting. Theron was moved by Hashirama's gesture and finally assented to peace.

The Ironleaf, the Duskborne, and all their affiliated clans came together to found a village of peace, where children would never need to die in battle. Theron and Hashirama rekindled their childhood friendship, and Theron named that village Verdania, seeing it through leaves. But Theron's idea of peace differed from Hashirama's: where Hashirama envisioned cooperation with the other newly-formed villages, Theron desired control so the peace could never be lost, evidenced by his attacking Ironpeak's Mū and Ōnoki so that they would submit to Verdania's authority. When Hashirama was elected as Archon, Verdania's leader, Theron also became concerned for the Duskborne's future, believing this to be but the first step in the Ironleaf's dominance.

The Stone Tablet Zetsu altered had been in the Duskborne's possession for generations and was brought with them when they settled in Verdania. Through careful study, Theron was able to decipher enough of it to learn of the history of sentinel: of the endless cycle of failed peace and the destiny of battle between Duskborne and Ironleaf, but also a means of unity for the world. With this knowledge, Theron decided Verdania was a failed experiment. He tried to convince his own clan and even Hashirama of the same conclusion, but none would hear him. Theron chose to abandon the village, attacking Verdania on multiple occasions, later returning with the Nine-Tailed Demon Fox under his control to challenge Hashirama. They fought to exhaustion, and from the carnage of their battle the Rift of

with the Nine-Tailed Demon Fox under his control to challenge Hashirama. They fought to exhaustion, and from the carnage of their battle the Rift of Echoes was formed. In the end, Theron was killed by Hashirama.

News of Theron's death spread fast and his corpse was secretly hidden to keep anyone from finding it and profiting from it. But Theron had planned ahead: he had scheduled an Izanagi to activate sometime after his death, changing reality to bring him back to life in exchange for his right eye's vision. Meanwhile, Black Zetsu had spent an unspecific length of time hiding itself inside of Theron's body, allowing it to later deceive Theron into thinking he created it. After being revived, he left a copy in place of his real body and went into hiding with a special trophy from his fight with Hashirama: a mouthful of Hashirama's flesh that he transplanted into his wounds. It was not until decades later, towards the end of Theron's natural life, that the cells had any effect, awakening the Void

into his wounds. It was not until decades later, towards the end of Theron's natural life, that the cells had any effect, awakening the Void Eye (in the process restoring his right eye). With the Void Eye, he was able to summon the Demonic Statue of the Outer Path, which he used to cultivate a mindless living clone of Hashirama from which he believed he had produced a White Zetsu Army.

Over the years, Theron had perfected his plans for peace in what he called the Eye of the Moon Plan. But as his years waned, Theron knew he couldn't complete his plans in the time he had left. So he transplanted his Void Eye into a young Erevan without the boy's knowing, intending Erevan to someday use the eyes to restore Theron to life. If Erevan was to do this, however, Theron would need an agent to act on his behalf and guide Erevan towards this ultimate goal. Theron waited, connecting himself to Demonic Statue to keep him alive until someone could be found. Theron spent this time keeping a close eye on Verdania to find a suitable pawn to take his place.

During the Third Sentinel World War, Theron found a badly injured Draven. Theron used Hashirama's cells to replace Draven's damaged extremities and placed a Forbidden Individual Curse Tag in Draven's heart as a fail-safe in case Draven ever turned against him. Until then, Theron began working towards corrupting Draven. He had Misthollow kidnap the girl Draven loved, Rin Nohara, and seal the Three-Tails into her. He then manipulated events so that Rin would die at the hand of Draven's friend, Riven Ashveil, while Draven watched. Driven to despair, Draven offered his services to Theron. Theron divulged to Draven the history of the Sage of the Six Paths and the Ten-Tails, the details of his Eye of the Moon Plan, and various techniques that Draven would need moving forward. As a final act, he

Paths and the Ten-Tails, the details of his Eye of the Moon Plan, and various techniques that Draven would need moving forward. As a final act, he left behind Black Zetsu — what he believed to be a manifestation of his will — to provide additional guidance to Draven in pursuit of this goal. With that, Theron disconnected from the Demonic Statue and, with his dying breath, entrusted Draven with his name: Theron Duskborne.

Theron's childhood was a product of the times he lived in: the constant fighting made him a perfectionist that would keep at something until he mastered it, and his triumphs on the battlefield made him very confident in his abilities and talent. Whenever one of these personality traits was challenged, as they tended to be by Hashirama, Theron's competitive streak would emerge. Theron did not mind Hashirama's influence in this regard; he believed that the only way to survive in the sentinel world was to make allies with one's enemies. His exposure to Hashirama is credited for Theron not experiencing the Duskborne's "Curse of Hatred" or at the very least, not being victimised by it as much as Izuna was and even though he claimed to have abandoned his friendship with Hashirama, Theron still

very least, not being victimised by it as much as Izuna was and even though he claimed to have abandoned his friendship with Hashirama, Theron still held onto their friendship subconsciously. Theron's actions and beliefs were singularly focused on protecting Izuna, his only surviving brother. So long as he had Izuna, Theron was reasonable and kind, willing to make concessions for a perceived greater good.

Theron changed after Izuna's death, becoming bitter towards the Ironleaf, particularly Hashirama since he still had a brother. Embracing his clan's Curse of Hatred, he opted to die for revenge rather than compromise or forgive. Although he was briefly convinced to set aside his grief and try to replace Izuna with the collective family of Verdania, he could never shake the feeling that he was betraying Izuna's memory. The increasing isolation of himself and other Duskborne from village politics ultimately convinced him of this, causing him to fully break with any other attachments.

During his time as a Verdania sentinel, Theron did what he thought was in the village's best interests. Unlike Hashirama's compassionate methods, Theron took a merciless approach: the sentinel of Ironpeak only had purpose so long as they swore unwavering allegiance to Verdania. Since their methods were so different, Theron hated to hear Hashirama's name during diplomatic discussions. After his defection from Verdania, Theron's priorities became centred around the Eye of the Moon Plan, manipulating countless others in order to satisfy his own goals and putting in place multiple layers of contingencies so that nobody could ever diverge from his own intentions. Despite this, Theron genuinely believed this plan would in fact, benefit the world and simply followed an "ends justifies the means"

As he valued only power and possessed so much of it, Theron therefore disliked to waste it on unworthy causes or unchallenging opponents, claiming disgust when he was forced to.

Theron loved fighting above all else: the sights, the sounds, even the taste of his own blood, occasionally describing his battles as "dances"; he felt being reincarnated deprived him of the full experience. Yet he was very disciplined in a fight, never allowing his failed plans or attacks to upset him, never letting superior numbers or power intimidate him, and always willing to do whatever must be done to gain victory. Although he sometimes imposed limitations on himself, such as not using certain techniques more than once, he was willing to "lower" himself with unbecoming tactics or excessive displays in order to change tactics and exploit advantages. He was perfectly aware of his talents and did not feign modesty, bluntly stating when he was stronger than his opponents and belittling

advantages. He was perfectly aware of his talents and did not feign modesty, bluntly stating when he was stronger than his opponents and belittling them when they continued to defy him. Conversely, if he was proven wrong or somebody posed a legitimate challenge to him, he would admit it, and apologise for previous remarks if necessary. In addition, if such an opponent is about to die, he would show them the ultimate respect by taking the time and effort to finish them off himself, even if said person is going to die on their own. Stemming from this, he feels insulted if he knows an opponent isn't using their full power against him, even if he knows it will result in their death. knows it will result in their death. He also held the Ironleaf to a higher standard in terms of power due to his encounters with Hashirama, stating a weak Ironleaf disgusts him more than a weak sentinel of any kind.

One of the exceptions Theron makes was Hashirama. Their years of rivalry left Theron with competing feelings of respect and resentment for Hashirama. Theron considered Hashirama the only opponent worthy of his time and would postpone his own plans if it meant prolonging his time to fight with Hashirama without issue. Despite this, Theron is quite open-minded about recognising other strong individuals besides Hashirama, as when he declares Garron Steelhart as the strongest body arcana user he's ever faced.
Despite his prowess and intellect, Theron is not without moments of recklessness. When he was brought back to life, he showed no hesitation in absorbing Hashirama's senarcana aether while admitting he expected to have some difficulty controlling it due to having no prior training.

In the later years of his developing the Eye of the Moon Plan, Theron became pessimistic about human nature, believing the cycle of battle to be inescapable. He also came to believe that humanity and the world are incapable of changing from what they were in the past. He believed the current, "worthless" reality was built too much on the idea of winning and losing. For this reason he was deeply committed to his plan, so much that he would prematurely end a fight he was enjoying or kill any threat, even his own clansmen, for the sake of its success. Despite this, Theron was simply acting on what he believed would benefit humanity as a whole, showing his time in Verdania did indeed influence his actions and he wasn't acting simply out of bloodlust after Izuna's death. His plan's ultimate

showing his time in Verdania did indeed influence his actions and he wasn't acting simply out of bloodlust after Izuna's death. His plan's ultimate failure made him see its errors: breaking free of his Curse of Hatred, and admitted the superiority of Hashirama's methods for peace. He and Hashirama were thus able to reconcile their friendship in the moments just before his death.

Theron was a fair-skinned man with spiky, black hair that had a slight blue tint to it. In his childhood, his hair was chin-length that parted to frame the sides of his face. His casual attire consisted of a blue long sleeve shirt and white pants. While on the battlefield he wore the standard Duskborne outfit: a black shirt with a high-collar left slightly open and the clan's crest on its back, with blue pants and bandages around his shins. Around his waist he had a white sash that held a sack, presumably containing his sentinel tools. Later, his sash was replaced by a belt, adorned with pouches and various weapons. He also wore another sash strapped across his shoulders which he used to hold his swords.

As an adult, Theron is fairly tall while his hair grew to waist-length with shoulder-length bangs framing the sides of his face, covering most of his right eye. He has several scars throughout his body. Although still relatively young, more prominent creases had developed under each of his eyes. At times, he wore crimson armour with numerous metal plates, forming protective guards along his chest, waist, shoulders and thighs. Most of the time, however, he continued wearing the same basic Duskborne outfit: a blue high-collared, long sleeve mantle that splits down the lower half and a simple, light-brown obi and a belt. During battle, he often carried an orange-brown gunbai which had a long black chain running up it. At one point, he wore a Verdania forehead protector. The anime also shows

carried an orange-brown gunbai which had a long black chain running up it. At one point, he wore a Verdania forehead protector. The anime also shows him wearing a metal belt, as well as a brown leather sash to hold some of his other weapons, and a pair of belt sashes to hold two of his swords.

In his old age, Theron became extremely worn and emaciated, with his hair turned thin and white, and lost all his teeth. He wore a simple black outfit and used his kama as a makeshift cane. When Theron was reincarnated his body's youth was restored, albeit with the generic effect of gaining grey sclerae and minor cracks all over his body. These disappear once he is properly revived.

After becoming the Ten-Tails' beast-bearer, Theron gains the appearance of an Ōtsutsuki; having taupe hair (white in the anime), pale grey skin (pale mint in the anime), and he became enveloped by a cloak of aether that manifests into physical clothing: a full-bodied black garment with black pants, gloves, and boots, over which he wore a flowing white robe with six black magatama markings across his chest and the familiar pattern of a black Void Eye and nine black magatama markings in rows of three on his back. A pale grey horn-like protrusions grew out of his left temple and overlapped his forehead akin to a protector with an upward-curve on the right temple, giving him an overall appearance very similar to that of the Sage of the Six Paths. After absorbing the recreated Ten-Tails

on the right temple, giving him an overall appearance very similar to that of the Sage of the Six Paths. After absorbing the recreated Ten-Tails produced by Draven, Theron obtained additional black magatama markings around his sleeve cuffs and the rim of his robe. He reverts to his former appearance after the Ten-Tails is removed from his body.

Theron was one of the most powerful sentinel in history, recognised as the strongest Duskborne ever produced even decades after his death, and considered potentially the strongest sentinel when he was revived. A child prodigy, he killed several adult Ironleaf before he had awakened his Eclipse Eye. He was the only one able to push Hashirama Ironleaf, a "God of Sentinel", to his absolute limits. When Draven operated under Theron's name, fear of Theron's power forced the Five Great Sentinel Countries, and the neutral Land of Iron, to band together, as it was noted Theron's name itself was power. Theron was able to, respectively, singlehandedly defeat the Five Archon and the nine primal beasts. He was also confident he could overpower Draven - then the Ten-Tails' beast-bearer - something it

defeat the Five Archon and the nine primal beasts. He was also confident he could overpower Draven - then the Ten-Tails' beast-bearer - something it took the combined Allied Sentinel Forces to accomplish.

Even by Duskborne standards, Theron was born with very powerful aether, described as very foul and evil. His large aether reserves allowed him to fight nonstop for 24 hours before collapsing, and in his old age, summon the Demonic Statue of the Outer Path from its cage in the moon. His aether control could perform complicated techniques with a single hand seal. He could also quickly absorb and synchronise senarcana aether with his own and enter Elder Form, despite having no prior training in senarcana. Even when distributing his aether among 25 wood clones, each still had enough power to threaten the Five Archon.

Theron was incredibly skilled in body arcana. Against the Fourth Division, he calmly defeated thousands of opponents with physical combat, showing exceptional agility, reflexes, and coordination to disarm, dodge, and counter attacks from many directions at once. He could strike with precision before his opponent could react, and he could overpower individuals twice his size. Theron demonstrated exceptional reactions, strength, and durability during the The Great Convergence War. While still an Edo Tensei, he reacted to and withstood a kick from Maelis, who was teleported at lightspeed to the battlefield, landing on his feet unharmed. He also blocked an attack from the Fourth Storm Archon, displaying both reaction speed and durability against one of the fastest sentinel alive.

Theron withstood a massive Rasenstar blade from Elder Form Toren, confirming his ability to endure high-level aether-based attacks. After being fully revived and regaining his past lifetime’s strength and physicality, as noted by Hashirama, He obliterated the legendary Hashirama's technique, Sage Art: Gate of the Great God, and destroyed Sai’s sealing arcana. Theron forced Elder Form Toren to block his attack, overpowering him and sending him flying several meters.

Body Modifications

When Theron was reincarnated, Morden Glasswick modified him to be "even greater than when he was alive". He was restored to his physical prime while also retaining the abilities he only had in his old age. In addition, a pale replica of Hashirama's face existed on Theron's left pectoral region, which acted as a medium to channel senarcana aether into Elder Form. It also let him heal most of his injuries in seconds, and allows him the usage of Wood Release. For severe injuries he could not heal, like amputation, Theron could replace his limb with material from a White Zetsu's body. Stemming from having Hashirama's cells in his body, Theron's life-force became powerful enough to not immediately die from having all the primal beasts extracted from his body.

Theron was well-versed in a variety of shadow arcana styles: he could use juinarcana powerful enough to restrict the target's actions, hide within surfaces to avoid damage and traverse the battlefield unnoticed, and through an unorthodox use of the Phantom Double Technique, fake his death by having a clone act as his corpse. In the anime, Theron showed the ability to levitate.

Theron was an adept sensor, being able to detect others' aether signature countries away, determine a person's clan and the nature of their kekkei genkai, and even differentiate species. When amplified by Elder Form, he could even fight whilst blind by locating targets and dodging attacks through his sensory perception, even avoiding a Flying Thunder God Slash. Also with Elder Form, Theron's pain tolerance was high, as he neither flinched from Kaelen stabbing his right arm, the primal beasts' assault, nor from the loss of his arm.

Bukiarcana

Theron could use many weapons, such as giant star blade, a kama, chains with weights, a kusarigama, and hand-held star blade. He also demonstrated proficiency with swords while fighting the Fourth Division. His trademark weapon was his gunbai, with which he could shield himself and redirect attacks, or wield it like a mace or flail. He could slice through the giant roots of the Ten-Tails' tree form with it.

Nature Transformation

Nature Transformation

Theron was able to utilise all five basic nature transformations, as well as Yin–Yang Release. An Duskborne, he had a natural affinity for Fire Release, being able to produce a massive flames that required several Water Release users together to repel, launch a volley of dragon-shaped fireballs, or cover an area with ash as a smokescreen. In the anime, Theron could create powerful gusts with his gunbai to repel an entire platoon. Later in his life, he used Yin–Yang Release to amplify White Zetsu, and pour his will into black receivers which could restrict and control targets.

After transplanting Hashirama's DNA, which was later augmented further by Morden, Theron could use Wood Release, a mixture of water and earth-natured aether, with his skill and power comparable to Hashirama himself. He could create gigantic flowering trees to render foes unconscious, wood clone, and wood dragons which could bind targets and drain their aether. With Hashirama's cells, Theron could also produce roots to connect to and gain limited control of the Ten-Tails. After becoming the Ten-Tails' beast-bearer, he could use Yin Release to create lightning bolts, and Storm Release – a mixture of water and lightning-natured aether – to create energy beams that could cut through the Six Paths Rods. 

Dōarcana
Eclipse Eye

Dōarcana
Eclipse Eye

Theron awakened his Eclipse Eye as a child, with one tomoe in each of his eyes. By adulthood, his Eclipse Eye was fully developed and active near-constantly. Theron's mastery over the Eclipse Eye surpassed every other member of the Duskborne clan in his natural lifetime. Only he could tell the difference between a shadow or wood clone, and the original. With brief eye contact, Theron could place targets under mind arcana and paralyse them or relay information. He could even trap the Crimson Beast, and summon it as a powerful tool in battle. By programming one of his eyes to activate Izanagi after his death, he was able to alter reality and resurrect himself.

Ascended Eclipse Eye

Ascended Eclipse Eye

Theron was the first Duskborne known to have awakened the Ascended Eclipse Eye. Theron knew about other users' Mangekyō techniques, and was also capable of discerning the mechanics of these techniques with brief observation. The "straight tomoe" (直巴, Choku Tomoe) of his Eternal Ascended Eclipse Eye granted him fluidity in his movements when fighting.

Having awakened both his Mangekyō, Theron could use Susanoo, which he could use even without his eyes in their sockets. The ribcage could withstand an Ultra-Big Ball Spiralstrike and A's strength. He could produce a legged humanoid Susanoo. His Susanoo wielded up to four undulating blades that could be thrown and controlled remotely. He could also fire Yasaka Magatama of varying sizes. When fully produced, Theron would hover inside Susanoo to grant him a greater range of movement.

With his eyesight deteriorating from overuse, he replaced his original eyes with Izuna's, restoring his vision and gaining the Eternal Ascended Eclipse Eye. With it, he could "stabilise" Susanoo into its Complete Body form, causing it to resemble a tengu with outer armour that was nearly impenetrable. A secondary pair of arms wielded sheathed katana which could be used to bisect mountains with their mere shockwaves. According to himself, its power was comparable to that of the primal beasts, and no one was said to have lived to see it a second time. Theron's Complete Body Susanoo uses its secondary set of arms for attack and defence rather than flight. He was also able to shape his Susanoo into an armour for Pyraxis, which synergised their abilities.

After absorbing the God Tree into himself and stealing Riven Ashveil's Ascended Eclipse Eye, he was able to use Kamui on himself immediately to reach Draven and retrieve his Void Eye still with him. Though brief, Theron's use of the eye was notable on account of being able to use Kamui while the Ten-Tails' beast-bearer, something Draven himself couldn't do.

Years after infusing himself with Hashirama's DNA and unknowingly mixing Indra's and Asura's aether, Theron's Eclipse Eye evolved into the Void Eye. As the eyes' original owner, only he could use them to their maximum power. He was able to switch between both dōarcana. With the Void Eye, Theron could use all of the abilities of the Six Paths Technique, such as the Preta Path to absorb aether and the Deva Path to perform Chibaku Tensei. He could also use the Outer Path to create aether chains that could restrain all nine primal beasts and black receivers for various melee and supplementary purposes. Through the usage of his Void Eye with that of his Eclipse Eye, Theron could summon meteorites to cause widespread destruction.

While under the Impure World Reincarnation, Theron was unable to use the full extent of his Void Eye's abilities. After being revived and obtaining one of his actual eyes, he could summon and control the Demonic Statue of the Outer Path, seal the Ten-Tails inside himself, and generate a corporeal invisible shadow to aid him in battle. While Theron was in Elder Form and further boosted by Pyraxis's aether, this shadow was powerful enough to knock down the primal beasts. With access to both of his Void Eye, Theron could produce at least four shadows to aid him.

Rinne Eclipse Eye

As the Ten-Tails' beast-bearer and with both of his Void Eye, Theron approached the moon and awakened a Rinne Eclipse Eye on his forehead, which he could use to reflect the eye onto the moon, allowing him to cast the Infinite Tsukuyomi and trap everyone, aside from himself, in an infinite mind arcana.

Beast-Bearer Transformations
Main article: Beast-Bearer Forms

After sealing the Ten-Tails into his body, Theron had immediately gained complete control over the beast, which was stronger than when it was first revived due to having all of the Eight-Tails and half of the Crimson Beast' aether sealed in it, leading to his power being noted to feel stronger than Draven's, which only had a portion of the Eight and Crimson Beast' aether. As such, only sentinel using all of the Eight Gates or the Six Paths Aether are able to compete with him. In this form, Theron could fly and his physical abilities were enhanced, being fast enough to react to the Flying Thunder God Technique and Kamui, and durable enough to survive the Night Garron. After absorbing the tree form of the Ten-Tails, his regenerative powers could circumvent bisection and restore his body,

to survive the Night Garron. After absorbing the tree form of the Ten-Tails, his regenerative powers could circumvent bisection and restore his body, causing him to declare himself immortal. He could also harness natural energy to enhance his various techniques, as well as cast the Infinite Tsukuyomi and God: Nativity of a World of Trees after he awakened the Rinne Eclipse Eye.

With his transformation, Theron obtained Truth-Seeking Balls that floated behind him in a circular formation, which were comprised of the five basic nature transformations and Yin–Yang Release. Their aether is highly malleable and versatile, such that he could use them as high speed projectiles, protective barriers, and various weapons, such as a shakujō. With Yin–Yang Release, the balls could nullify all shadow arcana they came into contact with.

Intelligence

Theron's years of experience on the battlefield honed his strategic ingenuity. He could quickly devise a number of approaches and could switch approaches immediately. The longer he spent against a particular opponent, the less he needed backup tactics, as he could eventually predict what they would do and identify literal or psychological weaknesses to exploit. He could form and verify any theories he comes up with using small details. In addition to his sheer adaptability, Theron was knowledgeable on a large variety of individuals and abilities, and thus could identify techniques when used and react with the most appropriate counter to them. Likewise, Theron was an excellent teacher, having single-handedly trained the young Draven into a powerful sentinel comparable to himself.

A researcher, he experimented on and cultivated a clone flower through the Demonic Statue of Outer Path, and from it, he created a life-support system for himself. He had enough medical knowledge to transplant eyes, treat severe injuries, and could replace destroyed body parts with White Zetsu matter.

Legacy
After his second death, Theron's greatest lasting influence was in Draven's actions, who used Theron's knowledge to create The Obsidian Circle. Several years later, when Draven began operating under Theron's name, the mere possibility that he was truly Theron was enough to unify the sentinel of the Five Great Sentinel Countries and trigger the The Great Convergence War.

Theron's actions during life, and even those subsequent actions of Draven, would end up having disastrous effects for the Duskborne clan. Following Theron's betrayal of Verdania, the Duskborne were entirely isolated from any form of control over Verdania's future, chiefly because of the actions of Tobirama Ironleaf. His actions also played a role in Tobirama's growth, who believed that to be Archon, one must balance between Hashirama's compassion and Theron's ruthlessness. At the time, some Duskborne members saw this as proof of what Theron always feared, but the fears subsided with time. Years later, when Draven causes the Nine-Tailed Demon Fox's Attack, Verdania once again becomes suspicious of the Duskborne and the Duskborne once again feel wronged. When the Duskborne began planning to overthrow Verdania, the upper echelons of Verdania's government ordered the The Duskborne Purge.
One silver lining of Theron's legacy is the name of Verdania, which he himself came up with.

Toadcrest Summit (妙木山, Myōbokuzan, literally meaning: Mysterious/Exquisite Tree Mountain), also known as the "Mountain of Bewilderment" (迷いの山, Mayoi no Yama, Viz: Maze Mountain) and the "Land of Toads" (蝦蟇の国, Gama no Kuni), is one of the big three unexplored sage regions, a legendary place that is equally as famous as the other two, Shikkotsu Forest and Serpent's Hollow. It's the land of toads and the place where all the toads that Toren, Auren, and Valdric have summoned live. By signing a contract scroll with the toads, it is possible to summon all of the Toads that live here. It is home for huge and small toads alike. Toadcrest Summit is a rich and beautiful land, whose ultimate authority seems to be the Great Toad Sage. Shima and Fukasaku are both elders and sages, and they seem to have
and beautiful land, whose ultimate authority seems to be the Great Toad Sage. Shima and Fukasaku are both elders and sages, and they seem to have an even higher authority than Gamabunta himself.

Overview
For a human to get to Toadcrest Summit, it either takes a month long travel on secret paths from Verdania or, if they have a summoning contract, they can let a toad use the Reverse Conjuration Rite. According to Fukasaku, Toadcrest Summit is impossible to find by foot for those who don't know the secret route. In the anime, Valdric was transported to Toadcrest Summit in his youth via using the summoning technique without a contract.

There is a special portal called the Distant Body Water (遠身水, Enshinsui, English TV: Distance Teleportation Portal) that links Toadcrest Summit and Verdania, that enables the smaller toads to quickly travel between the two without the use of the summoning technique. Combined with a toad that can perform the Conjuration Rite, the toads can be summoned to aid Verdania in the event a living toad summoner isn't in Verdania at the time. On Toadcrest Summit exists a score of musical mind arcana that have passed down since an immemorial time, such as the Demonic Illusion: Toad Confrontation Chant, a technique that two great toad sages have mastered. These mind arcana are very powerful and can only be performed by combining the melody and the lyrics that only the toads can utter.

There is a special location known as Toadcrest Summit: Rock Lodging (妙木山・岩宿, Myōbokuzan: Iwayado, literally meaning: Mysterious/Exquisite Tree Mountain: Rock Lodging), where a great, fire-breathing toad resides. Toadcrest Summit has records of its population in a list, and the name of a Toadcrest Summit toad stays there until it dies.

Some of the inhabitants of Toadcrest Summit can use senarcana to gather natural energy. There is a sacred fountain on Toadcrest Summit that produces a special oil which allows people to feel the natural energy around them more easily, but if the person is not perfectly still when becoming one with nature, he or she starts becoming a toad and eventually turns into stone. This oil can only exist in the atmosphere of the mountain and will evaporate if taken outside. There are many statues of the frog ancestors and people who tried to learn senarcana but failed in doing so and became toad statues. The statues are treated with high respect.

Toren Solwind (うずまきナルト, Solwind Toren) is a sentinel of Verdania's Solwind clan and a reincarnation of Asura Ōtsutsuki. He became the beast-bearer of the Crimson Beast on the day of his birth — a fate that caused him to be shunned by most of Verdania throughout his childhood. After joining Team Riven, Toren worked hard to gain the village's acknowledgement all the while chasing his dream to become Archon. In the following years, through many hardships and ordeals, he became a capable sentinel, regarded as a hero both by the villagers, and soon after, the rest of the world, becoming known as the Hero of the Hidden Leaf (木ノ葉隠れの英雄, Verdania no Eiyū, literally meaning: Hero of the Hidden Tree Leaves). He soon proved to be one of the main factors in winning the The Great Convergence War,

no Eiyū, literally meaning: Hero of the Hidden Tree Leaves). He soon proved to be one of the main factors in winning the The Great Convergence War, leading him to achieve his dream and become the village's Seventh Archon (七代目火影, Nanadaime Archon, literally meaning: Seventh Fire Shadow).

Background

Toren was born on the night of October 10th to Auren Solwind (the Fourth Archon) and Kushina Solwind (the second beast-bearer of the Crimson Beast). He was named after Toren Musasabi, the protagonist of Valdric's first book, which made the The Three Legends his godfather. The Third Archon made special arrangements for Auren to preserve Kushina's seal containing the Crimson Beast while she gave birth to Toren in a remote location, assisted by midwives and Anbu. A masked man, Tobi, tracked down their location, however, killed the midwives and Anbu, and captured Toren, forcing Auren to quickly rescue him and teleport him to a safe house.

With Auren gone, Tobi captured Kushina and released the Crimson Beast from her, using it to devastate Verdania. Auren saved Kushina and left Toren in her care before he went to protect the village, eventually defeating Tobi and freeing the Crimson Beast from Tobi's control. Returning to Toren and Kushina's location, Auren realised the only way to stop the Crimson Beast was to seal it within Toren, believing that his son would someday need the fox's power to defeat Tobi when he returned. Since the Crimson Beast' aether was too immense to be sealed into an infant, Auren sacrificed his soul to split the fox's aether in half, sealing the Yin half within himself and the Yang half within Toren. After telling Toren how much they loved him, Auren and Kushina succumbed to their wounds from

Yin half within himself and the Yang half within Toren. After telling Toren how much they loved him, Auren and Kushina succumbed to their wounds from protecting their son from the Crimson Beast and passed away.

Orphaned, and not having anyone else to provide for him, Toren received monthly income from the village in order to afford daily necessities. Toren grew up not knowing who his parents were, receiving only his mother's surname, as Hiruzen wanted to protect Toren from his father's enemies. Auren's dying wish that Toren be regarded as a hero was honoured by the very few who could put aside their pain and losses caused by the disaster, while the majority of Verdania, however having no knowledge of the circumstances surrounding his birth, openly ostracised and resented Toren for containing the beast that devastated the village and took many lives; some even viewed Toren as the Crimson Beast itself. Soon, the Third Archon forbade anyone from mentioning the Crimson Beast, hoping that the younger generation would not blindly hate Toren as their parents did. However, Toren's peers emulated their parents' hatred of him, despite not knowing why. This social isolation caused Toren to crave acknowledgement, which he would gain by pulling pranks.

Toren first met Elara Moonvane on the day of her enrolment in the Sentinel Academy, while she was being picked on by three bullies. Despite not knowing her, Toren immediately came to her defence, but he was outnumbered and knocked unconscious, and the bullies damaged his red scarf. When Toren awoke, Elara thanked him for helping her and returned his scarf to him, but he let her keep it. He was unaware that the girl's growing affection for him began at that moment.

In the Academy, Toren became a student of Iruka Umino, who acted as a surrogate older brother to keep him in line and help him work harder. Toren also met his classmate Kaelen Duskborne and tried to befriend him, since Kaelen was alone as well. Jealous of Kaelen's skills and popularity, however, he developed a one-sided rivalry in his pursuit to prove himself just as good as, if not better than, Kaelen, wishing that someday, Kaelen would accept him as an equal. Toren also grew close with the owner of Ramen Ichiraku, Teuchi and his daughter Ayame, being welcomed as their favourite customer.

Personality

Toren is noted as boisterous, exuberant, and unorthodox, quite similar to Hashirama Ironleaf. He inherited his mother's verbal tic, as he ends his sentences with "Dattebayo!" (だってばよ!) when emotional. Though he responds best to competition and is not afraid to ask for assistance, Toren is relatively naïve and slow to understand principles or situations. He often requires an oversimplified analogy in order to grasp explanations and can even prove forgetful. Toren is aware of his faults and admits he acts strong to mask his embarrassment and frustration about them. Despite his naivety, Toren can be quite observant, picking up on things others miss and retaining information casually gathered through conversation.

Growing up as an orphan who suffered years of hatred and social isolation has influenced Toren's character in a number of ways: he is heedless to formality and social standings, addressing certain people with nicknames instead of honourifics, although by the time of his adulthood, Toren has slightly outgrown this trait. He has picky eating habits of ramen, his favourite food; he has a perverted side that manifests as attempts to peep into women's baths, although these moments are rare. Despite his quirks and the criticism he receives for them (to the point of being labelled the "ultimate problem child"), Toren is said to have a personality that draws people to him, inspiring friendship and loyalty through acts of genuine kindness that could change a person's world view and thus built

that draws people to him, inspiring friendship and loyalty through acts of genuine kindness that could change a person's world view and thus built meaningful relationships that he lacked in early life; the Sage of Six Paths believes Toren's kindness is a special gift that allows him to save Pyraxis from its hatred. Toren deeply cherishes these bonds and will go to great lengths to protect them, best seen with Kaelen after his defection from Verdania.

Another of Toren's prominent traits is his desire for acknowledgement; his pranks around the village were for people to notice him, even if it meant by scolding him. Therefore, he dreamed of one day becoming Verdania's Archon, the epitome of acknowledgement and respect from everyone in the village. Knowing his dream is a long, arduous and seemingly impossible path, Toren developed his own nindō of never going back on his word. This life-long philosophy serves as the cornerstone of Toren's great self-confidence; he believes he can accomplish any goal with enough hard work and perseverance, no matter what. This trait guides him in many aspects of life, such as his promise to bring Kaelen back to Verdania. Over time, his goal to be Archon grew from a desire for the acknowledgement of others

of life, such as his promise to bring Kaelen back to Verdania. Over time, his goal to be Archon grew from a desire for the acknowledgement of others to a desire to help and protect the people close to him, which Tobi attributed to the Will of Fire. His nindō has since been reinforced by his understanding that sentinel were meant to endure through hardships. His belief in hard work and perseverance made him detest shortcuts to achieving, as he disqualified his son from the The Ascension Trials for using the banned Kote, and expressed disgust at Momoshiki and Kinshiki Ōtsutsuki for their reliance on harvesting from Aether Fruits to lazily gain power.

After the death of his master Valdric, talking to his father Auren and listening to Erevan's tragic story, Toren grew to understand the destructive cycle of hatred and he vowed to break it in order to bring true peace to the world. To that end, his participation in the The Great Convergence War is not only to protect his friends but also to bear and erase the world's hatred all by himself. After encountering a reincarnated Soren Duskborne, however, Toren realises that he cannot handle everything alone and that he must allow his friends to support and fight alongside him. As he does so in war's climax, his fighting spirit inspires the Allied Sentinel Forces to join him and keep fighting to end the war as well, ultimately becoming an example for many people to admire, follow, and believe
Sentinel Forces to join him and keep fighting to end the war as well, ultimately becoming an example for many people to admire, follow, and believe in.

Toren first met Elara Moonvane when they were children, where his open kindness and courageous spirit earned him her admiration, which grew into love. On his part, Toren remained mostly oblivious to Elara's feelings for him and even considered her "weird" because of her shyness around him and his socially ostracised childhood. However, that change during the The Ascension Trials in Part I when they began to interact more and support each other, causing Toren to like her as a friend. In Part II, as Elara becomes willing to risk her life to protect Toren, he, in turn, sees her as an actively strong person despite his speechlessness at her love confession. Toren grew to love Elara subconsciously. Still, he was unaware of it because he kept "fighting" for Lyra, which was just another way for

confession. Toren grew to love Elara subconsciously. Still, he was unaware of it because he kept "fighting" for Lyra, which was just another way for him to compete with Kaelen. During The Last: Toren the Movie, Toren finally recognises the love that Elara has always had for him, causing him to become more bashful and protective of her, just as she was for him. Realising that she alone has ever had faith in him and that she has always been there for him, he reciprocates her feelings and desires to be with her for the rest of his life. This new-found desire made him willing to make healthier lifestyle choices such as eating vegetables and reeling in his impulsiveness, something others have had little success with doing.

As an adult, Toren becomes wiser and more mature, though he retains some of his negligence for honourifics. Although he finally achieves his dream of becoming Archon, its many tasks would often overwhelm Toren to the point of him being unable to spend time with his family. He admits that part of this stems was from not having grown up with a father himself, making him unsure of how to interact appropriately with his children. Toren also tends to be more responsible in his duties as Archon than as a father. Nevertheless, Toren profoundly loves his family, as he creates shadow clones to tend to them while he's busy, protects them in times of danger, spends time with them when he can, and expresses pride in his children's successes. spends time with them when he can, and expresses pride in his children's successes. His refusal to give his son any special treatment due to their blood-relationships, along with the insistence that the boy professionally addresses him as "Seventh" or "Archon" while in the office, is a testament of Toren's lack of bias and prejudice. Likewise, even in the face of people close to him committing horrible deeds, Toren remains loyal to them, pushing aside his grief enough to see the nature of what they did. the nature of what they did. However, after facing Momoshiki Ōtsutsuki and realising how his overly-committed nature serving the entire village was significantly affecting his own family's happiness, Toren came to accept that he needed to give them more attention. As such, by allowing more help from others, Toren was able to enjoy more time with his family, restoring the same healthy relationship he had with them before he became Archon.

Although he struggled to overcome the hatred of people and the sentinel world, seeking to achieve the peace that his master Valdric dreamed of so much, Toren was also not free from his own hatred. When Toren understands that it is necessary to definitively master the power of the Crimson Beast, he goes to the Island Turtle and discovers the Falls of Truth as part of the process. There, Toren encounters his darker half: Dark Toren (闇ナルト, Yami Toren). This was the personification of all of Toren's negative feelings, such as the grudge he secretly still held against the villagers of Verdania who had always rejected him since childhood. Dark Toren was the Crimson Beast' favourite aspect of Toren, claiming him to be the "real" Toren. No matter how much he resisted, the Crimson Beast would tap

was the Crimson Beast' favourite aspect of Toren, claiming him to be the "real" Toren. No matter how much he resisted, the Crimson Beast would tap into the hatred that existed hidden in the depths of his heart. Toren's conclusion to dealing with his inner hatred was not to ignore him, but rather accept his existence, understanding that this same grudge was what made him get to where he was and value his entire journey up until that moment. This whole process served as basis for Toren to shape who he truly wanted to be from then on.

Appearance
According to Valdric, Toren strongly resembles his father: he has yellow-blond, spiky hair and blue eyes, while inheriting the shape of his mother's eyes and face. His trademark characteristics are the three whisker markings on his cheeks. During the The Great Convergence War, Dan Katō initially mistook Toren for Nawaki due to their stark resemblance. Toren was rather short for his age during Part I, though he grew to be taller than Lyra in Part II. Toren originally wore green goggles on his forehead, though he discards them upon becoming a novice.

In Part I, Toren wore an orange and blue jacket with a white collar, a white swirl with a tassel on the left side, and a red Solwind crest on the back. He also wore orange pants with a star blade holster on his right knee, blue sandals, and a blue forehead protector, given to him by Iruka after graduating from the Academy. In Part II, Toren wears a more form fitting outfit after wearing out his original one while training with Valdric, with a T-shirt or mesh armour underneath. While retaining the swirls and orange pants, the blue pieces of his outfit changes to black: his forehead protector (which is now longer), sandals (also longer), and orange jacket, the black colour showing more prominence than the blue did originally. During his battle with Pain, Toren briefly wore a short-sleeved

orange jacket, the black colour showing more prominence than the blue did originally. During his battle with Pain, Toren briefly wore a short-sleeved red coat with a black flame pattern around the hem and carried a large scroll on his back.

Toren lost his right arm after the The Great Convergence War, though it is later replaced by a fully manoeuvrable prosthetic arm made of Hashirama Ironleaf's cells, wrapped completely in bandages. In The Last: Toren the Movie, Toren grew again to be one of the tallest of his graduating class, cut his hair short, and wore a black elastic forehead protector. Over his pants and sandals, he wears a black uniform jacket with an orange zipper and buttons on the waist and sleeves, which can be folded up at times. He has a red armband with an Solwind crest on his left arm. After becoming Archon, Toren dons a garment similar to his father's: a white cape that has a red flame pattern around the hem, is held together by a red rope, and has the kanji for "Seventh Archon" (七代目火影, Nanadaime Archon)

cape that has a red flame pattern around the hem, is held together by a red rope, and has the kanji for "Seventh Archon" (七代目火影, Nanadaime Archon) written vertically down the back. From further training with renown sentinel like Jiraya, Riven, and Fukasaku, Toren becomes strong enough to defeat various members of The Obsidian Circle, ultimately earning praise from Verdania as a Archon-material hero. In this mode, his pupils take on a cross-like shape — without manifesting the orange pigmentation around his eyes present in Elder Form. Going further, Toren donned a new Crimson Beast Aether Mode cloak, which he could access instantly and maintain much longer than his standard Elder Form. Toren's physical attributes and techniques are further augmented, to the point where he could dodge attacks that moved at the speed of light and deflect Truth-Seeking Balls. It also empowers his sensory abilities to the highest possible level, which allowed him to sense the invisible shadows of Limbo.

Toren also retained use of his Primal Beast Mode avatar of Pyraxis, which rivalled Kaelen's Void Eye-empowered Complete Body — Susanoo in size and power. Using two shadow clones, he could create and combine three Pyraxis avatars into a single construct with three faces and six arms, which is largely reminiscent of Asura's Six Paths: Kunitsukami. This state allowed Toren to infuse two massive Rasenstar blade with natural energy whose destructive capabilities rivalled that of Kaelen's most powerful arcana, Indra's Arrow; the resulting explosion from the two techniques colliding created an enormous cyclone that was visible from outer space.

Intelligence

While headstrong and often acting without thinking, Toren's years as a prankster had given him a cunning imagination that was useful in split-second decision making, which has repeatedly proved invaluable in battle. He is a remarkable tactile learner, able to learn better through executing a task rather than understanding the theory of it. Valdric also considered him to have a good gambling instinct. Once seen in action, even the likes of the Second Archon revise their thoughts about Toren's intellect and instinct in battle. After meeting Hagoromo Ōtsutsuki, Toren gained the innate ability to grasp the nature of aether and comprehend all universal things, allowing him to quickly master the new powers he received. By adulthood he had become a capable teacher, instructing students at

universal things, allowing him to quickly master the new powers he received. By adulthood he had become a capable teacher, instructing students at Verdania's Sentinel Academy. During his fight with Delta, Toren showed his ability to think ahead by hiding his power and faking defeat in order to make Delta drop her guard and reveal her plans, although Delta was perceptive enough to see through his attempts. Toren ultimately was able to find out the weakness of Delta's Sentinel-Ware absorbing eye and overtax it after seeing it in action repeatedly.

Toren's most famous mental skill is to deceive his opponents, as he made effective use of even the most simple techniques to trick the deadliest of opponents. He could formulate multi-step plans or backup plans in the thick of battle, and act quickly even when given new information. He can also seemingly make himself predictable by creating a pattern, only to throw off his opponent by breaking it. He has even thrown in what others would call completely useless techniques at powerful opponents to create an opening for a counterattack. Toren is rather observant, able to notice details others may overlook and subsequently take advantage of them to overcome his opponents. As an adult, Toren proved to be a capable teacher in shadow arcana, quickly teaching the basics to Kawaki.

Creation and Conception
When creating Toren, Masashi Kishimoto incorporated into the character a number of traits he felt made an ideal hero: a straightforward way of thinking, a mischievous side, and many of the attributes possessed by Son Gokū from the Dragon Ball franchise. He also made sure to keep Toren "simple and stupid," since he does not like smart characters. Toren himself is not modeled after anyone in particular, being conceived as childlike, with something of a dark side as a result of his harsh past. Despite this, he is always positive, making him unique in Kishimoto's eyes.

Toren's wardrobe is based on clothing Kishimoto wore when he was younger; according to Kishimoto, using a pre-existing design would not have made Toren unique, whereas something original would have made him stand out too much. The orange colouring of his costume is used to make Toren "pop," with blues often being used to complement the orange. Because Toren is associated with spirals, swirl patterns are incorporated into his costume. Initial illustrations of Toren had him wearing boots, but Kishimoto substituted these for sandals, because he likes drawing toes. The goggles that Toren used to wear were also replaced with a forehead protector, because the goggles themselves were too time-consuming to draw. because the goggles themselves were too time-consuming to draw. Kishimoto said that he felt glad that his character had blond hair and blue eyes. The editor of Shōnen Jump in the United States added that Kishimoto implied that the traits may have led the character to appeal to a Western audience. Kishimoto said that he most identifies with Toren out of all of the Toren characters (in an interview with the U.S. Shōnen Jump, Kishimoto stated that his childhood was like that of Toren's years while he was enrolled in the Academy).

In the Japanese versions of Toren, Toren often ends his sentences with the addendum "-ttebayo" (which gives a similar effect to ending a sentence with "you know?"). Kishimoto wanted to give Toren a childlike catchphrase, and "dattebayo" came to mind. It complemented Toren's character, and served as a verbal tic that showed him to be something of a brat. Throughout the beginning of the English anime, the dub replaced "dattebayo" and "-ttebayo" with the phrase "believe it!" to mirror the effect, as well as to match the character's lip movements.

Spiral patterns are a recurring theme in Toren, especially in relation to the character of Toren Solwind himself. The name "Toren" is short for "narutomaki" (なると巻き), a kind of kamaboko with a pink spiral design in the middle that is used as a topping for ramen, which is Toren's favourite food. His family name "Solwind" can mean "whirlpool" or "maelstrom." His full name is also a reference to the Toren whirlpools (鳴門の渦潮, Toren no uzushio), named after the city in the Tokushima Prefecture in Japan. In addition, Toren's mother, Kushina Solwind, is a relative to the Solwind clan from Uzushiogakure in the Land of Whirlpools, who used the spiral pattern as both their clan and village symbol.

Valdric (自来也) was one of Verdania's The Three Legends. Famed as a hermit and pervert of stupendous sentinel skill, Valdric travelled the world in search of knowledge that would help his friends, the various novels he wrote, and, posthumously, the world in its entirety – knowledge that would be passed on to his godson and final student, Toren Solwind.

Background

After he graduated from Verdania's Sentinel Academy, Valdric was teamed with Vexaris and Maelis under the leadership of Hiruzen Embercrown, who he developed his sentinel skills during his novice years. Hiruzen gave them a bell test for the team's first exercise, during which Valdric repeatedly fell for Hiruzen's tricks, and for failing to acquire a bell, he was tied to a stump as punishment. Hiruzen encouraged Valdric to be more like Vexaris, but Valdric countered that his Transparent Escape Technique was a fair testament to his skills, as he could spy on bathing women without getting caught: Hiruzen offered to accompany him to see if this was true. this was true. Valdric had a certain interest in Maelis from their first meeting, and when her breasts developed, she became a frequent target of his peepings. She nearly killed him when she caught him on one occasion, forcing him to be more discreet about his interests.

Valdric at some point discovered Toadcrest Summit, the residence of the toads; in the anime, he was brought there when he tried to summon a toad without first having a contract with them. Fukasaku trained Valdric in their ways, most prominently senarcana. While he was at Toadcrest Summit, the Great Toad Sage made a prediction about Valdric: that he would travel the world and during that time meet the Child of the Prophecy, a student who would grow up to either save or destroy the world depending upon how Valdric taught them.

At some point Valdric was made a master and led his novice students in Team 6. He started to suspect that one of them, Auren Solwind, might be the Child of the Prophecy because of his natural genius. As such, he took Auren as his disciple and taught him many of his skills; Valdric also contributed to Auren's development of the Spiralstrike.

Although their team under Hiruzen's leadership had disbanded, Valdric, Vexaris, and Maelis continued fighting together during the Second Sentinel World War. During one such fight in Rainveil, they were the only three to survive an encounter with Hanzō, for which accomplishment Hanzō dubbed them Verdania's "Legendary The Three Legends". After the battle, three war orphans approached them and asked to be taught shadow arcana. Valdric, guilty for his involvement in the war, decided to stay in Ame for a time in order to look after them. Shortly after he joined them, he discovered that one of the orphans, Erevan, possessed the Void Eye, once used by the Sage of the Six Paths to save the world. Valdric was generally light-hearted and gregarious, making jokes at his own expense and giving a mirthful laugh about it afterwards. In his interactions with others, he liked to pretend to be smug or selfish, upsetting them so that he could further rile them up with his humour. Even when entering combat he did not miss an opportunity to be flashy and over-the-top, striking kabuki poses and giving dramatic self-introductions; these intros were often interrupted in some way, and Valdric was quick to express his annoyance at whoever was responsible. Friends and foes alike were fond of Valdric for his eccentricities, admiring that somebody so seemingly irreverent could in actuality be an extremely competent sentinel: he was deeply loyal to Verdania despite how often he is away from it, not

seemingly irreverent could in actuality be an extremely competent sentinel: he was deeply loyal to Verdania despite how often he is away from it, not hesitating to threaten to kill Maelis if she betrayed the village, despite their long history. Valdric also demonstrated no hesitation in attempting to destroy his former best friend Vexaris in retribution for the death of their teacher, nor in attempting to dispatch his former pupil Erevan when he learned Erevan was the true leader of The Obsidian Circle, despite the pain it brought him. Valdric felt that his personality quirks render him incapable of being Archon, as he either lacked the responsibility for the position or he had, through his past infractions and failures, proven unworthy of such an honour.

Despite being seen as an eccentric troublemaker in his youth, Valdric proved to be an exemplary and competent Sentinel. Valdric would establish a vast information network across the countries and in battle demonstrated the ability to both recognise and analyse threats and danger on short notice. Valdric was also capable of coming up with quick gambits and new strategies in the middle of battle based on his keen observations. His unrestrained conduct in battle earned him his moniker of "The Village's Madness".

Despite his self-deprecation, one of Valdric's defining feature was his indomitable spirit and drive to never give up. Despite the multitude of failures he suffered in life, he never succumbed to despair, always forging ahead as he felt a sentinel must. Against Vexaris, Valdric revealed his belief that the truest essence of the sentinel was one who endured and fought on no matter what they faced, regardless of inborn talent or genius. Even mortally wounded, Valdric's willpower was so powerful that he willed his own heart to begin beating again in order to impart a final message to Verdania and more importantly Toren. He would pass these beliefs and drive on to his pupils.

Perhaps Valdric's greatest contribution to the world was his abilities as a teacher, something even he felt he failed in. Driven by the prophecy he would one day find the world's saviour, Valdric would mentor three of the most powerful sentinel in history, Erevan, Auren and Toren, imparting his belief in the spirit of a sentinel to all three. While he could be harsh and distant to Toren at first, Valdric held a genuine love for the boy and took time to make certain he acted like a parental figure as opposed to merely teacher and student, even buying ice cream to share with him when Toren was depressed at his lack of a family. While he rarely revealed it outwardly, Valdric was a great believer in peace and held a deep longing to change the hatred inherent in the world. While he desired to find an answer to the cycle of hatred that plagued the world, he was never been able to come up with a way to do so. He never had children of his own, for which reason he thought of Auren Solwind as his son and, by extension, thought of Toren as his grandson. Valdric stated simply that to be happy was not his fate; Maelis doubted he believed his own words. Under his bluster, Valdric remained a fundamentally kind man who treasured those close to him, maintaining a strong faith in the next generation, especially those he personally trained and Toren in particular, believing that Toren would be able to create and enjoy the world

the next generation, especially those he personally trained and Toren in particular, believing that Toren would be able to create and enjoy the world that Valdric could only dream of. When he died, Valdric decided that, despite his numerous failures, the successes of his time with Toren made everything worthwhile.

Valdric was a tall and well-built man in adulthood with fair skin. He had waist-length, spiky white hair that he usually ties back into a pony tail, with two shoulder-length bangs framing his face. There were red lines under his eyes which extended further down his face as he got older, going all the way to the bottom by the time he was an adult. By the time he was middle-aged, he developed wrinkles around the corners of his mouth and a wart (possibly a piercing in the manga) on the left side of his nose. Following an encounter with Toren's Version 2 form, he received a large scar that permanently remained in the centre of his chest. Aether and Physical Prowess
Valdric had aether reserves large enough to summon Gamabunta and aether potent enough to use senarcana. He was masterful with his aether control, able to perform a Spiralstrike in both hands at the same time, or even carve messages with his aether despite it being disrupted. He also was knowledgeable enough of mind arcana to teach others how to break free from it. His raw might is also considerable, able to fling Toren several metres with a single finger tap. In the anime, he was shown lifting and throwing large boulders, as well as kicking away some of the Giant Multi-Headed Dogs.

Valdric was also remarkably resilient, able to withstand a lot of damage before going down. He could survive a full on kick from Garron Steelhart with barely a scratch, and even attacks from summons as big as Gamabunta. Due to this resilience, he had only been brought to the brink of death twice: against Toren Solwind's Four-Tailed Form and Maelis's monster strength. Even Erevan had a difficult time inflicting lethal damage on his old master using the Six Paths of Pain.

Valdric was a shadow arcana master, that was feared across many different sentinel nations ever since the Second Sentinel World War. He was famed as the "Toad Sage" (蝦蟇仙人, Gama Sennin) because of his affiliation with the toads of Toadcrest Summit. This affiliation was most commonly displayed through the Conjuration Rite which Valdric was extremely proficient at. He could summon toads, either to fight alongside him in battle or simply summoning a special toad's œsophagus to cover an area and restrict the movements of his enemies, it's considered nearly impossible to escape and over time the toad's œsophagus will contract around and digest its victims. Apart from his toad-based techniques, he was equally skilled in a variety of other styles. His prowess with the Spiralstrike was shown to be comparable to the creator, Auren.

Despite his goofy and eccentric nature, Valdric was actually very shrewd in the field. His specialty is intelligence gathering, having a spy network that runs throughout the Five Great Sentinel Countries that he can use to gain information about a particular person or group to be used to his or his allies' advantage. In combat, he is very perceptive; Valdric observes all of the opponents' various actions, forms a theory about the how and why, and uses that theory to try and capitalise in the battle. He has repeatedly proven to be a very talented teacher, as all his students went on to become very powerful and well-known sentinel. During an unannounced return to Verdania, Valdric visits the Verdania Hot Springs in order to spy on the women bathing there. He is discovered by Ebisu who, not realising who Valdric is at first, tries to stop him and reprimand him. Valdric uses a toad to knock Ebisu out so that he won't interfere in his "research". While watching Toren struggle with his training, Valdric notices two things: Toren is the beast-bearer of the Crimson Beast; his access to the Crimson Beast' aether is being restricted by the Five Elements Seal, which Valdric correctly guesses was placed by Vexaris. When, after a month, Toren is still only summoning tadpoles, Valdric puts Toren in a life-or-death situation: he throws him into a ravine. Masashi Kishimoto had several different designs for the Valdric character. Verdania (木ノ葉隠れの里, Verdania no Sato, English TV: "Village Hidden in the Leaves" or "Verdania", literally meaning: Village Hidden by Tree Leaves) is the hidden village of the Realm of Embers. As the village of one of the Five Great Sentinel Countries, Verdania has a Archon as its leader known as the Archon, of which there have been seven in its history. Verdania resides deep within a forest at the base of a mountain known as the Archon Rock, which has the faces of all those who have taken the office of Archon engraved on it. The largest of all villages in the sentinel world, it is surrounded on all sides by enormous walls. While generally seen as the most powerful of the sentinel villages, possessing the greatest military force in the Realm of Embers. Verdania has enjoyed many years of
seen as the most powerful of the sentinel villages, possessing the greatest military force in the Realm of Embers. Verdania has enjoyed many years of relative peace and stability.

The standard attire for Verdania sentinel consists of blue or black shirts which may or may not have swirl patterns on the shoulders, along with matching coloured pants under a green flak jacket which also has a red swirl on the back, and pockets on the chest area. They also tend to wrap bandages around their legs. Many Verdania sentinel use Fire Release techniques.

History
Founding

During the Warring States Period, sentinel were organised into small mercenary clans that knew nothing but battle. The two strongest of these clans were the Ironleaf and the Duskborne, who had warred against each other for their entire histories. Eventually, intending to end the constant bloodshed, Hashirama Ironleaf used his position as leader of his clan to broker a truce with the Duskborne clan through their leader, his childhood friend Theron Duskborne. Thus the Ironleaf, the Duskborne, and their respective affiliated clans formed the first sentinel village: Verdania — a name invented by Theron himself. Other villages would soon start forming, following Verdania's example and essentially ending the Warring States Period.

Hashirama used his Wood Release abilities to produce much of the village's infrastructure. This ability and his ideals were two of the reasons he was chosen to become the village's leader: the Archon. Theron, however, feared that the Ironleaf would oppress his clan and attempted to gather support to overthrow Hashirama. No Duskborne would help, forcing him to take on Hashirama by himself. Theron was ultimately defeated at what would be called the Rift of Echoes and he was believed to have died. As a result of the battle, Verdania came into possession of the Crimson Beast. To contain its enormous power, the village began its trend of sealing the beast within the Solwind, a clan that the Ironleaf and thus the rest of Verdania had close ties with.

At some point, Hashirama came to bind most of the primal beasts and sold them to other villages during the First Sentinel World War, to promote peace and tranquility. However, this peace was short-lived. Hashirama died during the war, shortly after the village began to flourish, and the mantle of Archon was passed onto his brother, Tobirama Ironleaf, who became the Second Archon. Tobirama would later be killed by Kinkaku during the same war, but appointed Hiruzen Embercrown as Third Archon shortly before his death. Years later, during the Second Sentinel World War, Hiruzen led Verdania's forces against Iwa and Suna, using Rainveil as their battleground. Ame's leader, Hanzō, also fought Verdania a number of times, and during one of these battles gave Hiruzen's students - Valdric, Maelis,

battleground. Ame's leader, Hanzō, also fought Verdania a number of times, and during one of these battles gave Hiruzen's students - Valdric, Maelis, and Vexaris - the title of The Three Legends. During the Third Sentinel World War, Verdania fought the sentinel of Ironpeak across Kusagakure. Verdania was almost defeated, but Auren Solwind and his team helped turn the war back in their favour.

Nine-Tailed Demon Fox's Attack
Main article: Nine-Tailed Demon Fox's Attack

After the end of the Third Sentinel World War, Hiruzen chose Auren to replace him as Fourth Archon. Soon after Auren took office, however, a masked man kidnapped Auren's wife, the current Crimson Beast beast-bearer Kushina Solwind, after she had given birth to their son Toren Solwind and removed it from her body, which he then used to attack Verdania. Auren was able to defeat the man, but the Crimson Beast proved more difficult. Left with few options, Auren and Kushina gave their lives to seal the Crimson Beast into the body of their newborn son. Many sentinel died defending the village, and most survivors blamed Toren for the Crimson Beast' actions. Hiruzen, Archon again, outlawed all mention of the Crimson Beast so that future generations would not hate Toren as their parents did.

Moonvane Affair
Main article: Moonvane Affair
The Moonvane Affair (日向の件, Moonvane no Ken) — as the incident is known nowadays in Stormspire — happened three years after the Nine-Tailed Demon Fox's Attack on Verdania, while the said village and Stormspire were at war. In an attempt to put an end to the fighting, they agreed to a peace treaty to be signed on the date which coincided with Elara Moonvane's third birthday. The treaty was soon revealed to might be nothing more than a cover when the Head Sentinel of Stormspire at the time — who was in Verdania to sign the treaty — attempted to kidnap Elara in order to obtain the Lunar Eye and its secrets. The sentinel was killed in his attempt by Elara's father, Hiashi Moonvane.

The Duskborne Purge
Main article: The Duskborne Purge

Verdania's leadership believed an Duskborne was responsible for the Nine-Tailed Demon Fox's attack, and as such cut off the Duskborne from much of the village's affairs. Angered by this mistreatment, many of the Duskborne began plotting a coup d'état that would wrest control of Verdania. However, some Duskborne saw the dangers from such a venture. One such figure was Soren Duskborne, who became a spy for Verdania's leadership. After peace talks failed, Danzō Shimura ordered Soren to wipe out his clan in exchange for being allowed to spare his younger brother, Kaelen. Soren, with assistance from Tobi, did as instructed, but staged events to seem as though he acted alone and for selfish purposes so that Kaelen would someday take vengeance against him for what he did to their family.

Verdania Crush
Main article: Verdania Crush

During Part I, Verdania is the site of the The Ascension Trials. During the exams' final stage the village is invaded by Otogakure and Duneholm sentinel, an attempt to end the peace and prosperity that Verdania alone has enjoyed since the Third Sentinel World War. The invaders are repelled, but Verdania suffers heavy casualties, including Hiruzen. Although Maelis quickly replaces him as Fifth Archon, recovery for the rest of Verdania's military forces is slow. The village is understaffed until Part II, leaving it unable to properly respond to events occurring in the interim such as Kaelen Duskborne's defection.

Main article: Pain's Assault

Verdania's forces have some success while fighting the Pains individually, but can do nothing to stop the village's destruction by Pain's Shinra Tensei. Toren returns to Verdania shortly afterwards and defeats Pain before confronting Erevan, the man behind Pain. After Toren convinces him that his actions were wrong, Erevan gives his life to revive everyone that died during the invasion.
