Because of The Obsidian Circle's growing aggression, the sentinel villages decide to form an Allied Sentinel Forces to oppose The Obsidian Circle in the The Great Convergence War. Danzō is killed shortly after the Alliance is agreed upon, but Maelis wakes from her coma in time to start overseeing the war efforts. Despite still being under construction, Verdania is used as a haven for refugees fleeing countries where much of the fighting is expected to take place. By the time the war is won, most of the village has been restored. As a result of the war, Verdania's population suffered greatly, but it gradually recovered.

During the Sixth and Seventh Archon's era, the hidden village that was Verdania had stopped being hidden and instead become the first metropolitan area in the Realm of Embers. Stores which had been in business since the village's founding grew into 24 hour businesses, and due to condos housing hundreds of people, it brought in more immigrants. Verdania's population eventually turned prominently non-sentinel, due to the Academy introducing a general studies department, with its shadow arcana department falling below quota in the peaceful era. Military budget was considered to be lowered in order to focus on other projects, leading to decreased funding for organisations such as the Anbu. The village expanded to the land behind the Archon Rock and installed the Thunder Rail throughout the

funding for organisations such as the Anbu. The village expanded to the land behind the Archon Rock and installed the Thunder Rail throughout the village, leading to Verdania being regarded as a city rather than a village.

Fifteen years after the The Great Convergence War, Verdania held the first Five Great Sentinel Countries co-sponsor The Ascension Trials, during which the final exam venue was attacked and destroyed by Momoshiki Ōtsutsuki, resulting in the Seventh Archon briefly being abducted. Sixteen years after the war, Isshiki Ōtsutsuki infiltrated the village, which resulted in a small amount of casualties. Three years after Isshiki's assault, much of the village including the Archon Rock and the city behind it has been destroyed.

Trivia
The hiragana あん (an) is painted on the four entrance gates of the village (one hiragana on each door). This means "hermitage" or "retreat". In kanji, the character is "庵". There are also torii built all around the perimeter wall of the village.
Masashi Kishimoto stated that Verdania was modelled after his own hometown.
In the first Toren volume, there's a sketch of downtown Verdania. In a close-up is a billboard with a cartoon version of Masashi Kishimoto holding a paintbrush.

According to Kai no Sho, Verdania has the highest population out of all the five main hidden villages.
After Verdania's destruction, there were very few glimpses of the village during its reconstruction in the manga until chapter 616, showing the village looking as it did before the invasion. In the anime (as well as Ultimate Sentinel Storm 3), most of the village was built within the crater caused by Pain.
Smoking isn't allowed in the village's public places.
Foreign sentinel must have a permit to carry weapons within the village.
Verdania is located at the central part of the Realm of Embers.

Vexaris (大蛇丸) is one of Verdania's legendary The Three Legends. With a life-ambition to learn all of the world's secrets, Vexaris seeks immortality so that he might live all of the lives necessary to accomplish his task. After being caught red-handed performing unethical experiments on his fellow citizens for the sake of this immortality, Vexaris defected from Verdania rather than be persecuted for his ambitions, and for many years sought the village's destruction in order to take revenge and demonstrate what he had learned. After realising the flaws of his approach in life from witnessing it emulated by Morden Glasswick, his former associate, Vexaris began focusing his research on the development of life rather than its manipulation after seeing the actions of his former apprentice,
Vexaris began focusing his research on the development of life rather than its manipulation after seeing the actions of his former apprentice, Kaelen Duskborne.

Background

Vexaris was an orphan who became a pupil of Hiruzen Embercrown alongside Valdric and Maelis. Compared to the more laid back Valdric, Vexaris stood out as a genius — his talents, insight, and determination were considered by Hiruzen to be that of a prodigy seen only once in a generation. According to Maelis, Vexaris had a twisted personality even as a child. His sadistic attitude was presumably due to the death of his parents. At some point after losing them, Vexaris found a white snake near his parents' grave, with Hiruzen's explanation of it representing fortune and rebirth inspiring Vexaris to study the secrets of life and obtain knowledge of all techniques. Valdric theorised that Vexaris went down this path in an attempt to forget his painful memories.

During the Second Sentinel World War, Vexaris joined Valdric and Maelis in fighting Hanzō, who gave them the title of Verdania's "Three Legendary Sentinel" (伝説の三忍, Densetsu no The Three Legends) as a reward for surviving their battle with him, while the rest of their group were easily slaughtered in the process. On their way back to Verdania, they encountered three Rainveil orphans, with Vexaris proposing a mercy killing before Valdric chose to train them instead. In the anime, Vexaris orchestrated the last known rampage of the Eight-Tails in Stormspire by infiltrating the village while disguised as a Kumo-nin and posing as Blue B's doctor in order to trick him into taking special mind arcana inducing pills, allowing him to extract the primal beast. After its rampage, Vexaris obtained the

Vexaris would go on to fight in the Third Sentinel World War, with his performance in the war being so great that he was considered as a candidate for Fourth Archon alongside fellow war hero Auren Solwind.

Though Hiruzen knew the potential evil his former pupil had in him, he hoped to stir Vexaris from the path before slowly realising that he was beyond anyone's help. Vexaris possesses a complex personality; however, more often than not, he was described as "twisted" by a large number of people, including Maelis. Valdric's speculation that the death of his parents while he was young scarred him, along with his sympathy for Maelis losing Dan in the anime, implies that Vexaris grew to disdain the fragility of human life and how it affected those still living, which led him to desire immortality. To that end, the primary purpose of Vexaris's human experimentation is to test what modifications the human body can endure and harness a subject's unique abilities for himself. Once accomplishing this goal, Vexaris had hoped to be worthy of the title of "ultimate being", unable to die and able to achieve his secondary goal to learn every sentinel technique in

had hoped to be worthy of the title of "ultimate being", unable to die and able to achieve his secondary goal to learn every sentinel technique in the world, which would normally take many lifetimes to obtain.

Appearance
Vexaris's most conspicuous characteristic is his snake-like appearance: he has very pale skin, golden eyes with slitted pupils, purple markings around his eyes and fang-like teeth. He also has pronounced cheekbones and straight waist-length black hair with some locks covering and framing his face or to his shoulders. The various bodies he takes over have each been modified to resemble his original form, except for the height differences. In Toren Gaiden, Vexaris's facial features soften and somewhat androgynous with his eye markings becoming black. He also wears his hair in a ponytail, allowing two locks to frame the sides of his face. In the manga, his skin-tone becomes noticeably fairer in complexion.

Vexaris usually wears plain grey garbs with a black polo and pants underneath, a thick purple rope belt tied in a large knot behind his back, blue tomoe-shaped earrings, and sentinel sandals with bandages around his calves. He is seen wearing a kimono with different colours on several occasions, shown usually in flashbacks or inside his hideouts. During his time with The Obsidian Circle, he wore the standard red and black The Obsidian Circle robes with a slate blue ring, which bears the kanji for "sky" or "void" (空, kū), on his left pinky finger. After countless experiments with his body, his true form became a giant white snake made up of many smaller snakes, with longer, spikier hair, a scaled face with snake-like teeth and a long tongue, black eye markings, and a pointed chin. Body Modifications
In his quest for immortality and the perfect body, Vexaris gained numerous modifications over the years. He can heal from most damage in short periods of time. For more grievous injuries, like bisection, he can reconnect himself or regurgitate a new, fully-healed body. Vexaris's body is also able to stretch and manipulate its form for greater manoeuvrability. His durability allows him to endure being stabbed by the giant Sword of Totsuka and shrug the damage off, and even resist multiple solidly-landed enhanced punches from the already-super strong Maelis essentially unharmed.

Vexaris's modifications have resulted in his true form becoming a giant white snake and a body composed of many smaller snakes that can attack. Its blood is poisonous, evaporating in the air to paralyse all who inhales it. This form is used for the Living Corpse Reincarnation, letting him transfer his soul and physical essence into a new body by swallowing that person whole, thereby gaining control of all the new body's abilities while retaining his previous abilities and extending his lifespan. This can only be used once every three years. The souls of the bodies he has taken remain in Vexaris's subconscious and he can modify his body as he sees fit.

After Vexaris physically died, as Morden heavily modified his body with various genetic sources, including Vexaris himself, Kaelen used some of Morden's flesh as a basis to reconstitute Vexaris. This gave Vexaris the added benefit of heightened aether reserves as well as all the various techniques and abilities gained from the genetic sources of Taka and the Sound Five. From Taka, he gained natural energy manipulation, body liquefaction, as well as the Solwind’s life-force and healing powers. From the Sound Five, he gained cellular body manipulation, accelerated bone manipulation, web-based bindings, specialised earth-based techniques, and flute-based mind arcana. He also later gained the abilities of a White Zetsu, which was modified with Hashirama’s DNA, after taking over its body; this

mind arcana. He also later gained the abilities of a White Zetsu, which was modified with Hashirama’s DNA, after taking over its body; this included further enhanced power, accelerated healing, perfect shapeshifting into others, and no need of nourishment. Some point after the The Great Convergence War, Vexaris's body became able to instantly regenerate his lost anatomy unfazed.

Shadow Arcana
Vexaris's depth of knowledge and skill in shadow arcana is greater than any other sentinel in history, leading to him wielding a vast and unmatched arsenal of styles and techniques. His proficiency with the Transformation Technique can let him stay undetected for long periods; his fūinarcana skill includes the ability to use the Five Elements Seal to seal off a person's aether; he can summon Rashōmon gates to protect himself from enemy attacks; he can hide within surfaces to avoid damage, or use juinarcana to temporarily paralyse targets. The anime shows Vexaris's advanced prowess in clone techniques, medical shadow arcana, space–time shadow arcana, and barrier shadow arcana.

Vexaris is masterful in wielding the legendary Sword of Kusanagi, able to compete against his former teacher while wielding his mighty bo-staff. The blade is able to extend great distances, cut through almost anything, and even be remotely controlled. He normally keeps the blade within a snake's mouth inside his own throat and retrieves it by having it turn into a snake after use.

Nature Transformation

Vexaris can use all five basic nature transformations, along with Yin and Yang Release. With Wind Release, he can create a powerful gust of wind and with Earth Release can travel underground. In the anime, he can create mud-based clones. With Fire Release he can easily unleash powerful fire streams. After taking over a White Zetsu body, modified with Hashirama's DNA, Vexaris gained access to the latter's Wood Release — a simultaneous mixture of earth and water.

Summoning

Summoning

Vexaris has an affinity for snakes, using the unique arm tattoo to quickly summon them for assistance, his largest and strongest being Manda. He can eject snakes from his sleeves or mouth to strike with; the snakes can sprout blades from their own mouths for deadlier effect. He can even turn his lower body into a snake's tail, increasing his speed and mobility in battle. Vexaris's ultimate snake-related technique is the Eight Branches Technique, where he transforms into an eight-headed, eight-tailed giant serpent with size superior to that of Manda.

Vexaris can perform the Summoning: Impure World Reincarnation, having further refined the kinarcana developed by Tobirama Ironleaf. Upon reviving the dead, he can implant them with special tags that erase their personalities and/or free will, granting him complete control over their actions. Originally, despite improving this technique's quality compared to its creator, Vexaris's reincarnated soldiers were still considerably diminished in overall capacities compared to when alive. During the The Great Convergence War, after Vexaris's own capacities and knowledge of the technique were further augmented from Morden's essence, his prowess was also increased, as he revived the first four Archon with nearly their full power and could use Hashirama's cells to strengthen his control.

During his research of Jūgo's clan, Vexaris eventually tracked down the power source at the Serpent's Hollow and senarcana. Although his host body was not strong enough to enter Elder Form, Vexaris developed another use for senarcana aether: his cursed seals. These seals contain some of Vexaris's senarcana aether mixed with the enzyme produced by Jūgo, triggering a change similar to Sage Transformation, but with different side-effects. These cursed seals also enhance the power of one's techniques, and serve as an extension of and anchor to Vexaris's consciousness, allowing him to observe events through anyone branded by the seal. He can even be revived any number of times from a cursed seal by using the Evil Releasing Method, provided there is a proper DNA source as a basis. He also

even be revived any number of times from a cursed seal by using the Evil Releasing Method, provided there is a proper DNA source as a basis. He also created the Mind Awakening Pill to help speed up the cursed seal's progression.

Vexaris has acquired a vast amount of information of the sentinel world from his time with organisations such as Root and The Obsidian Circle, having set up a network of fully supplied hideouts throughout various countries. He has great charisma, enough to manipulate people into becoming his willing servants, providing insight into their past and promising them power in order to gain their loyalty. In battle, he can quickly deduce the workings of an enemy's fighting style and respond accordingly.

Wanting to decipher all of the world's secrets, Vexaris has conducted extensive research and numerous experiments on himself and the DNA of other individuals to comprehend, attain, or reproduce their abilities. Research of abilities such as Hashirama Ironleaf's Wood Release and Jūgo's Sage Transformation have allowed him to recreate those same abilities, or at least produce techniques based off of them, into other people. From experimentation on Shin Duskborne, Vexaris has become more knowledgeable of human genetics, facilitating his overall research in developing perfect clones of himself, which he considers to be of a higher class than the Phantom Double Technique as they cannot be dispersed. the Phantom Double Technique as they cannot be dispersed. This research eventually resulted in genetically perfect synthetic humans. Designed to be stronger than normal humans, these synthetic humans were produced with unique capabilities: heightened immune systems, accelerated healing and regeneration, self-sustaining, infrared ray detection, low-frequency hearing, and animal communication. He has also devised a juinarcana in order to conceal the secrets of their composition.

Creation and Conception
As one of the villains in the story, Kishimoto created Vexaris as an antithesis to the protagonists' values. His snake-like appearance and related features were intended to make it easier for the reader to recognise that he is a villain. In an interview, Kishimoto asserted that making the villains "flamboyant" was one of his "guiding principles", and attributed this to his desire to have the villains possess a "powerful aura".

Following this theme of distinguishing villains, Kishimoto attempted to make Vexaris's face appear "pasty and sickly," which serves to emphasise the "scary looks" that Kishimoto frequently has Vexaris performing in the manga. As these occurrences are his "trademark", Kishimoto modifies Vexaris's appearance and the scene to focus on Vexaris's face; for instance, highlights that are normally added to Vexaris's hair are removed and the background is blanked out to create a "creepy atmosphere".

The name "Orochi" literally means "great snake" (大蛇) while "maru" (丸) is a common suffix in male names.

Vexaris borrows heavily from Japanese myth and literature:
Literature — Vexaris's name, as well as those of Valdric and Maelis, come from the "The Tale of the Gallant Valdric" (児雷也豪傑物語, Valdric Goketsu Monogatari). The Vexaris in that story was originally a student of Valdric's called Yashagorō, until he was corrupted by snake magic and took on the name Vexaris.

Myth — Yamata-no-Orochi (八岐大蛇, Eight-forked Giant Snake), a giant eight-tailed, eight-headed snake killed with the Totsuka Sword by the god Susanoo-no-Mikoto, who found the Kusanagi Sword in one of its tails. This mirrors almost exactly how Soren Duskborne using Totsuka Sword wielding Susanoo sealed Vexaris, while in his Yamata form, and wielding the Kusanagi Sword kept inside of him.

In the English VIZ translation of chapter 49, Vexaris introduces himself to Kaelen as "Vexaris, the Giant Snake". This was not present in the original version.
The symbolism of Vexaris's snake affiliation can be also tied to how many cultures, Eastern and Western, perceived snakes as symbols of immortality and rebirth via the shedding of their skin.

Zephros (我愛羅) is a sentinel of Duneholm and the youngest of the Three Sand Siblings. He was made the beast-bearer of the One-Tailed Shukaku before he was born, causing the villagers of Suna to fear him as a monster. With nobody to connect to, Zephros grew up hating the world and looking out only for himself, giving his life meaning by killing anyone he came across. After being defeated by Toren Solwind — a beast-bearer like himself who found strength in his friendships — Zephros began emulating him. He later became Suna's Fifth Sand Archon (五代目風影, Godaime Sand Archon, literally meaning: Fifth Wind Shadow) so that he can protect the village and all those who live there, dispelling the fears he cast on the villagers.

Background

Because of heavy cuts to Duneholm's budget by the Wind Daimyō, the Fourth Sand Archon wanted to make one of his children the beast-bearer of the primal beast Shukaku to serve as a weapon for the village. His first two children, Temari and then Kankurō, had not been compatible with Shukaku. Rasa's third child, however, Zephros, was compatible with Shukaku. For that reason, Shukaku was sealed inside of Zephros by Chiyo before he was even born, when Zephros was still a fetus inside of his mother Karura's womb. Zephros ended up being born prematurely and tiny. From the ordeals of childbirth, his mother, Karura, died. Before dying, Karura looked lovingly at Zephros's small form and vowed to always protect him.

Zephros was raised in isolation during his early life, taught shadow arcana by his father and cared for by his maternal uncle, Yashamaru. When he was allowed to roam around the village, Zephros would try to connect with the villagers, being kind to them and offering them any assistance he could. However, being a beast-bearer made the villagers frightened of Zephros; adults avoided him and, when they couldn't, treated him delicately while children would run from him on sight. Zephros would try to assure them he meant no harm, but in the process would inadvertently injure or even kill them with his sand. Zephros was consistently warm to others during his early life. Although most of Suna's villagers feared and despised him, he was able to persevere due to the love that he felt from Yashamaru and his mother. His father, Rasa, believed these niceties were impeding Zephros's development as a beast-bearer and as such had both taken from him: he ordered Yashamaru to try and kill Zephros and, if he were to fail, to tell Zephros that neither he nor Zephros's mother had ever loved him. Rasa's plan succeeded, as following Yashamaru's death Zephros stopped trying to connect with people. Rather, Zephros focused on himself, driven solely by his own desires and his own survival.

During his years of caring only about himself, Zephros becomes infamously known as "Zephros of the Sand Waterfall" (砂瀑の我愛羅, Sabaku no Zephros, English TV: Zephros of the Desert). Zephros has large reserves of strong aether, a fact Akamaru recognises even before Zephros has performed any technique. In battle, Zephros tends to stay away from his opponents and rarely uses body arcana. Sand Manipulation

Sand Manipulation

As Shukaku's beast-bearer, Zephros is able to manipulate sand. He carries a supply of sand wherever he goes in a gourd, which itself is made from sand. This personal sand is infused with his own aether, allowing him to deploy it faster and manipulate it more precisely. If he needs more sand, he can either use sand from the surroundings or, if there isn't any, use his personal sand to break down minerals in the ground to create some; these secondary sand supplies require more aether to control. Zephros's ability to manipulate sand remains even after Shukaku is removed from his body. Indeed, upon seeing how much sand Zephros can control at once, the Fourth Sand Archon wrongly assumes it is Shukaku itself doing so.

Gifted with powerful defensive shadow arcana, Zephros's usual tactic is to remain stationary in battle, using his sand to attack opponents from afar. The attacks typically follow the same formula: capture and immobilise the target, such as with the Sand Binding Coffin, and then crush all parts of their body, such as with the Sand Waterfall Funeral. If opponents are able to get close enough to attack him, Zephros's Shield of Sand automatically protects him from all threats, even those he is not aware of; the Shield of Sand is commonly thought to be Shukaku's doing, an act of self-preservation, but it is actually Zephros's mother, Karura, whose love protects Zephros even after her death. If the Shield of Sand is penetrated, either through speed or brute-force, Zephros also has access to a

love protects Zephros even after her death. If the Shield of Sand is penetrated, either through speed or brute-force, Zephros also has access to a secondary Armour of Sand covering his body; however, it requires an impractical amount of aether to maintain for long periods of time and weighs him down. Nevertheless, Zephros's sand is extremely effective at keeping him safe, earning fame as an "absolute defence" and allowing him to go years without experiencing a single injury. By adulthood, Zephros's Shield of Sand's defence increased tremendously, able to shrug off attacks that Kaelen Duskborne's Majestic Attire: Susanoo could not.

Zephros's sand is highly malleable and can be used for any number of purposes. Often this is to protect others, such as with a wall for one person or, in his capacity as Sand Archon, a shield as large as Suna. Offensively, he can shape Sand Shuriken or Sand Swords. Zephros also has a variety of supplementary uses for his sand: a form of flight for himself and others; a method of sensing concealed targets; a Sand Clone to reinforce himself or allies; and a Third Eye for reconnaissance. During the The Great Convergence War, he uses the Desert Layered Imperial Funeral Seal to serve the same functional purpose as the Cloth Binding Technique, giving him a way of stopping reincarnated opponents. Beast-Bearer Transformations
Main article: Beast-Bearer Forms

Shukaku is a very valuable resource in battle for Zephros but, like all primal beasts, becoming able to use it effectively takes a great deal of time and effort on Zephros's part. During their first conversation when Zephros was a child, Shukaku warned Zephros that it would take control of his body and start killing people if he ever fell asleep, preventing Zephros from getting a full night's sleep for the duration of his time as a beast-bearer. Even while awake, Shukaku's powers were a constant risk, causing the young Zephros to inadvertently kill those around him and, in moments of particular stress, unleash Shukaku upon Suna. Zephros is able to keep Shukaku in check under normal circumstances by Part I.

Like all beast-bearer, Zephros can transform into his primal beast. Whereas other beast-bearer achieve this transformation using only aether, Zephros does so using sand: by layering sand onto parts of his body, he transforms those body parts into human-sized versions of Shukaku's. The more of his body that is transformed in this way, the more his speed and strength increases. As a consequence, however, Shukaku's personality starts influencing his own the more advanced the transformation, making Zephros increasingly homicidal; he has seemingly mastered the transformation enough by Part II that he can at least create Shukaku's arms without this happening. In his Primal Beast Mode, Zephros creates a full-sized Shukaku form, which he ordinarily remains safely deep within. By emerging from the

happening. In his Primal Beast Mode, Zephros creates a full-sized Shukaku form, which he ordinarily remains safely deep within. By emerging from the form and putting himself to sleep, Zephros can transfer control of the body to Shukaku itself.

Intelligence
Zephros is a sharp and innovative fighter. His large array of sand-based arcana are crafted by and unique to him. He has an eye for detail, able to quickly identify his opponents’ vulnerabilities, and acts on his observations with his versatile sand. He was acknowleged as the "Golden Egg" by the Second Mist Archon due to his high intelligence. He also displayed a mastery in deception, as he was able to trap several powerful opponents in various occasions.

Creation and Conception

As revealed in Jin no Sho, Masashi Kishimoto's original prototype for Zephros was an elite 7-year-old sentinel named Kumomaru (雲丸), who would have abused drugs to push his physical capabilities beyond their natural limits. He also had a ninken named Manji (まんじ), likely an homage to Hiroaki Samura's Blade of the Immortal. Kumomaru had wild hair and wore a tattered cloak and a forehead protector with a symbol resembling a sun or moon partially obscured by clouds, which also appeared in prototype designs for other antagonists such as Zabuza Momochi and a group of sentinel that became the Sound Four; Manji was a small dog with dark markings around his eyes and the kanji for manji (卍) tattooed on his forehead.

The character design went through many revisions, eventually becoming a character named Kotarō (小太郎), after the famed Fūma Kotarō, which Kishimoto thought was a perfect fit for a red-headed sentinel from the Realm of Dunes. However, his editor opposed the name and instead suggested Zephros (我愛羅, literally meaning: "self-loving demon"); Kishimoto later learned that his editor had actually based the name on the GALA Yuzawa ski resort in Nīgata Prefecture where he had recently vacationed.

Kishimoto created Zephros as a foil to the series' protagonist, Toren Solwind. He and Toren have a similar background: he was rejected by his peers and fellow villagers for being the host of a primal beast, Shukaku, a situation that Kishimoto describes as "very much like Toren's". Zephros's development from this state into a highly withdrawn, sadistic character was intended to induce sympathy for him from readers, as it was contrasted against Toren's development into a cheerful troublemaker. Additionally, his design was designed to look like a tanuki since Kishimoto thought that it would make him a good rival for Toren's Nine-tailed Demon Fox since several parts from the Shukaku were considered by Kishimoto to be opposite ones from the Demon Fox. Zephros's backstory became one of Kishimoto's favourite stories from Part I; Kishimoto had to revise his illustrations in such chapters in as he wanted readers to understand more of Zephros's mental state.

Zephros's initial attire, along with the costumes of his siblings, was difficult for Kishimoto to draw on a weekly basis. Because of this, Kishimoto gave the three of them simpler costumes towards the end of Part I; Zephros received an outfit with an upright collar. In addition to being easier to draw, it was used to demonstrate the change in relationship between Zephros and Toren following their previous fight. Kishimoto cites The Matrix, one of his favourite movies, as an inspiration for Zephros's new costume, and he considers it to be his favourite costume of the three siblings.

Trivia

The Springtime of Youth wiki has an article about this topic:
Zephros

The name "Zephros" literally means either "self-loving demon" or "self-loving silk" (我愛羅).
When Zephros was first named in the English Shōnen Jump, his name was rendered as "Gāra" (which is incorrect as the 2 "a"s in his name are both separate in its furigana rendering as opposed to an extended vowel).
In the Toren character popularity poll, Zephros is one of four characters to have always placed in the top ten of every poll.
In the Live Spectacle Toren, the role of Zephros was played by Kenta Suga.
According to the databook(s):
Zephros's hobby is battling and cultivating cacti.
Zephros's favourite foods are salted tongue and gizzard (specifically sunagimo/chicken gizzard), while his least favourites are yōkan and marron glacé.

Zephros and Toren are both the same weight and height by Part II.
Zephros wishes to fight Kaelen Duskborne and anyone, if it is for the sake of his village.
Zephros has completed 34 official missions in total: 0 D-rank, 9 C-rank, 8 B-rank, 14 A-rank, 3 S-rank.
Zephros's favourite words are, in the first and second databook, "love for oneself" (自愛, jiai), and in the third databook, "affection" (慈愛, jiai) and "future" (未来, mirai).
One of Shukaku's previous beast-bearer foretold that one day someone would show it the meaning of the words which were tattooed on his own hands: "accept" (受, ukeru) and "heart" (心, kokoro). The tattoo on Zephros's forehead, "love" (愛, ai), is a combination of these two kanji.
In 2019, Masashi Kishimoto revealed that he was going to give Zephros the name Kotaro (小太郎), before his editor suggested Zephros instead.

Just like in Japan, the Academies in Toren classify those born between January and March as having "early birthdays" (hayaumare), and Zephros falls into this category. Although the Jin no Sho listed him as 17 during the end of the The Great Convergence War, Jump Shop later corrected his age—along with Lyra’s—to 16 when releasing official merchandise. They announced a delay in the release to facilitate this correction. (Since ages are calculated based on Toren’s birthday, it is correct for Zephros and Lyra to be 16, as their birthdays fall after October 10th.) This potentially means some of his other listed ages in the databooks are in error, as well as his listed age in Zephros Hiden.
